entries.title: Adbeel (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Third of Ishmael's twelve sons. Each of the twelve ended up heading an Arabian tribal confederation.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Adbeel was the third of Ishmael's twelve sons, each of whom became head of an Arabian tribal confederation (Genesis 25:13; 1 Chronicles 1:29). Some scholars connect his descendants with the “Idibi'ilu” named in the eighth-century BC annals of the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser III as a tribe controlling Egypt's desert border. Nothing further is recorded of Adbeel himself.

entries.title: Addan
entries.summary: A place rather than a person, one of the Babylonian localities exiles came back from, and the families from it could not prove their descent.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Not a person but a place name, one of several Babylonian localities named in Ezra 2:59 (called Addon in the parallel list of Nehemiah 7:61) from which a group of exiles returned to Judah after the exile but could not prove their genealogical descent from Israel. Its exact location is unknown.

entries.title: Addar
entries.summary: A son of Bela and grandson of Benjamin. Genesis and Numbers call him Ard.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: It is a duplicate record of that same individual rather than a separate location.

entries.title: Addi (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Luke's genealogy has him between Cosam and Melchi, and that is his only appearance.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Addi appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus as the son of Cosam and father of Melchi, one link in the ancestral chain traced through Joseph back to David (Luke 3:28).

entries.title: Addon
entries.summary: Named among the returning exiles who could not produce proof of Israelite descent when the family records were checked.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Addon is named among a group of returning exiles who could not produce genealogical proof of their Israelite descent when the community's family records were checked after the return from Babylon (Neh. 7:61; called Addan in the parallel list at Ezra 2:59). The episode reflects how carefully priestly and tribal lineage was guarded in the postexilic community.

entries.title: Ader (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: He is a Benjaminite leader, son of Beriah, among the family heads settled in Aijalon. Some manuscripts spell the name Eder.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Benjaminite leader, son of Beriah, listed among the family heads settled in Aijalon; some manuscripts give the name as Eder (1 Chronicles 8:15).

entries.title: Adiel (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Father of one of David's treasury officials, and that is his whole appearance in the record.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Adiel (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Simeonite clan leader carrying the same name. One verse in Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Adiel (Priest living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Third man of the name, a priest in the Chronicles genealogies.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Adiel was a common name, borne by a Simeonite clan leader, a priest in the genealogies of Chronicles, and the father of one of David's treasury officials.

entries.title: Adin (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Head of a family among the returning exiles, big enough that both Ezra and Nehemiah count the household.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Adin was the head of a family among the returning exiles, large enough to be listed by household count in both Ezra and Nehemiah.

entries.title: Adin (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: The same family name again. It gets one verse in Nehemiah.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Adina (Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He was a Reubenite who led thirty men, and he served among David's warriors.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Adina was a Reubenite who led thirty men and served among David's mighty warriors (1 Chronicles 11:42).

entries.title: Adithaim
entries.summary: A lowland town of Judah, named once between Sharaim and Gederah, and its site is still unidentified.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Adithaim, a lowland town of Judah named between Sharaim and Gederah in the Shephelah district list of Joshua 15:36. It occurs only here and its site remains unidentified.

entries.title: Adlai (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Father of Shaphat, the man who looked after David's cattle out in the valleys. That is his whole appearance.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Adlai was the father of Shaphat, who oversaw King David's cattle grazing in the valleys as one of the officials managing the royal estates (1 Chronicles 27:29). He is mentioned only to identify his son.

entries.title: Admah
entries.summary: One of the five cities of the plain, always paired with Zeboiim, and destroyed along with Sodom and Gomorrah.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Admah was one of the five "cities of the plain" in the Jordan Valley, paired throughout Scripture with its neighbor Zeboiim, destroyed along with Sodom and Gomorrah for their wickedness (Genesis 10:19; 19:24-25; Deuteronomy 29:23). Hosea later cites Admah and Zeboiim's total destruction as a measure of the mercy God chose instead to show Israel (Hosea 11:8).

entries.title: Admatha (Prince living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of seven princes of Persia and Media who sat first in the kingdom and had access to the king. Ahasuerus consulted them after Queen Vashti refused to appear before him, and that is the only time his name comes up.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Admatha was one of seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to the king and sat first in the kingdom, consulted by Ahasuerus after Queen Vashti's refusal to appear before him (Esther 1:14).

entries.title: Adna (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Among the Israelites Ezra listed who had married foreign wives during the exile and agreed to separate from them.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Adna (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of the priests in Nehemiah's register of the house of Harim.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Two men bear this name. One was among the Israelites listed by Ezra who had married foreign wives during the exile and agreed to separate from them (Ezra 10:30). The other was a priest, head of the family of Harim, in the generation after the return from exile (Nehemiah 12:15).

entries.title: Adnah
entries.summary: Jehoshaphat's senior commander, at the head of 300,000 men, the largest single division named when the king reorganised his army.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Adnah refers to two distinct men in Chronicles who share this name. The first was a chief of the tribe of Manasseh who defected to David's side just before the battle of Gilboa, one of several Manassite commanders who joined him at Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:20). The second, evidently unrelated, was the senior commander in King Jehoshaphat's army, leading a force of 300,000 men, the largest single division named in Jehoshaphat's military reorganization (2 Chronicles 17:14).

witness.excerpt: Now the army of men that wore their armor, was three hundred thousand of the tribe of Judah, of whom Adnah was the chief; but John was chief of two hundred thousand.

entries.title: Adonibezek (King living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: He ruled at Bezek, a Canaanite king who had beaten seventy rival chiefs, cut off their thumbs and big toes, and left them to scavenge scraps under his table. The tribes of Judah and Simeon defeated him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Adonibezek was a Canaanite king ruling at Bezek who had subdued seventy rival chiefs, mutilating each by cutting off his thumbs and big toes and forcing them to scavenge scraps under his table. The tribes of Judah and Simeon defeated him during the conquest and inflicted the same mutilation on him before bringing him to Jerusalem, where he died (Judges 1:4-7). He is recorded acknowledging the punishment as just retribution for his own cruelty, one of the few conquest-era accounts that quotes a defeated Canaanite ruler's own words.

witness.excerpt: But the affairs of the Canaanites were at this time in a flourishing condition; and they expected the Israelites with a great army at the city Bezek: having put the government into the hands of Adonibezek: which name denotes the Lord of Bezek : for Adoni in the Hebrew tongue is called Lord .

entries.title: Adonijah (David's son living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: David's fourth son. With his older brothers dead, he was the presumed heir. He tried to have himself crowned while David was still dying, and left Solomon, Nathan and Benaiah off the invitation.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Adonijah was David's fourth son and, with his older brothers dead, the presumed heir to the throne, so he tried to have himself crowned king while David was still dying, without inviting Solomon, Nathan the prophet, or Benaiah. Nathan and Bathsheba intervened, and David ordered Solomon anointed king immediately, collapsing Adonijah's attempted coup. Adonijah survived that failure only to be executed soon after for requesting marriage to one of David's former attendants, a request Solomon read as a renewed claim on the throne.

witness.excerpt: But Adonijah, who, while his father was living, attempted to gain possession of the government, came to the king's mother Bathsheba, and saluted her with great civility; and when she asked him, whether he came to her as desiring her
He was named Adonijah, and was in his disposition like to Absalom; and exalted himself as hoping to be king, and told his friends that he ought to take the government upon him.

The eldest was by Ahinoam, and he was called Arenon; the second was Daniel, by his wife Abigail; the name of the third was Absalom, by Maacah, the daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur; the fourth he named Adonijah, by his wife Haggith; the fifth was Shephatiah, by Abital; the sixth he called Ithream, by Eglah.

entries.title: Adonijah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Adonijah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Adonijah. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Adonikam (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: The census of returning exiles counts 666 men of his family in Ezra. Nehemiah's copy of the same list says 667, which is the kind of disagreement these two registers have all the way through.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Adonikam was the ancestor of a family of 666 men who returned from Babylonian exile to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel, according to the census list in Ezra 2:13; a slightly different number, 660, appears in the parallel list in Nehemiah 7:18. A further group of his descendants came up later under Ezra (Ezra 8:13).

entries.title: Adoniram (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Son of Abda, and the man in charge of forced labour under David, Solomon and, briefly, Rehoboam. He also goes by Adoram.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Adoniram, also called Adoram, was the son of Abda and served as the official in charge of forced labor levies under David, Solomon, and briefly Rehoboam (2 Samuel 20:24; 1 Kings 4:6; 1 Kings 12:18). When Rehoboam sent him to enforce the labor tax on the northern tribes after Solomon's death, the people stoned him to death, an act that helped trigger the kingdom's split into Israel and Judah (1 Kings 12:18).

entries.title: Adonizedec (King living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: The Amorite king of Jerusalem in Joshua's day. When Gibeon made peace with Israel he pulled together five Canaanite kings to attack it, and Joshua marched out to defend the city.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Adonizedec was the Amorite king of Jerusalem who organized a coalition of five Canaanite kings to attack Gibeon after it made peace with Israel, prompting Joshua's forces to march to Gibeon's defense in the battle where the sun and moon reportedly stood still (Joshua 10:1-13). His coalition was defeated and the five kings were captured, humiliated, and executed (Joshua 10:16-27). His name, meaning “lord of righteousness,” echoes the earlier Melchizedek, priest-king of the same city centuries before (Genesis 14:18), and the fourteenth-century BC Amarna letters independently show Jerusalem ruled by its own king corresponding with Egypt around this period, confirming the city's status as an established Canaanite city-state.

entries.title: Adoraim
entries.summary: Rehoboam fortified it after the kingdom split, one link in Judah's southern line of defence. The name survives in Dura, a village southwest of Hebron.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A fortified city built by Rehoboam as part of Judah's southern defensive line after the kingdom split (2 Chronicles 11:9). Its name survives in Dura, a village southwest of Hebron.

entries.title: Adoram (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: The same man as Adoniram, over the forced labour for David and Solomon. Years later Rehoboam sent him to collect tribute from the northern tribes in the crisis that split the kingdom.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Adoram, also called Adoniram, was the official in charge of forced labor under David and Solomon (1 Kings 4:6). Years later, King Rehoboam sent him to collect tribute from the northern tribes during the crisis that split the kingdom, and the people stoned him to death, a killing that confirmed the revolt against the house of David (1 Kings 12:18).

witness.excerpt: He also set Adoram over the tribute, and Sabathes and Achilaus over the records.

Nay, they were so bitter, and retained their wrath so long, that when he sent Adoram, which was over the tribute, that he might pacify them, and render them milder, and persuade them to forgive him, if he had said any thing that was rash or grievous to them in his youth, they would not hear it, but thre
Now Joctan, one of the sons of Heber, had these sons, Elmodad, Saleph, Asermoth, Jera, Adoram, Aizel, Decla, Ebal, Abimael, Sabeus, Ophir, Euilat, and Jobab.

entries.title: Adoram (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Adoram. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Adrammelech (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A son of Sennacherib who killed his own father. The same name belongs to an Assyrian god the people of Sepharim sacrificed their children to after they were resettled in Samaria.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Adrammelech was an Assyrian deity to whom the people of Sepharim sacrificed their children after being resettled in Samaria, and separately the name of one of Sennacherib's sons who assassinated him.

witness.excerpt: And when he had abode there a little while, he was treacherously assaulted, and died by the hands of his elder sons  Adrammelech and Sarasar: and was slain in his own temple, which was called Araske.

entries.title: Adrammelech (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 2 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Adria
entries.summary: The sea Paul's ship drifted across in the storm before the wreck, the central Mediterranean between Crete, Sicily and Malta.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Adria, or the sea of Adria, refers to the central Mediterranean waters between Crete, Sicily, and Malta through which Paul's ship drifted during the storm before his shipwreck (Acts 27:27). In the first century the term covered this broader stretch of sea rather than only the modern Adriatic between Italy and the Balkans.

entries.title: Adriel (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Saul had promised his elder daughter Merab to David, then gave her to Adriel instead. Their five sons were later handed over to the Gibeonites.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Adriel, son of Barzillai the Meholathite, married Merab, Saul's elder daughter, after Saul withdrew her from his earlier promise to give her to David (1 Samuel 18:19). Their five sons were later handed over to the Gibeonites and executed as part of the reparations for Saul's earlier massacre of Gibeonite lives (2 Samuel 21:8-9); a textual difficulty in that passage names Michal rather than Merab as the mother, which most interpreters resolve either as scribal confusion between the two sisters or as Michal having raised her sister's sons.

entries.title: Adullam
entries.summary: A Canaanite royal city in the Shephelah, near the valley of Elah. David killed Goliath in that valley. Later, running from Saul, he hid in a cave near Adullam, and his family joined him there, and so did everyone in distress.
entries.books: Joshua, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Nehemiah, Micah
entries.label: 7 books
entries.dictNote: Adullam was a Canaanite royal city in the Shephelah near the valley of Elah, where David killed Goliath. After fleeing Saul, David took refuge in a cave near Adullam, where he was joined by family members and by everyone in distress, debt, or discontent, roughly four hundred men who became the core of his fighting force. Rehoboam later fortified Adullam against Egyptian invasion, and Micah calls it "the glory of Israel."

witness.excerpt: And when I went to him I saw Parsaba, king of Adullam; and he spake unto us, and he made us a feast; 3 and when I was heated he gave me his daughter Bathshua to wife.
So when David had escaped in this manner out of Gath, he came to the tribe of Judah, and abode in a cave, by the city of Adullam.

Now Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, who, as we said before, was king of the two tribes, built strong and large cities, Bethlehem, and Etare, and Tekoa, and Bethzur, and Shoco, and Adullam, and Ipan, and Maresha, and Ziph, and Adorlam, and Lachlsh, and Azekah, and Zorah, and Aijalon, and Hebron; these he built first of all in the tribe of Judah.

entries.title: Adullamite
entries.summary: Hirah, Judah's friend in the story of Judah and Tamar, was one. It means a man from Adullam, a Canaanite town in Judah's territory.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Adullamite marks someone from Adullam, a Canaanite town in Judah's territory. Judah's friend Hirah, mentioned in the account of Judah and Tamar in Genesis 38, was an Adullamite, and Adullam later gave its name to the cave where David gathered the band of outcasts who became his core fighting force.

witness.excerpt:
And Judah sent a kid of the goats by the hand of his shepherd, an Adullamite, and he found her not; and he asked the people of the place, saying: "Where is the harlot who was here?" And they said unto him: "There

is no harlot here with us." 15.

Testament of Judah, Chapter 8

8 1, 2 And I had much cattle, and I had for chief herdsman Iram the Adullamite.

entries.title: Adummim
entries.summary: The name means the red ones, and it was a pass on the road between Jerusalem and Jericho. It marked the boundary between Judah and Benjamin.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Adummim, meaning "the red ones," was a pass on the road between Jerusalem and Jericho, on the boundary between the territories of Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15:7; 18:17). The rugged, blood-colored rock of the ascent made it a natural setting for banditry, and the location is traditionally associated with the road pictured in Jesus' parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30-37).

entries.title: Aeneas (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Paralysed and in bed for eight years at Lydda until Peter told him to get up and make his bed. Many in Lydda and on the plain of Sharon turned to the Lord after it.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Aeneas was a paralyzed man at Lydda who had been bedridden for eight years before Peter healed him, telling him to get up and make his bed; the miracle led many in Lydda and the nearby plain of Sharon to turn to the Lord (Acts 9:32-35).

witness.excerpt: Now it came to pass that Obodas was dead; and Aeneas, whose name was afterward changed to Aretas, (12) took the government, for Sylleus endeavored by calumnies to get him turned out of his principality, that he might himself take it; with which design he gave much money t

entries.title: Aenon
entries.summary: John the Baptist baptised here because there was plenty of water. John 3:23 puts it near Salim, and where exactly that was is still debated.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A place "near Salim" with abundant water where John the Baptist carried out baptisms (John 3:23). Its precise location is debated, with proposals ranging from a site near Salim east of Shechem to another closer to the Jordan Valley further south, but its description as a well-watered spot fits either region.

entries.title: Agabus (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: A prophet at Antioch who said a severe famine was coming. It came in the reign of Claudius, and the church sent relief to the believers in Judea.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Agabus was a Christian prophet in the early church who, at Antioch, predicted a severe famine that later occurred during the reign of Claudius, prompting the church to send relief to believers in Judea (Acts 11:27-30). Years later he met Paul at Caesarea and dramatically bound his own hands and feet with Paul's belt to warn that Paul would be arrested and handed over to the Gentiles if he went to Jerusalem, a warning Paul heeded as a caution but not a command to turn back (Acts 21:10-14). His famine prediction is one of the clearer instances in Acts of a specific, later-verified prophecy.

witness.excerpt: Hudson’s Note here: “This, says he, is that famine foretold by Agabus Acts 11:28.

entries.title: Agag (King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Numbers names him once, and he is a king from the wilderness years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Agag (King living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: King of the Amalekites. Saul was told to destroy him and his people completely. He spared Agag and the best of the livestock, and that disobedience cost him God's favour.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Agag was a king of the Amalekites whom King Saul was ordered to destroy completely along with his people and livestock, but Saul spared Agag and the best animals instead, a direct act of disobedience that cost Saul God's favor and the kingdom. The prophet Samuel personally executed Agag afterward to finish what Saul had refused to do. Agag also appears to function as a dynastic title for Amalekite kings generally, since a much later Amalekite figure, Haman in the book of Esther, is identified as an Agagite.

entries.title: Agagite (King living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: What the book of Esther calls Haman, most likely marking him as a descendant of Agag, the Amalekite king Saul spared against God's command and Samuel then killed.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Agagite is the title given to Haman in the book of Esther, most likely marking him as a descendant of Agag, the Amalekite king Saul had spared against God's command and whom Samuel then killed. The label sharpens the story's irony, since it casts Haman's plot against the Jews as a late echo of Israel's old unfinished conflict with Amalek.

entries.title: Agee (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: His son Shammah was one of David's three chief mighty men, and Agee is named only to say whose son that was.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: The father of Shammah, one of David's three chief mighty men, named in the roster of 2 Samuel 23:11. He appears only to identify his son.

entries.title: Agrippa (Tetrarch living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Herod Agrippa the Second, the last king of the Herodian line. Paul made his defence before him and his sister Bernice, and Agrippa told him he had almost persuaded him to become a Christian.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Herod Agrippa the Second was the last king of the Herodian dynasty, and Paul made his defense of the gospel before him and his sister Bernice, with Agrippa famously telling Paul he had almost persuaded him to become a Christian.

witness.excerpt: Agrippa also did himself write after the manner following, on behalf of the Jews: \"Agrippa, to the magistrates, senate, and people of the Ephesians, sendeth greeting.

AGRIPPA IS ADVANCED FROM CHALCIS TO A GREATER KINGDOM.

1 NOW after the death of Herod, king of Chalcis, Claudius set Agrippa, the son of Agrippa, over his uncle's kingdom, while Cumanus took upon him the office of procurator of the rest, which was a Roman province, and therein he succeeded Alexander; under which Cureanus began the troubles, a

Now Agrippa was [about this time] sent to succeed Caesar in the government of the countries beyond the Ionian Sea, upon whom Herod lighted when he was wintering about Mitylene, for he had been his particular friend and companion, a
WHEN Agrippa had finished what I have above related at Berytus, he removed to Tiberias, a city of Galilee.
Notes 1 Agrippa dwelt with Cesar, as said before : XIX.9.2 .

entries.title: Agur (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Proverbs 30 is his. He is called the son of Jakeh, and nothing else about him is recorded.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: The otherwise unknown author to whom the sayings of Proverbs 30 are attributed, introduced simply as the son of Jakeh; nothing else about him is recorded in the text.

witness.excerpt: They are to the like purport with one branch of Agur’s prayer: One thing have I required of thee, deny me it not before I die: give me not riches; lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, who is the Lord? Prov.

entries.title: Ahab (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: King of northern Israel for about twenty-two years. He married Jezebel, a Phoenician princess. She brought Baal worship into a kingdom that was supposed to belong to Yahweh alone, and he let her.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Ahab was king of northern Israel for about twenty-two years, remembered above all for marrying the Phoenician princess Jezebel and letting her import Baal worship into a kingdom that was supposed to belong to Yahweh alone. His reign is really the story of his running conflict with the prophet Elijah, from the three-year drought Elijah announced as judgment to the fire-from-heaven contest on Mount Carmel to Elijah's blunt condemnation of Ahab for murdering Naboth to steal his vineyard. Ahab's own father, Omri, is confirmed outside the Bible on the Moabite Stone and in Assyrian records, which also name Ahab directly as a major military contributor at the battle of Qarqar in 853 BC.

witness.excerpt: NOW Ahab the king of Israel dwelt in Samaria, and held the government for twenty-two years; and made no alteration in the conduct of the kings that were his predecessors, but only in such things as were of his own invention for

WHEN the affairs of Ahab were thus, at that very time the son of Hadad, [Benhadad,] who was king of the Syrians and of Damascus, got together an army out of all his country, and procured thirty-two kings beyond Euphrates to be his auxiliaries:
899.] And now Ahaziah, the son of Ahab, reigned over Israel, and made his abode in Samaria.

This Omri also died in Samaria and Ahab his son succeeded him.
6.
And it was Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab, whom he had married, who taught him to be a bad man in other respects, and also to worship foreign gods.

entries.title: Ahab (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Jeremiah names him twice, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Aharah (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Benjamin's third son in the 1 Chronicles 8 list. Numbers calls him Ahiram and 1 Chronicles 7 calls him Aher, likely the same man, since the lists of Benjamin's sons vary.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Aharah was the third son of Benjamin, listed in the tribal genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:1). He is likely the same figure called Ahiram in Numbers 26:38 and Aher in 1 Chronicles 7:12, since the lists of Benjamin's sons vary somewhat between Genesis, Numbers, and Chronicles.

entries.title: Aharhel (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A descendant of Harum's clan, in a short and difficult fragment of Judah's genealogy that leaves little else to reconstruct.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Aharhel is named as a descendant of Harum's clan in a terse and difficult fragment of Judah's genealogy (1 Chr. 4:8). Little else can be reconstructed about his family from the text.

entries.title: Ahasai (Levite living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of the priests in the list of those who resettled Jerusalem after the exile, named as an ancestor of Maasiai. 1 Chronicles 9:12 gives the same man as Jahzerah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ahasai was a priest listed as an ancestor of Maasiai among those who resettled in Jerusalem after the exile (Nehemiah 11:13). The parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 9:12 gives the same figure's name as Jahzerah.

entries.title: Ahasbai (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Eliphelet's father. His son was one of David's mighty men, and the parallel roster in Chronicles garbles the family line into Ur and Eliphal.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Father of Eliphelet, one of David's mighty men listed in the roster of 2 Samuel 23:34; the parallel roster in 1 Chronicles 11:35 gives a garbled form of the same family line as Ur and Eliphal.

entries.title: Ahasuerus (Emperor Xerxes I, living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: The Persian king who deposed Vashti and made Esther his queen. He is usually identified with Xerxes the First, whose reign is documented independently in Greek and Persian sources.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Ahasuerus is the Persian king who made Esther his queen after deposing Vashti, usually identified with Xerxes the First, whose reign is independently documented in Greek and Persian sources and whose famously lavish, extended banquets match the opening scene of the book of Esther closely. A different Ahasuerus appears briefly in the book of Daniel as the father of Darius the Mede.

entries.title: Ahava
entries.summary: A river or canal in Babylonia. Ezra gathered the exiles there before the journey to Jerusalem and proclaimed a fast, because he was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ahava was a river or canal in Babylonia where Ezra gathered the exiles who would return with him to Jerusalem, and where he proclaimed a fast to seek God's protection for the journey since he was ashamed to ask the king for a military escort (Ezra 8:15, 21-23). Its precise location is unknown, though it likely lay along one of the canals feeding the Euphrates near ancient Babylon.

entries.title: Ahaz (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He abandoned his predecessors' reforms, sacrificed his own son in the fire and closed the temple. Facing a coalition of enemies, he paid Assyria for protection instead of trusting the promise Isaiah brought, and Judah stayed an Assyrian vassal for a generation. The Immanuel prophecy was given in his crisis.
entries.books: 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Isaiah, Hosea, Micah
entries.label: 6 books
entries.dictNote: Ahaz was a king of Judah who abandoned the reforms of his predecessors, sacrificing his own son in the fire and closing the temple to set up pagan altars instead, and rather than trust God's promise of protection through the prophet Isaiah, he paid the Assyrian empire for protection against a coalition of enemies, a decision that made Judah an Assyrian vassal for a generation. It was during Ahaz's crisis that Isaiah delivered the famous prophecy of a child to be called Immanuel, God with us.

witness.excerpt: And how Hezekiah reigned instead of Ahaz ; and what actions of piety and justice he did.

entries.title: Ahaz (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Not the king of Judah. This Ahaz appears only in the family lists at 1 Chronicles 8:35 and 9:42, and nothing else about him is recorded.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahaziah (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Ahab's grandson through his mother Athaliah, and king of Judah for only one year. He was killed in the same purge that brought Jehu to power.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Two kings named Ahaziah appear in the Old Testament, one ruling northern Israel and dying after a fall through a palace lattice sent him seeking healing from a foreign god instead of the Lord, provoking Elijah's rebuke; the other ruling Judah, a grandson of Ahab through his mother Athaliah, killed in the same purge that brought Jehu to power after only one year on the throne.

witness.excerpt: For as we told you before, he was departed from his obedience to his brother [Ahaziah:] while he payed to his father Ahab two hundred thousand sheep, with their fleeces of wool.

entries.title: Ahaziah (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He ruled northern Israel, fell through a palace lattice, and sent to a foreign god to ask about healing. Elijah rebuked him for not asking the Lord.
entries.label: 3 books

entries.title: Ahban (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A son of Abishur and his wife Abihail in Judah's genealogy, and nothing more is known.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ahban was a son of Abishur and his wife Abihail, listed in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles 2. Nothing further is known of him.

entries.title: Aher (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Some identify him with Ahiram, Benjamin's son in Numbers 26:38. Here he is a Benjamite ancestor of Hushim in 1 Chronicles 7:12.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Aher was a Benjamite ancestor of Hushim, named in the tribal genealogy of 1 Chronicles 7:12; some identify him with Ahiram, a son of Benjamin listed in Numbers 26:38.

entries.title: Ahi (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Ahi means brother, and this one was a chief of a family of Gad living in Bashan.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahi (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: The name means my brother. Two unrelated men in Chronicles carry it, and this is the one in Asher's line.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ahi, meaning “brother” or “my brother,” is the name of two otherwise unrelated men in Chronicles: a chief of a family within the tribe of Gad living in Bashan (1 Chronicles 5:15) and a family head within the tribe of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:34).

entries.title: Ahiah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A man from the exile and the return, and Nehemiah is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahiah (Priest living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: The priest with Saul at Michmash, carrying the ephod when Saul asked whether to go into the battle. He is a son of Ahitub, and the same man the lists elsewhere call Ahimelech.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahiah (Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Ahijah, the prophet from Shiloh. He tore his own cloak into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam, for the ten tribes about to be torn from Solomon's line, and after Solomon died the kingdom split just that way.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ahijah was a prophet from Shiloh who tore his own cloak into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam as a symbolic prophecy that ten tribes would be torn from Solomon's line and given to him, a prophecy fulfilled when the kingdom split after Solomon's death.

entries.title: Ahiam (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Son of Sharar the Hararite, and one of David's thirty mighty warriors. Chronicles calls his father Sacar. Nothing further is recorded.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ahiam, son of Sharar (also called Sacar) the Hararite, was one of David's thirty mighty warriors (2 Samuel 23:33; 1 Chronicles 11:35). Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Ahian (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: From Shemida's line, in Manasseh's genealogy east of the Jordan, with nothing further recorded.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ahian was a Manassite descendant of Shemida, listed in the tribal genealogy of Manasseh east of the Jordan (1 Chr. 7:19). Nothing further is recorded of him.

entries.title: Ahiezer (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Dan's leader in the wilderness census, one of twelve men appointed to assist Moses.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ahiezer was the tribal leader of Dan during the wilderness census, one of twelve representatives appointed to assist Moses.

entries.title: Ahiezer (Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a warrior from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahihud (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: When the land west of the Jordan was divided, each tribe sent one leader to work with Eleazar the priest and Joshua. Ahihud was Asher's.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A leader of the tribe of Asher chosen by Moses to help Eleazar the priest and Joshua divide the land of Canaan among the tribes west of the Jordan (Numbers 34:16-27). He represented Asher on the twelve-man commission, one leader from each tribe. He is a different man from the Ahihud, son of Bela, listed in Benjamin's genealogy (1 Chronicles 8:7).

entries.title: Ahihud (Man living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: Benjamin's grandson through Bela, and head of one of the families deported from Geba to Manahath. He is not the Ahihud of Asher who helped divide the land.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A son of Bela and grandson of Benjamin, listed as head of a family group that was deported from Geba to Manahath, likely during an early population shift within Benjamin's territory (1 Chronicles 8:6-7). He is a different man from the Ahihud of Asher who helped divide the land under Moses (Numbers 34:27).

entries.title: Ahijah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 8 men called Ahijah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named 4 times in 1 Kings and 2 Kings.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Ahijah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 8 men called Ahijah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahijah (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: A man from the united kingdom, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahijah (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: A man from the united kingdom. 1 Kings names him once.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahijah (Man living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: A man from the years before the monarchy. 1 Chronicles names him once.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahijah (Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a warrior from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahikam (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A court official under Josiah. He backed the warnings of Huldah the prophetess and later protected Jeremiah from a mob that wanted him killed, and Gedaliah was his son.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Ahikam was a court official under King Josiah who supported the prophetess Huldah's warnings and later protected the prophet Jeremiah from a mob that wanted him killed for his prophecies of judgment. His son Gedaliah was later appointed governor of Judah after Jerusalem's fall.

witness.excerpt: 588.] Now the general of the army, Nebuzaradan, when he had carried the people of the Jews into captivity, left the poor, and those that had deserted, in the countrey; and made one, whose name was Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, a person of a noble family, their governour.

entries.title: Ahilud (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Two of his sons served kings: Jehoshaphat was David's royal recorder, and Baana governed one of Solomon's twelve districts.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Ahilud was the father of Jehoshaphat, David's royal recorder, and also of Baana, one of Solomon's twelve district governors.

witness.excerpt: He had for the general of his whole army Joab; and he made Jehoshaphat, the son of Ahilud, recorder.

entries.title: Ahimaaz (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Ahimaaz. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in 1 Kings.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahimaaz (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahimaaz (Priest living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Zadok's son, who carried intelligence to David during Absalom's rebellion. After the battle he raced another messenger to be first with the news.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ahimaaz was Zadok's son, and during Absalom's rebellion he served as a courier relaying intelligence to David, later racing another messenger to be first to bring David news of the battle's outcome, though he couldn't bring himself to tell David directly that his son Absalom was dead.

witness.excerpt: But now Ahimaaz, the son of Zadok the high priest, went to Joab, and desired he would permit him to go and tell David of this victory, and to bring him the good news that God had afforded his assistance and his providence to him.

entries.title: Ahiman (Levite living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a Levite from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahiman (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: One of the descendants of Anak. That clan's size terrified the Israelite spies. Decades later Caleb drove Ahiman and his brothers out of Hebron, the land he had been promised.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Ahiman was one of the descendants of Anak, the giant clan whose size terrified the Israelite spies, and Caleb personally drove Ahiman and his brothers out of Hebron decades later when he finally claimed the land he'd been promised.

entries.title: Ahimelech (High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: The priest at Nob. He helped David, who was fleeing Saul, without knowing it, and gave him the consecrated bread and Goliath's sword. Once Doeg reported it, Saul had him and the rest of the priests at Nob massacred.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ahimelech was the priest at Nob who unknowingly helped David while he was fleeing Saul, giving him consecrated bread and Goliath's sword, and Saul had him and the rest of the priestly community at Nob massacred for it once Doeg reported the assistance.

witness.excerpt: Accordingly when Saul commanded his guards to slay Ahimelech, and the Priests at Nob, they knew it to be an unlawful command, and would not obey it, 1 Sam.

To this his end did Saul come, according to the prophecy of Samuel; because he disobeyed the commands of God about the Amalekites; and on the account of his destroying the family of Ahimelech, the High Priest, with Ahimelech himself; and the city of the High Priests.

entries.title: Ahimelech (Priest living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: A priest in David's time, named in the list at 2 Samuel 8:17 and in the priestly divisions of 1 Chronicles 24. He is not the priest of Nob, who belongs to Saul's years.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Ahimelech (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Ahimelech. This one is a warrior from the united kingdom, named once in 1 Samuel.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahimoth (Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Kohathite Levite in 1 Chronicles 6, whom the same genealogy later calls Mahath.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ahimoth was a Kohathite Levite named in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 6. The same genealogy later gives the name as Mahath, reflecting the sort of variant spellings common in these priestly family records.

entries.title: Ahinadab (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Solomon put him over Mahanaim, east of the Jordan, one of twelve district officers who each supplied the royal household for one month a year.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of Solomon's twelve district officers, assigned to Mahanaim east of the Jordan, responsible for supplying provisions to the royal household one month each year (1 Kings 4:14).

entries.title: Ahinoam (Woman living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: The Ahinoam from Jezreel whom David married, mother of his firstborn son Amnon, and a different woman from Saul's wife of the same name.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Ahinoam was the name of two women in David's life: Saul's wife, and a separate Ahinoam from Jezreel whom David married and who became the mother of his firstborn son Amnon.

witness.excerpt: [The wife was Ahinoam.] 18 This farther account is not, I think, found in Josephus’s present works.

The eldest was by Ahinoam, and he was called Arenon; the second was Daniel, by his wife Abigail; the name of the third was Absalom, by Maacah, the daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur; the fourth he named Adonijah, by his wife Haggith; the fifth w
He had with him also his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail; and he dwelt in Gath.

entries.title: Ahinoam (Woman living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Samuel names her once, and she is a woman from the united kingdom.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahio (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Ahio. This one is a man from the wilderness years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahio (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: He and his brother Uzzah were guiding the cart that carried the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem. Uzzah reached out to steady it and was struck dead.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ahio was Uzzah's brother, and together they were guiding the cart carrying the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem when Uzzah reached out to steady it and was struck dead.

entries.title: Ahio (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ahira (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: He stood for Naphtali among the twelve tribal leaders who helped Moses with the wilderness census.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ahira was the tribal leader of Naphtali during the wilderness census, one of twelve representatives appointed to assist Moses.

entries.title: Ahiram (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Benjamin's son, and the man the Ahiramite clan in the Numbers 26 census came from. Genesis 46:21 probably calls him Ehi.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ahiram was a son of Benjamin, ancestor of the Ahiramite clan counted in the wilderness census (Num. 26:38). He is probably the same figure called Ehi in Genesis 46:21, since the lists of Benjamin's sons differ somewhat across Genesis, Numbers, and Chronicles.

entries.title: Ahiramites (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: The clan descended from Ahiram, Benjamin's son, counted in the Numbers 26 census.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ahiramites were the clan descended from Ahiram, a son of Benjamin, counted in the Numbers 26 census; the same man is usually identified with Ehi in Genesis 46:21.

entries.title: Ahisamach (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Father of Oholiab, the skilled craftsman from Dan who worked beside Bezalel on the tabernacle.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ahisamach was the father of Oholiab, the skilled craftsman from the tribe of Dan appointed alongside Bezalel to help construct the tabernacle.

witness.excerpt: Now their names are set down in writing in the sacred Books; and they were these: Besaleel , the son of Uri , of the tribe of Judah, the grandson of Miriam, the sister of their conductor; and Aholiab the son of Ahisamach , of the tribe of Dan.

entries.title: Ahishar (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Listed once in the tribal genealogies, at 1 Chronicles 7:10, and nothing else about him is recorded.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: An official "over the household" in Solomon's royal administration, part of the list of high officers who ran the kingdom's affairs (1 Kings 4:6).

entries.title: Ahishar (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Solomon's steward, over the household in the list of high officers who ran the kingdom.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Benjamite listed among the sons of Bilhan in the tribal genealogies, where the Hebrew text actually reads Ahishahar, "brother of dawn" (1 Chronicles 7:10). Despite the similar spelling, he is a different person from the Ahishar who served as steward of Solomon's household.

entries.title: Ahithophel (David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: David's most trusted counsellor, whose advice was treated as if it came from God. He went over to Absalom. When Absalom turned down his plan for a rival counsellor's, Ahithophel saw the rebellion was finished, went home, put his affairs in order and hanged himself.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ahithophel was David's most trusted counselor, so respected that his advice was regarded as equal to consulting God directly, and his defection to Absalom's rebellion was one of the most devastating betrayals of David's reign. When Absalom rejected Ahithophel's sound military advice in favor of a rival counselor's plan, Ahithophel recognized the rebellion was doomed, went home, put his affairs in order, and hanged himself.

witness.excerpt: Among them came Ahithophel the Gilonite, a counsellor of David's, and two hundred men out of Jerusalem itself, who knew not his intentions, but were sent for as to a sacrifice.

entries.title: Ahitub (High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Ahimelech's father, in Israel's high priestly line.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Ahitub was a common name among Israel's high priestly line, borne by at least two priests in that lineage, including Ahimelech's father and, generations later, Zadok's father.

witness.excerpt:
