entries.title: Apollos (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: An eloquent Jewish preacher from Alexandria who knew the Scriptures and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only John's baptism. Priscilla and Aquila took him aside and explained the way of God more fully. In Corinth he did so well that a faction started claiming him over Paul.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Apollos was an eloquent Jewish preacher from Alexandria, well versed in the Scriptures, who taught accurately about Jesus but knew only the baptism of John until Priscilla and Aquila took him aside and explained the way of God more fully. He went on to become an effective teacher in Corinth, so much so that a faction in that fractious church began claiming him as their favorite leader over Paul, a rivalry Paul directly addressed in his letters.

entries.title: Apollyon (A male deity/angel in the New Testament)
entries.summary: The name means Destroyer. John gives it in Revelation 9:11 to the angel over the locust creatures from the abyss, the Greek for Abaddon in the same verse.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Apollyon, meaning "Destroyer," is the Greek name John gives in Revelation 9:11 to the angel ruling over the locust-like creatures released from the abyss, equivalent to the Hebrew name Abaddon, covered separately, which appears in the same verse.

entries.title: Appaim (People, perhaps from Aph)
entries.summary: Nadab's son, in the Jerahmeelite branch of Judah, and his line ran on through his son Ishi. Nothing further is recorded of him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Appaim was a son of Nadab in the Jerahmeelite branch of Judah's tribe, one of the family lines that helped establish Judah's prominence among the twelve tribes (1 Chronicles 2:30-31). His own line continued through his son Ishi. Nothing further is recorded of him.

entries.title: Apphia (Woman living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Paul names her beside Philemon and Archippus at the opening of his letter to Philemon, and tradition, not the text, makes her Philemon's wife.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Christian woman at Colossae whom Paul addresses alongside Philemon and Archippus at the opening of his letter to Philemon (Philem. 1:2). Tradition, though not the text itself, identifies her as Philemon's wife, and her place in the greeting suggests she held some standing in the household church that met there.

entries.title: Appii (Forum of Appius)
entries.summary: Appii Forum, a market town on the Appian Way about 43 miles from Rome. Christians came out that far to meet Paul as he was brought to the capital a prisoner.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Appii, more fully 'Appii Forum' in most English Bibles, is not a person but a town or market square along the Appian Way in Italy, about 43 miles from Rome, where a group of Christians met Paul as he traveled toward the capital as a prisoner (Acts 28:15).

entries.title: Aquila (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: A Jewish tentmaker from Pontus. He and his wife Priscilla had been expelled from Rome with other Jews, met Paul in Corinth, and worked beside him. Churches met in their home in more than one city.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Aquila was a Jewish tentmaker from Pontus who, with his wife Priscilla, had been expelled from Rome along with other Jews and met Paul in Corinth, where they worked together and became close partners in ministry. The couple hosted churches in their home in multiple cities and helped instruct Apollos more fully in the faith.

entries.title: Ar
entries.summary: The chief city of Moab on the Arnon, so central that "Ar of Moab" could stand for Moab itself. God told Israel to leave it alone on the way through. Its ruins survive at Rabba in modern Jordan.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Ar was the chief city of Moab on the Arnon River, so central to the nation that "Ar of Moab" became a byname for Moab itself (Numbers 21:28; Isaiah 15:1). It was spared by God's command when Israel passed through Moabite territory (Deuteronomy 2:9), and in Roman times it was known as Areopolis; its ruins survive at Rabba in modern Jordan.

entries.title: Ara (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Jether's son, and head of an Asherite family. Nothing else is recorded about him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ara was one of the sons of Jether, listed among the heads of Asherite families in 1 Chronicles 7:38. Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Arab
entries.summary: A town near Hebron in Judah's hill country, likely home to Paarai the Arbite of David's mighty warriors. It is generally identified with the ruin of er-Rabiyeh, south of Hebron.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Arab was a town in the hill country of Judah, listed in Joshua 15:52 among the cities near Hebron. It was likely the hometown of Paarai the Arbite, one of David's mighty warriors named in 2 Samuel 23:35, and is generally identified with the ruin of er-Rabiyeh south of Hebron.

entries.title: Arabia
entries.summary: Paul says he went away into Arabia for a time after his conversion, and in the New Testament the word covers the region south and east of Judea.
entries.label: 5 books
entries.dictNote: Arabia in the New Testament refers to the region south and east of Judea, and Paul mentions withdrawing there for a period after his conversion, likely a time of reflection before beginning his public ministry.

entries.title: Arad
entries.summary: Its king attacked Israel as they came up toward Canaan from the south and took prisoners, and Israel destroyed the town under the ban. The Canaanite city lay about 20 miles south of Hebron, at Tel Arad.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Arad was a Canaanite city about 20 miles south of Hebron whose king attacked Israel as they approached Canaan from the south, taking prisoners, before Israel destroyed the town under the ban (Numbers 21:1-3; 33:40); it was later subdued by Joshua's forces (Joshua 12:14). The name also belongs to a descendant of Benjamin through Beriah (1 Chronicles 8:15). Excavations at Tel Arad have uncovered both a Canaanite city and, on a nearby hill, a fortified Israelite citadel with its own small temple, among the few Israelite sanctuaries yet excavated outside Jerusalem.

entries.title: Arah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: He headed a family among the returning exiles. His descendant Shecaniah's daughter married Tobiah, the Ammonite official who opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Arah was the head of a family among the returning exiles, and his descendant Shecaniah's daughter married Tobiah, the Ammonite official who later opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding project.

entries.title: Aram (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

entries.dictNote: Aram is the biblical name for the region and people better known as Syria, centered on Damascus, and Aram was one of Israel's most persistent enemies through the divided-monarchy period, repeatedly clashing with both Israelite kingdoms under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael.

entries.title: Aram-zobah
entries.summary: An Aramean kingdom under its king Hadadezer. David beat it in a series of campaigns, pushed Israel's borders out, and brought home heavy tribute.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Aram-zobah was an Aramean kingdom David defeated in a series of campaigns under its king Hadadezer, expanding Israel's territory and bringing substantial tribute into David's kingdom.

entries.title: Aran (Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: A descendant of Seir the Horite, among the clan chiefs of Edom. The Horites were the cave-dwelling people of Mount Seir before the Edomites pushed them out, and lists like this keep their tribal structure. Nothing else about him is recorded.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Aran was a descendant of Seir the Horite, listed among the clan chiefs of Edom in Genesis 36:28 and 1 Chronicles 1:42. The Horites were the indigenous cave-dwelling population of Mount Seir before the Edomites displaced them, and genealogies like this one preserve their tribal structure. Nothing else about him is recorded.

entries.title: Ararat
entries.summary: Noah's ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat as the floodwaters went down. The region is in what is now eastern Turkey.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: The mountains of Ararat, in the region of modern eastern Turkey, are where Genesis records Noah's ark came to rest as the floodwaters receded.

witness.excerpt: And the ark went and rested on the top of Lûbâr, one of the mountains of Ararat.  29.
And Noah slept with his fathers, and was buried on Mount Lûbâr in the land of Ararat.
And in the seventh week in the first year thereof, in this jubilee, Noah planted vines on the mountain on which the ark had rested, named Lûbâr,  one of the Ararat Mountains, and they 1320 A.M.

entries.title: Araunah (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: The Jebusite, also called Ornan, whose threshing floor David bought for the site of Solomon's temple. He offered it as a gift, and David insisted on paying full price.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Araunah, also spelled Ornan, was the Jebusite from whom David purchased the threshing floor that became the site of Solomon's temple, insisting on paying full price rather than accept it as a gift.

witness.excerpt: I shall now make mention of Araunah, who was a wealthy man among the Jebusites, but was not slain by David in the siege of Jerusalem, because of the good-will he bore to the Hebrews, and a particular benignity and affection which he had to the king himsel

When God heard his supplication, he caused the pestilence to cease, and sent Gad the prophet to him, and commanded him to go up immediately to the thrashing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite, and build an altar there to God, and offer sacrifices.

entries.title: Arbahite (Beth-arabah)
entries.summary: It marks Abi-albon, one of David's mighty men, as a man of Beth-arabah, a town in the Arabah plain near the Dead Sea.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Arbahite identifies Abi-albon, one of David's mighty men, as being from Beth-arabah, a town in the Arabah plain near the Dead Sea assigned to Judah and Benjamin.

entries.title: Arbite (Arabia)
entries.summary: Paarai, of David's mighty men, came from Arab in Judah's hill country, and this is the label that says so.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Arbite identifies Paarai, one of David's mighty men, as being from Arab, a town in the hill country of Judah.

entries.title: Archelaus (Ethnarch living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Herod the Great's son. He inherited Judea, Samaria and Idumea and ruled them as ethnarch, harshly enough that his own subjects sent a delegation to Rome against him, and Augustus deposed him and exiled him to Gaul. Joseph settled in Galilee coming back from Egypt because Archelaus was reigning in Judea.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Son of Herod the Great, who inherited Judea, Samaria, and Idumea after his father's death and ruled them as ethnarch. His harsh rule prompted a delegation of his own subjects to petition Rome against him, and Augustus eventually deposed and exiled him to Gaul. Joseph's decision to settle in Galilee rather than Judea on returning from Egypt was made because Archelaus was reigning there (Matthew 2:22).

witness.excerpt: Archelaus also, Herod’s son, did like his father in the appointment of the High Priests: as did the Romans also, who took the government over the Jews into their hands afterward.

WHEN Archelaus was entered on his ethnarchy, and was come into Judea, he accused Joazar, the son of Boethus, of assisting the seditious, and took away the high priesthood from him, and put Eleazar his brother in his place.
And now Archelaus took possession of his ethnarchy, and used not the Jews only, but the Samaritans also, barbarously; and this out of his resentment of their old quarrels with him.

AND now Archelaus's part of Judea was reduced into a province, and Coponius, one of the equestrian order among the Romans, was sent as a procurator, having the power of [life and] death put into his hands by Caesar.

But when Archelaus, king of Cappadocia, heard of the state that Herod was in, and being in great distress about his daughter, and the young man [her husband], and grieving with Herod, as with a man that was his friend, on account of so gr

entries.title: Archevite (Erech)
entries.summary: People of Erech, better known as Uruk, settled in Samaria by the Assyrians. Later they wrote to the Persian king against the rebuilding of Jerusalem's temple. Uruk itself was one of the world's earliest cities, the traditional setting of the Epic of Gilgamesh, and its ruins have been dug in modern Iraq.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Archevites were people of Erech, the ancient Mesopotamian city better known as Uruk, among the foreign populations the Assyrians settled in Samaria who later wrote to the Persian king opposing the rebuilding of Jerusalem's temple. Uruk was one of the world's earliest cities and the traditional setting of the Epic of Gilgamesh, and its extensive ruins have been excavated in modern Iraq.

entries.title: Archi (People, perhaps from Arach)
entries.summary: Hushai's clan. He was the loyal friend of David who worked against Ahithophel's advice during Absalom's rebellion.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: The Archites were a clan associated with Hushai, David's loyal friend who helped counter Ahithophel's advice during Absalom's rebellion.

entries.title: Archippus (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Paul calls him a fellow soldier and tells him in public to finish the ministry he received in the Lord. He was at Colossae, likely part of Philemon's household.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Archippus was a Christian at Colossae, likely a member of Philemon's household, whom Paul calls a “fellow soldier” and urges publicly to fulfill the ministry he had received in the Lord (Colossians 4:17; Philemon 1:2).

entries.title: Arcturus (A star or constellation)
entries.summary: The King James rendering of a Hebrew word in Job. It most likely means the Great Bear, not the star we now call Arcturus.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Arcturus is not a person but the King James rendering of a Hebrew word in Job 9:9 and 38:32 that most likely designates the constellation now called Ursa Major, the Great Bear, rather than the star Arcturus itself; the verses point to God's authority over the fixed courses of the constellations.

entries.title: Ard (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Bela's son and Benjamin's grandson, from whom the Ardites came. 1 Chronicles 8:3 calls him Addar.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ard (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: A grandson of Benjamin through Bela, and the ancestor of the Ardites. Chronicles calls him Addar.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ard was a grandson of Benjamin, son of Bela, and became the ancestor of the clan of the Ardites; he is called Addar in the parallel genealogy of 1 Chronicles 8:3 (Genesis 46:21; Numbers 26:40).

entries.title: Ardites (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: The clan from Ard, Benjamin's grandson through Bela, counted in the Numbers 26 census.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ardites were the clan descended from Ard, a grandson of Benjamin through Bela, counted in the Numbers 26 census; the same man is called Addar in 1 Chronicles 8:3.

entries.title: Ardon (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Youngest of Caleb's three sons by his first wife Azubah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: The youngest of Caleb's three sons by his first wife Azubah, part of the Judahite genealogy in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 2:18).

entries.title: Areli (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: He went down to Egypt with Jacob among the seventy, a son of Gad, and his clan, the Arelites, was counted again in the wilderness census.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Areli was a son of Gad and ancestor of the Arelite clan, listed among the seventy who went down to Egypt with Jacob and later among the clans counted in the wilderness census (Genesis 46:16; Numbers 26:17).

witness.excerpt: And these are the names of their sons who went with him into Egypt: the sons of Gad: Ziphion, and Haggi, and Shuni, and Ezbon, (and Eri) and Areli, and Arodi--eight.

entries.title: Areopagite (Areopagus)
entries.summary: Dionysius was one, a member of the old council of Athens that met on the rock of the Areopagus. He was among the few Athenians who believed after Paul spoke there.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Areopagite marks Dionysius as a member of the Areopagus, the ancient council of Athens that met on the rock outcrop of that name near the Acropolis. He was among the few Athenians who believed after hearing Paul's speech there, and the Areopagus itself still stands today, overlooking the Athenian agora.

entries.title: Areopagus
entries.summary: Mars' Hill. It was a rocky outcrop below the Acropolis in Athens and also the council of leading magistrates that met on it. Paul was brought before them to explain what he taught about Jesus and the resurrection, and gave his speech about the unknown god.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: The Areopagus, Mars' Hill, was both a rocky outcrop below the Acropolis in Athens and the ancient council that met there, composed of the city's leading magistrates and former magistrates. Paul was brought before this body to explain his teaching about Jesus and the resurrection, and delivered there his address to the men of Athens about the unknown god (Acts 17:19-34).

entries.title: Aretas (King living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Aretas IV, king of the Nabataeans at Petra. His daughter was married to Herod Antipas until Antipas divorced her for Herodias, and the war that followed went against Antipas. An official of his held Damascus and tried to arrest Paul, who got away lowered over the wall in a basket.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Aretas IV was king of the Nabataean kingdom based at Petra, whose daughter married Herod Antipas until Antipas divorced her to marry Herodias, an insult that led to war between the two rulers, a conflict Antipas lost. After the death of Emperor Tiberius, an official under Aretas controlled Damascus and sought to arrest Paul, who escaped the city by being lowered over the wall in a basket (2 Cor. 11:32-33; Acts 9:24-25). Aretas IV is well attested in Nabataean inscriptions and coinage found throughout the former Nabataean kingdom.

witness.excerpt: Aretas also, the king of Arabia Petrea, out of his hatred to Herod, and in order to purchase the favor of the Romans, sent him no small assistance, besides their footmen and horsemen; and when he had now collected all his forc
The Arabian king [Aretas] at first retreated, but afterward appeared on the sudden with ten thousand horsemen.

And when he was sent to Aretas, as an ambassador by Scaurus, because he had lived with him formerly, he persuaded Aretas to give Scaurus a sum of money, to prevent the burning of his country, and undertook to be his surety for three hundred talents.

Sylleus was also accused by Aretas, that without his consent he had slain many of the chief of the Arabians at Petra; and particularly Soemus, a man that deserved to be honored by all men; and that he had slain Fabatus, a servant of Caesar.

entries.title: Argob
entries.summary: A region of Bashan known for its sixty fortified cities, taken when Israel beat King Og.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Argob was a region in Bashan known for its sixty fortified cities, conquered by Israel when they defeated King Og.

entries.title: Argob (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 2 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Aridai (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Haman had ten sons, and he was one. The Jews of Susa killed them when they defended themselves against the slaughter Haman had planned. Nothing else is recorded of him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of the ten sons of Haman killed by the Jews of Susa when they defended themselves against the pogrom Haman had planned, an event the book of Esther says gave rise to the feast of Purim (Esther 9:7-10). Nothing else is recorded of him individually.

entries.title: Aridatha (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Another of Haman's ten sons, killed with his brothers on the day Haman had set for destroying the Jews, and his body was hanged afterwards.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Aridatha was one of the ten sons of Haman, the Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews of the empire under King Ahasuerus. He was killed along with his brothers when the Jews defended themselves on the day Haman had set for their destruction, and his body was later hanged (Esther 9:8-10).

entries.title: Arieh (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He died with King Pekahiah of Israel when the officer Pekah murdered the king in the citadel of the palace at Samaria. He and Argob are named only as victims of the coup.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of the men killed with King Pekahiah of Israel when his officer Pekah assassinated him in the citadel of the royal palace at Samaria (2 Kings 15:25). He and Argob are named only as fellow victims of the coup, otherwise unknown.

entries.title: Ariel (Jerusalem)
entries.summary: Isaiah's poetic name for Jerusalem, probably lion of God or altar hearth, in a prophecy of the city under siege and judged. A man called Ariel also turns up in Ezra 8:16.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ariel is a poetic name Isaiah uses for Jerusalem, likely meaning lion of God or altar hearth, used in a prophecy describing the city under siege and God's judgment on it.

witness.excerpt: These had with them, Gad seven - Saphoniah, Augis, Sunis, Azabon, Aerin, Erocd, Ariel.

entries.title: Ariel (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A man from the exile and the return. Ezra names him once.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Arimathaea (Mizpah)
entries.summary: Joseph's town. He was the rich, secret disciple who asked Pilate for Jesus' body and laid it in his own new tomb, and all four Gospels name him by this place. Where it was is uncertain, and many scholars put it at Ramathaim-zophim, a few miles northwest of Jerusalem.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Arimathaea was the hometown of Joseph, the wealthy and secret disciple of Jesus who requested Jesus' body from Pilate after the crucifixion and buried it in his own new tomb (Matthew 27:57-60; John 19:38). All four Gospels identify Joseph by this town, though its precise location is uncertain; many scholars have proposed identifying it with Ramathaim-zophim, the hometown of the prophet Samuel a few miles northwest of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Arioch (King living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Genesis names him twice, and he is a king from the patriarchs.
entries.label: 1 book

witness.excerpt: And in this year came Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, and Amraphel, king of Shinar, and Arioch, king of Sêllâsar  and Têrgâl,  king of nations, and slew the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Sodom fled, and many fell through wounds in the vale of Siddim, by the Salt Sea.

entries.title: Arioch (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: The captain of Nebuchadnezzar's guard, sent to kill Babylon's wise men, and the man Daniel talked into giving him time.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Arioch was a king of Elam who joined a coalition of eastern kings that raided Sodom and captured Lot, a raid Abraham personally reversed by rescuing Lot and recovering the stolen goods.

witness.excerpt: Yet did they persuade Arioch, who was thus fearful, to give them what food they desired for ten days, by way of trial: and in case the habit of their bodies were not altered, to go on in the same way: as expecting that they should not be hurt there

entries.title: Arisai (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One more of the ten sons of Haman the Agagite, killed with his brothers in Esther 9 and named only in that list.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of the ten sons of Haman the Agagite, killed by the Jews of Susa along with his brothers during the events of Esther 9. His name appears only in the list of Haman's sons impaled after Purim (Esther 9:6-10), with nothing else recorded about him.

entries.title: Aristarchus (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: A Macedonian who travelled with Paul. He was dragged into the riot at Ephesus, sailed with Paul to Rome, and was imprisoned with him there.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Aristarchus was a Macedonian companion of Paul who was swept up in a riot at Ephesus, later traveled with Paul to Rome, and shared imprisonment with him there, described by Paul as a fellow prisoner.

entries.title: Aristobulus (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Paul greets his household and not the man himself, who may have died or may not have believed. Some think he was a grandson of Herod the Great known from Josephus to have lived in Rome, but that cannot be confirmed.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Roman, or possibly a Jewish notable, whose household Paul greets in Romans 16:10 rather than Aristobulus himself, who may have already died or simply not been a believer while his household was. Some have speculated he was a grandson of Herod the Great known from Josephus to have lived in Rome, but the identification cannot be confirmed.

witness.excerpt:
Aristobulus was the second that did so, and took that dignity from his brother [Hyrcanus]; and this Herod was the third, who took that high office away [from Arianflus], and gave it to this young man, Aristobulus, in his stead.
2.
To Aristobulus he gave for a wife Bernice, Salome's daughter; and to Alexander, Glaphyra, the daughter of Archelaus, king of Cappadocia.
And Aristobulus is styled παιδίον παντάπασιν, a very little child , at 16 years of age: Antiq.
NOW Aristobulus ran away from Rome to Judea, and set about the rebuilding of Alexandrium, which had been newly demolished.

entries.title: Arkite (People, perhaps from Arak)
entries.summary: Descendants of Canaan who lived at Arka, about twelve miles northeast of Tripoli in modern Lebanon. The site is Tell Arqa, and it appears as Irqata in the Amarna letters.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Arkites descended from Canaan and inhabited Arka, a city about twelve miles northeast of Tripoli in modern Lebanon, opposite the northern end of the Lebanon range. The site, known today as Tell Arqa, has been excavated and appears as Irqata in the Amarna letters and in earlier Egyptian execration texts, confirming it as a real Bronze Age city.

entries.title: Armageddon (Megiddo)
entries.summary: Only Revelation 16:16 uses it, for the place the kings of the earth gather for the last battle against God. The name comes from Har-Megiddo, mount of Megiddo, the plain where Deborah and Barak beat Sisera and Josiah died fighting Pharaoh Necho.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Armageddon appears only in Revelation 16:16, where it names the place where the kings of the earth are gathered for the final battle against God. The name derives from the Hebrew Har-Megiddo, "mount of Megiddo," recalling the strategic plain of Megiddo where Israel fought several of its most decisive battles, including Deborah and Barak's victory over Sisera and Josiah's death in battle against Pharaoh Necho. Excavations at Tel Megiddo have uncovered more than twenty superimposed layers of settlement spanning millennia, confirming the site's long history as a military crossroads controlling the pass between the coastal plain and the Jezreel Valley.

entries.title: Armoni (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Saul's son by his concubine Rizpah. David handed him and his brother Mephibosheth to the Gibeonites, who executed them for Saul's slaughter of Gibeonites in breach of the old treaty. Rizpah guarded the bodies from scavenging animals until David gave the dead a proper burial.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of two sons of Saul by his concubine Rizpah, handed over by David to the Gibeonites and executed to atone for Saul's earlier slaughter of Gibeonites in violation of Israel's ancient treaty with them (2 Sam. 21:1-9). Rizpah's subsequent vigil guarding his exposed body, and that of his brother Mephibosheth, from scavenging animals became one of the Old Testament's most striking images of grief and finally moved David to give the dead a proper burial.

entries.title: Arnan (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One more name in Zerubbabel's line after the exile, at 1 Chronicles 3:21. Nothing further is recorded about him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Listed in the genealogy of Zerubbabel's descendants in 1 Chronicles 3:21, continuing the royal line of Judah after the exile. Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Arnon
entries.summary: A swift river running into the Dead Sea from the east, the line between Amorite and later Moabite land and Israel's tribes beyond the Jordan. Its gorge still carries water in the Wadi al-Mujib. King Mesha of Moab's inscription, the Moabite Stone, boasts of building a highway across it.
entries.books: Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, 2 Kings, Isaiah, Jeremiah
entries.label: 7 books
entries.dictNote: The Arnon was a swift river flowing into the Dead Sea from the east, marking the boundary between Amorite, and later Moabite, territory and Israel's tribal lands beyond the Jordan. Its steep gorge, about seventy miles long from its source in Gilead's mountains, still carries water in the modern Wadi al-Mujib. The Moabite Stone, an inscription set up by King Mesha of Moab in the ninth century BC, describes building a highway across the Arnon valley, corroborating the river's role as a real strategic boundary rather than a merely symbolic one.

witness.excerpt: The people mourned for Aaron thirty days: and when this mourning was over, Moses removed the army from that place, and came to the river Arnon: which issuing out of the mountains of Arabia, and running through all that wilderness fell into the lake Asphaltitis; and became the limit between the land of the Moabites, and the land of the Amorites.
Because fire has gone forth out of Heshbon, and a flame out of the city of Sihon, and has devoured as far as Moab, and has consumed the high places of Arnon.

entries.title: Arod (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: A son of Gad, ancestor of the Arodite clan in the census of Numbers 26:17. Genesis 46:16 calls him Arodi.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A son of Gad and ancestor of the Arodite clan, listed in the wilderness census of Numbers 26:17; he is called Arodi in the earlier genealogical list of Genesis 46:16.

entries.title: Arodi (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Arod again, under the spelling Genesis uses: Gad's son, founder of the Arodite clan, and one of the seventy who went down to Egypt with Jacob.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Arodi, also called Arod, was a son of Gad and the founder of the Arodite clan, listed among the seventy who went down to Egypt with Jacob (Genesis 46:16; Numbers 26:17).

witness.excerpt: And these are the names of their sons who went with him into Egypt: the sons of Gad: Ziphion, and Haggi, and Shuni, and Ezbon, (and Eri) and Areli, and Arodi--eight.

entries.title: Aroer
entries.summary: A border town on the edge of Moabite and Ammonite territory. It marked the southern limit of the land Israel took east of the Jordan.
entries.label: 5 books
entries.dictNote: Aroer was a border town on the edge of Moabite and Ammonite territory, marking the southern limit of the tribal lands Israel took east of the Jordan.

entries.title: Aroer
entries.summary: A second town of the name, in Numbers 32:34 and Joshua 13:25, on the same border between Israel's lands east of the Jordan and Ammonite territory.
entries.books: Numbers, Joshua, Judges, 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, Isaiah
entries.label: 6 books

entries.title: Aroer
entries.summary: 1 Samuel names him once, and nothing else is recorded.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Aroerite
entries.summary: Hothan, father of two of David's mighty men, Shama and Jehiel, came from Aroer. Most likely that means the town on the Arnon gorge rather than the one near Beersheba.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Aroerite marks Hothan, father of two of David's mighty men, Shama and Jehiel, as a native of Aroer, most likely the town on the Arnon gorge in Transjordan rather than the similarly named site near Beersheba.

entries.title: Arpad
entries.summary: A Syrian city near Hamath. Assyrian kings kept naming it to show what they could conquer, and it fell to Tiglath-pileser III after a long siege around 740 BC. Its ruins are at Tell Rifaat, north of Aleppo.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Arpad was a Syrian city near Hamath that Assyrian kings repeatedly cite as proof of their conquering power (2 Kings 18:34; 19:13; Isaiah 10:9; 36:19; 37:13); it fell to Tiglath-pileser III after a lengthy siege around 740 BC, an event confirmed in Assyrian royal annals. Jeremiah later pairs it with Damascus and Hamath in his oracle against Syria (Jeremiah 49:23), and its ruins are identified with Tell Rifaat north of Aleppo.

entries.title: Arphaxad (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Shem's son, born two years after the flood. Genesis runs his descendants down through several generations to Abraham, so he is the link between Noah and the patriarchs.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Arphaxad was a son of Shem born two years after the flood, and Genesis traces his descendants forward through several generations to Abraham, making him a key link in the genealogy connecting Noah to the patriarchs.

witness.excerpt: Arphaxad named the Arphaxadites, who are now called Chaldeans.

entries.title: Artaxerxes
entries.summary: He funded Ezra's return to Jerusalem with the temple articles and orders to teach the law, and later sent Nehemiah to rebuild the city's walls. A Persian king backing Judah's restoration.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Artaxerxes was a Persian king who authorized and funded both Ezra's return to Jerusalem with temple articles and instructions to teach the law, and later Nehemiah's mission to rebuild the city's walls, making him a decisive supporter of Judah's postexilic restoration despite being a foreign emperor.

witness.excerpt:
And how, in the reign of Artaxerxes, the whole nation of the Jews was in danger of perishing.

1.

On whose account it was also that Bagoses, the general of another Artaxerxes’s army, polluted the temple, and imposed tributes on the Jews; that out of the publick stock, before they offered the daily sacrifices, they should pay for every lamb fifty shekels.

entries.title: Artemas (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Paul thought of sending him to Crete to take over from Titus. Later church tradition makes him bishop of Lystra, though the New Testament does not say so.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Artemas was a companion of Paul whom the apostle considered sending to Crete to relieve Titus (Titus 3:12). Later church tradition names him bishop of Lystra, though this cannot be confirmed from the New Testament itself.

entries.title: Aruboth (Arubboth)
entries.summary: Ben-hesed's district, one of the twelve that each fed Solomon's court for a month a year. It took in Socoh and seems to have lain in the grain country of Judah's Shephelah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Aruboth was the district assigned to Ben-hesed, one of the twelve officials responsible for supplying provisions to Solomon's court one month each year (1 Kings 4:10). It included the town of Socoh and apparently lay in the fertile grain-growing lowlands of Judah's Shephelah.

entries.title: Arvad
entries.summary: Arwad today, a small fortified island city off the Syrian coast. Ezekiel says Tyre hired its sailors and soldiers. It was founded by Phoenician settlers and is in the Amarna letters already, with its own fleet.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Arvad, modern Arwad, was a small fortified island city off the Syrian coast whose sailors and soldiers Tyre hired as mercenaries and mariners according to Ezekiel's oracle against that city (Ezekiel 27:8, 11). Founded by Phoenician settlers early in the second millennium BC, Arvad ran its own fleet and local dynasty and appears already in the fourteenth-century BC Amarna letters, where its ships figure in the political struggles among the Levantine coastal cities.

entries.title: Arvadite (People, perhaps from Arvad)
entries.summary: The people of Arvad, an island city off the Phoenician coast now called Arwad, descended from Canaan. Assyrian records show it paying tribute to Tiglath-Pileser III and Sennacherib.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Arvadites were descendants of Canaan associated with Arvad, a fortified island city off the Phoenician coast, known today as Arwad in Syria. Ezekiel names Arvad's men as skilled mariners and soldiers hired by Tyre, and Assyrian records from Tiglath-Pileser III and Sennacherib confirm Arvad as a real Phoenician city-state that paid tribute to Assyria.

entries.title: Arza (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Steward of the palace at Tirzah. King Elah was drunk in Arza's house when his officer Zimri killed him and took the throne.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: The steward in charge of the royal palace at Tirzah under King Elah of Israel. Elah was assassinated in Arza's house during a drinking bout by his own officer Zimri, who then seized the throne (1 Kings 16:9).

entries.title: Asa (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: King of Judah for forty-one years, and a real reformer. He removed his own grandmother as queen mother over an obscene idol and drove the male shrine prostitutes out. Early on he trusted God against a huge Cushite invasion, but late in life he hired a foreign king against northern Israel instead.
entries.label: 5 books
entries.dictNote: Asa was king of Judah for forty-one years and one of the kingdom's genuine reformers, removing his own grandmother from her position as queen mother for making an obscene idol and expelling male shrine prostitutes from the land. Early in his reign he trusted God for a decisive victory over a massive Cushite invasion, but late in life, facing a threat from northern Israel, he hired a foreign king to attack Israel instead of trusting God as he once had, and a prophet's rebuke of that decision made Asa angry enough to throw the prophet in prison.

entries.title: Asa (Levite living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a Levite from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Asahel (David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Joab's younger brother, one of David's best warriors and famous for his speed. He died chasing Abner in the fighting between David's side and Saul's. Joab later murdered Abner for it, and that killing hung over David's reign.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Asahel was Joab's younger brother and one of David's elite warriors, known for his speed, and he died chasing down Abner during a battle between David's and Saul's rival factions, a death Joab later avenged by murdering Abner, an act that haunted David's reign afterward.

witness.excerpt: He had with him his brethren, Abistiai and Asahel, as also all David's armed men.

But as to that former wicked action, the death of his brother Asahel, which he seemed to revenge, afforded him a decent pretense, and made that crime a pardonable one; but in this murder of Amasa there was no such covering for it.

entries.title: Asahel (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Asahel (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 4 men called Asahel. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Asahel (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A man from the exile and the return, and Ezra is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Asaiah (Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A levite from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Asaiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of the officials Josiah sent to consult the prophetess Huldah.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Asaiah was a common name, borne by a royal official Josiah sent to consult the prophetess Huldah and by a Levite involved in bringing the ark to Jerusalem under David.

entries.title: Asaiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him twice, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Asaiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 5 men called Asaiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Asaiah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A man from the exile and the return. 1 Chronicles names him once.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Asaph (Levite living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of 4 men called Asaph. This one is a Levite from the exile and the return, named twice in 1 Chronicles and Nehemiah.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Asaph (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Not David's singer. This Asaph is the one in 2 Kings 18:18 and Isaiah 36:3, and nothing else about him is recorded here.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Asaph (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A man from the exile and the return, and Nehemiah is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Asaph (Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Levite David put in charge of one of the temple choirs. Twelve psalms carry his name, Psalm 50 and Psalms 73 to 83, which means either he wrote them or a guild of musicians kept his name for generations.
entries.label: 5 books
entries.dictNote: Asaph was a Levite David appointed to lead one of the temple's choirs and musical guilds, and his name is attached to twelve psalms, including Psalm 50 and the run from Psalm 73 through 83, suggesting either his personal authorship or a musical guild that continued under his name for generations after him.

witness.excerpt: And when the temple was finished, the priests, adorned with their accustomed garments, stood with their trumpets; while the Levites, and the sons of Asaph, stood, and sang hymns to God, according as David had first of all appointed them to bless God.

entries.title: Asareel (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Jehaleleel's son, in Judah's genealogies.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Asareel was a son of Jehaleleel listed in the genealogies of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:16).

entries.title: Asarelah (Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of Asaph's sons whom David appointed to prophesy with harp and cymbals. Later in the same chapter he is Jesharelah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Asarelah was one of the sons of Asaph whom David appointed to prophesy with the harp and cymbals in temple worship; he is called Jesharelah later in the same chapter (1 Chr. 25:2, 14).

entries.title: Asenath (Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Pharaoh gave her to Joseph as his wife. She was the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, and she bore him Manasseh and Ephraim, the ancestors of two tribes of Israel.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Asenath was an Egyptian woman, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On (Heliopolis), whom Pharaoh gave to Joseph as his wife (Genesis 41:45). She bore Joseph two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, who became the ancestors of two of Israel's twelve tribes (Genesis 41:50-52; 46:20). Her marriage into an Egyptian priestly family reflects Joseph's full integration into Egyptian court life during his rise to power under Pharaoh.

witness.excerpt: 3 And carry ye up Asenath your mother to the Hippodrome, and near Rachel your mother bury her.
And there were born to Joseph in Egypt before his father came into Egypt, those whom Asenath, daughter of Potiphar priest of Heliopolis bare unto him, Manasseh, and Ephraim--three.
He also married a wife of very high quality; for he married the daughter of Petephres, (4) one of the priests of Heliopolis; she was a virgin, and her name was Asenath.

entries.title: Aser (Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: The Greek form of Asher, Jacob's eighth son. Luke uses it for the tribe of the prophetess Anna, and Revelation 7:6 lists it among the sealed tribes.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Aser is the Greek New Testament form of Asher, Jacob's eighth son and ancestor of the tribe of Asher. The name appears identifying the prophetess Anna's tribal descent (Luke 2:36) and among the twelve tribes listed as sealed in Revelation 7:6.

witness.excerpt: Gad and Aser were the sons of Zilpha, who was the handmaid of Lea.
The tribe of Aser had that part which was called the Valley ; for such it was: and all that part which lay over against Sidon.

entries.title: Ashan
entries.summary: A small town in Judah's lowlands, later handed to Simeon, whose share lay inside Judah. Aaron's line of Levites got it as a priestly city. Nobody has found the site.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ashan was a small town in the lowlands of Judah that was later reassigned to Simeon, whose inheritance lay within Judah's larger territory (Joshua 15:42; 19:7). It was given to the Levites of Aaron's line as one of their priestly cities (1 Chronicles 6:59). Its exact site has not been identified.

entries.title: Ashbea
entries.summary: "The house of Ashbea" is all Chronicles gives: the source of a family of linen workers in Judah. Whether that means a man or the place his descendants lived is not clear from the text.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A name in the genealogy of Judah that Chronicles itself leaves ambiguous, "the house of Ashbea," identified only as the ancestor or founding location of a family of linen workers (1 Chr. 4:21). Whether Ashbea names an individual or the place his descendants settled is not clear from the text.

entries.title: Ashbel (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Benjamin's son, and his descendants made one of the clans of the tribe.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Ashbel was a son of Benjamin, and his descendants formed one of the clans counted among Benjamin's tribe.

witness.excerpt: And the sons of Benjamin: Bela and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, and Ehi, and Rosh, and Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard--eleven.

entries.title: Ashbelites (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Counted in the Numbers 26 census, the clan that came from Ashbel, Benjamin's son.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ashbelites were the clan descended from Ashbel, a son of Benjamin, counted in the Numbers 26 census.

entries.title: Ashdod
entries.summary: Ashdod spelled another way, one of the five chief Philistine cities, on the coast between Ekron and Gaza. The captured ark was put in its temple of Dagon, and the affliction started there.
entries.books: Joshua, 1 Samuel, 2 Chronicles, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Amos, Zephaniah, Zechariah
entries.label: 8 books
entries.dictNote: Ahdod is an alternate transliteration of Ashdod, one of the five chief Philistine cities, located on the coastal plain between Ekron and Gaza and home to a temple of Dagon where the captured ark was placed before it caused affliction among the Philistines.

entries.title: Ashdoth-pisgah
entries.summary: The slopes of Pisgah, east of the Jordan, in land taken from Sihon the Amorite. It is likely a description of the ridge rather than a place name, the same ridge Moses looked at the promised land from before he died.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ashdoth-pisgah, rendered "the slopes of Pisgah" in most modern translations, describes the descending ridges of Mount Pisgah on the eastern side of the Jordan, within territory taken from Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy 3:17; Joshua 12:3; 13:20). It is likely not a separate place name at all but a geographic description of Pisgah's terrain, the same ridge from which Moses viewed the promised land before his death (Deuteronomy 34:1). It has been associated with springs near Mount Nebo still known today as Ayun Musa, "the springs of Moses."

entries.title: Asher (Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Jacob's eighth son, by Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe got a fertile coastal strip in the north, running toward Phoenicia, some of the richest land in Israel. Beyond its borders and city list little of the tribe's own history is recorded, and like Simeon it produced no judge or great hero.
entries.books: Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, 1 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Ezekiel
entries.label: 10 books
entries.dictNote: Asher was Jacob's eighth son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah, and the tribe descended from him received a fertile coastal strip in northern Canaan running toward Phoenicia, described in Joshua as containing some of the richest land in Israel. Little is recorded of the tribe's individual history beyond its territorial boundaries and city list, and along with Simeon it produced no judge or major hero in the biblical narrative. Anna the prophetess, who recognized the infant Jesus in the temple, is identified in Luke as being of the tribe of Asher.

entries.title: Asherites (Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: The tribe of Asher. Judges 1:32 says they never drove out the Canaanites of their coastal land and settled down among them instead.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Asherites are the members of the tribe of Asher, descended from Jacob's eighth son by Zilpah. Judges 1:32 reports that Asher failed to drive out the Canaanite inhabitants of its allotted coastal territory and instead settled among them, a pattern of partial conquest repeated by several tribes in that chapter.

entries.title: Ashima (A male deity in the Old Testament)
entries.summary: A god, not a person: the god of the people of Hamath, whom the Assyrians resettled in Samaria after deporting the northern kingdom. Little is known of the cult beyond this one notice.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ashima is not a person but a deity, the god of the people of Hamath whom the Assyrians resettled in Samaria after deporting the northern kingdom's population (2 Kings 17:30). Little is known of the cult beyond this notice; some scholars connect the name to "Ashim-Bethel," a divine name that turns up centuries later among Aramaic-speaking Jews at Elephantine in Egypt.

entries.title: Ashkelon
entries.summary: One of the five main Philistine cities, a port on the coast midway between Gaza and Joppa. Samson killed thirty of its men there to pay off a wager. It is named on the Merneptah Stele, an Egyptian inscription from around 1208 BC.
entries.books: Judges, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, Jeremiah, Amos, Zephaniah, Zechariah
entries.label: 7 books
entries.dictNote: Ashkelon was one of the five principal Philistine cities, a coastal port midway between Gaza and Joppa that Judah briefly captured after the conquest before the Philistines retook it. Samson killed thirty of its men there to pay off a wager, and the prophets repeatedly singled it out for judgment. Ashkelon appears by name in the Merneptah Stele, an Egyptian inscription from around 1208 BC boasting of its conquest, one of the earliest extrabiblical references to a place named in the Bible; the same inscription contains the earliest known mention of Israel.

entries.title: Ashkenaz
entries.summary: Named once, in Jeremiah, and nowhere else.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ashkenaz (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Gomer's son and Japheth's grandson. Jeremiah later calls on a kingdom of Ashkenaz, with Ararat and Minni, to join in the destruction of Babylon.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ashkenaz was a son of Gomer and grandson of Japheth, and Jeremiah calls on the kingdom of Ashkenaz, along with Ararat and Minni, to join in Babylon's coming destruction.

entries.title: Ashnah
entries.summary: Two towns in Judah's lowland share the name. One sat near Zorah and Eshtaol, the other near Nezib and Keilah, and neither site is certain today.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ashnah is the name of two towns in the lowland (Shephelah) territory of Judah, not a person. One is listed near Zorah and Eshtaol (Joshua 15:33), and the other appears later in the same tribal boundary list near Nezib and Keilah (Joshua 15:43). Their exact sites are uncertain today.

entries.title: Ashpenaz (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: He ran Nebuchadnezzar's court eunuchs and picked out young Judean nobles to train for royal service in Babylon, Daniel and his three companions among them.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Chief official over Nebuchadnezzar's court eunuchs, responsible for selecting and training young Judean nobles, including Daniel and his three companions, for royal service in Babylon (Daniel 1:3).

witness.excerpt: So he came to Ashpenaz who was that eunuch  to whom the care of them was committed and desired him to take and spend what was brought for them from the King; but to give them pulse and dates for their food, and any thing else, besides the fle

entries.title: Ashriel (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Asriel, from Manasseh. His family made one of the tribe's clans.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Asriel was a descendant of Manasseh, and his family formed one of the clans counted among Manasseh's tribe in Israel's genealogies.

entries.title: Ashriel (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ashtaroth
entries.summary: Ashtaroth under another spelling, the fortified capital of Og, king of Bashan, east of the Jordan. It went to the half-tribe of Manasseh and then to the Levites of Gershon. The name comes from the goddess Ashtoreth, and the site is generally put at Tell Ashtarah in the Golan.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: The spelling here is a variant of Ashtaroth, the fortified capital of Og, king of Bashan, east of the Jordan (Deuteronomy 1:4; Joshua 12:4; 13:12). It was assigned to the half-tribe of Manasseh and later given to the Levites of Gershon; its name comes from Ashtoreth, the Canaanite goddess whose worship was centered there, and archaeologists generally locate it at Tell Ashtarah in the Golan region of modern Syria.

entries.title: Ashterathite (Ashtaroth)
entries.summary: Uzzia, one of David's mighty men, came from Ashtaroth, the Bashan city that had been the capital of Og's Amorite kingdom.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ashterathite marks Uzzia, one of David's mighty men, as a native of Ashtaroth, the Bashan city east of the Jordan that had once been the capital of Og's Amorite kingdom before Israel's conquest.

entries.title: Ashtoreth (A female deity in the Old Testament)
entries.summary: A Canaanite and Phoenician goddess of fertility and war, closely tied to Baal worship. Solomon built her a shrine late in his reign to please a foreign wife, and that is given as a main reason the kingdom split.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Ashtoreth was a Canaanite and Phoenician goddess of fertility and war, closely associated with Baal worship, and Solomon's construction of a shrine to her late in his reign, to please one of his foreign wives, is cited as a major reason for the kingdom's later division.

entries.title: Ashtoreth Karnaim (Ashteroth-karnaim)
entries.summary: Ashtoreth of the two horns, a city in Bashan east of the Jordan. A branch of the Rephaim lived there until Chedorlaomer's coalition beat them. It is generally identified with Tell Ashtarah in the Golan.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A city in Bashan, east of the Jordan, home to a branch of the Rephaim who were defeated by the coalition of eastern kings under Chedorlaomer in Genesis 14:5. The compound name, "Ashtoreth of the two horns," ties the town to the worship of the goddess Ashtoreth (Astarte), likely under a horned or crescent-moon symbol. It is generally identified with Tell Ashtarah in the Golan region of modern Syria.

entries.title: Ashur (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Hezron's son, born after his father died. Chronicles remembers him as the founder of Tekoa, the town Amos later came from.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ashur was a son of Hezron born after his father's death, remembered in Chronicles as the founder of Tekoa (1 Chronicles 2:24; 4:5), the town later home to the prophet Amos.

witness.excerpt: Ashur lived at the city Nineve; and named his subjects Assyrians: who became the most fortunate nation, beyond others.

entries.title: Ashvath (Man living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: Japhlet's son, in Asher's line.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Son of Japhlet, of the tribe of Asher, included in the genealogical record of Asher's descendants (1 Chronicles 7:33).

entries.title: Asia
entries.summary: Not the continent. The Roman province of Asia, in western Asia Minor, with Ephesus among its churches, and the region the seven churches of Revelation belonged to.
entries.books: Acts, Romans, 1 Corinthians, 2 Corinthians, 2 Timothy, 1 Peter, Revelation
entries.label: 7 books
entries.dictNote: Asia in the New Testament refers not to the continent but to the Roman province of Asia in western Asia Minor, home to major early churches including Ephesus, and it's the region addressed by the seven churches in the book of Revelation.

witness.excerpt: Wherefore there are but two tribes in Asia and Europe, subject to the Romans: while the ten tribes are beyond Euphrates till now; and are an immense multitude, and not to be estimated by numbers.

Now the cities ill-treated the Jews in Asia, and all those also of the same nation which lived ill Libya, which joins to Cyrene, while the former kings had given them equal privileges with the other citizens; but the Greeks affronted them at this time, and that s
