entries.title: Bani (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 10 men called Bani. This one is a warrior from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Samuel.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Baptist
entries.summary: John, son of the priest Zechariah and Elizabeth. He was born to elderly parents after an angel said he would be. He preached in the wilderness.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: John the Baptist was a wilderness preacher, the son of the priest Zechariah and Elizabeth, born to elderly parents after an angel announced his birth in the Jerusalem temple. He preached repentance and baptized in the Jordan River, and it was John who baptized Jesus and publicly identified him as the one Israel had been waiting for. Herod Antipas had John arrested and eventually beheaded after John condemned his marriage to his brother's wife, a death carried out, according to the Gospels, as a birthday party favor to Herod's stepdaughter.

witness.excerpt: The Recognitions assuring us that they began about the days of John the Baptist, I.54 .

entries.title: Bar-jona (Apostle living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Son of Jonah. Jesus calls Simon Peter this right after Peter says Jesus is the Christ, and it names Peter's father as a man called Jonah or John.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Bar-jona, meaning "son of Jonah," is the patronymic Jesus used to address Simon Peter after Peter's confession that Jesus was the Christ (Matthew 16:17). It identifies Peter's father as a man named Jonah or John (compare John 1:42; 21:15-17).

entries.title: Barabbas (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Held for insurrection and murder. Under a Passover custom Pilate offered the crowd one prisoner, Barabbas or Jesus. They chose Barabbas, and Jesus was crucified.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Barabbas was a prisoner held for insurrection and murder, and Pilate offered the crowd a choice between releasing him or Jesus as part of a Passover custom of pardoning one prisoner; the crowd chose Barabbas, and Jesus was crucified in his place.

entries.title: Barachel (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Barachel the Buzite was Elihu's father, and Elihu was the youngest of those who spoke to Job.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Barachel was a Buzite, the father of Elihu, the youngest of the friends who spoke to Job (Job 32:2, 6).

entries.title: Barachias (High Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Matthew 23:35 names him as father of the Zacharias murdered between the temple and the altar. The wording fits Zechariah the priest stoned in the temple court under King Joash.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Barachias is named in Matthew 23:35 as the father of the Zacharias whom Jesus says was murdered between the temple and the altar. The wording most closely matches Zechariah the priest stoned in the temple court under King Joash, whose father was actually named Jehoiada (2 Chronicles 24:20-22), so some see this as an added or confused patronymic, possibly conflating him with the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah (Zechariah 1:1).

entries.title: Barak (Judge living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: He led Israel against Sisera, the Canaanite general, because Deborah told him to, and he would not go unless she came with him. That hesitation cost him the glory of the win.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Barak was the military commander Deborah summoned to lead Israel's forces against the Canaanite general Sisera, and he refused to go into battle unless Deborah came with him, a hesitation that cost him the personal glory of the coming victory, since Deborah told him credit would go to a woman instead. That woman turned out to be Jael, who killed the fleeing Sisera in her own tent.

witness.excerpt: 1314.] Now when Barak and Deborah were dead; whose deaths happened about the same time; afterwards the Midianites called the Amalekites and Arabians to their assistance, and made war against the Israelites, and were too hard for those that f
After which they were delivered by Barak and Deborah ; who ruled over them for forty years.

entries.title: Barhumite (Bahurim)
entries.summary: The spelling 2 Samuel 23:31 uses for a man from Bahurim, a Benjaminite village near Jerusalem. It marks Azmaveth, one of David's mighty men, and Chronicles has Baharumite.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Barhumite marks Azmaveth, one of David's mighty men, as a native of Bahurim, a Benjaminite village near Jerusalem. The parallel list in 1 Chronicles 11:33 gives the same man's home town as Baharumite, an alternate spelling of the same name.

entries.title: Bariah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of five sons of Shemaiah, in the line of David after the exile. Nothing further is known of him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Bariah was one of five sons of Shemaiah, listed within the postexilic royal line of David in 1 Chronicles 3:22. Nothing further is known of him.

entries.title: Barjesus (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: A Jewish false prophet and magician who had attached himself to Sergius Paulus, the Roman proconsul of Cyprus. He also went by Elymas. He tried to turn the proconsul away from the faith and was struck blind for it.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Bar-Jesus was a Jewish false prophet and magician attached to the court of Sergius Paulus, the Roman proconsul of Cyprus (Acts 13:6). He is also called Elymas, sought to turn the proconsul away from the faith, and was struck blind by Paul for opposing the gospel, after which Sergius Paulus believed. His name means son of Jesus, an ironic title for a man Paul denounced as a son of the devil.

entries.title: Barkos (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: His family were temple servants, Nethinim, who came back from Babylonian exile but could not prove their Israelite descent from the records.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Barkos was the ancestor of a family of temple servants, or Nethinim, who returned from Babylonian exile, listed among those unable to prove their Israelite lineage through genealogical records (Ezra 2:53; Nehemiah 7:55).

entries.title: Barnabas (Levite living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Joseph was his given name. He was a Levite from Cyprus. The apostles called him Barnabas, son of encouragement, after he sold a field and gave the money to the Jerusalem church.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Barnabas was a Levite from Cyprus whose given name was Joseph, and the apostles nicknamed him Barnabas, meaning son of encouragement, after he sold a field and gave the money to the Jerusalem church. He was the one who vouched for the newly converted Saul when the other believers still feared him as a persecutor, and he later recruited Saul to help lead the church at Antioch and traveled with him on the first missionary journey. Barnabas and Paul eventually split over whether to bring Barnabas's cousin John Mark on a second journey, a sharp enough disagreement that they went separate ways afterward.

witness.excerpt: In the mean time, it is not to be doubted, but in their education they must have both learned more Jewish interpretations; such I mean as we meet with in the epistle of Barnabas , in that to the Hebrews, and elsewhere among the old Jews.

entries.title: Barsabas (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Son of Sabas, a surname two men carry in Acts. This one is Joseph, also called Justus, one of the two put forward to take Judas's place among the twelve.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Barsabas (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: A surname, son of Sabas. This is Judas Barsabas, sent with Silas to carry the council's letter to Antioch.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Barsabas, meaning son of Sabas, was a surname carried by two different men in Acts. Joseph Barsabas, also called Justus, was one of the two candidates put forward to replace Judas among the twelve apostles (Acts 1:23). Judas Barsabas was a prophet in the Jerusalem church sent along with Paul and Silas to deliver the council's letter to the believers in Antioch (Acts 15:22, 32). The two are unrelated beyond sharing the same family name.

entries.title: Bartholomeus (Apostle living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: One of the twelve. Many take him for Nathanael, since the Synoptic Gospels never mention a Nathanael and John's Gospel never mentions a Bartholomew.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Bartholomew was one of the twelve apostles, and many identify him with Nathanael, since the Synoptic Gospels never mention a Nathanael and John's Gospel never mentions a Bartholomew, and both names are consistently paired with Philip in their respective lists.

entries.title: Bartimaeus (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: A blind beggar at Jericho, the son of Timaeus. He called out to Jesus as Son of David, and the crowd tried to shut him up. He kept calling until Jesus gave him his sight.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Bartimaeus was a blind beggar at Jericho, son of a man named Timaeus, whose sight Jesus restored after Bartimaeus called out to him as Son of David (Mark 10:46-52). His persistence despite the crowd's attempts to silence him is presented as an example of faith. The parallel account in Matthew 20:30 mentions two unnamed blind men, while Luke 18:35 places the healing as Jesus approached rather than left the city.

entries.title: Baruch (Jeremiah's servant living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Jeremiah's scribe and close companion. He wrote the prophecies down as Jeremiah dictated them. King Jehoiakim cut the scroll up and burned it, and Baruch wrote it all out again.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Baruch was Jeremiah's scribe and close companion, personally writing down Jeremiah's dictated prophecies onto a scroll that King Jehoiakim later cut up and burned, and Baruch rewrote it from Jeremiah's dictation with additional material added. He was forced into exile in Egypt along with Jeremiah after Judah's remaining leadership was assassinated. A clay seal impression bearing his name and title, found in Jerusalem, is widely believed to be his own.

witness.excerpt: And as they intended to have Zacharias, the son of Baruch, one of the most eminent of the citizens slain; so what provoked them against him was, that hatred of wickedness, and love of liberty, which were so eminent in him.
And when the rulers heard of it, they took the book from him, and bid him and Baruch the Scribe to go their ways: lest they should be discovered by one or other.

Perhaps the copyists conflated Azarias and Sereus in Ἄζαρος] (22) Of this character of Baruch, the son of Neriah, and the genuineness of his Book, that stands now in our apocrypha; and that it is really a canonical book, and an appendix to Jeremiah, see Authent.

Accordingly Jeremiah abode in a city of that countrey which was called Mispah ; and desired of Nebuzaradan that he would set at liberty his disciple Baruch, the son of Neriah; one of a very eminent family; and exceeding skilful in the language of his countrey.

entries.title: Baruch (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of 4 men called Baruch. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Baruch (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A man from the exile and the return, and Nehemiah is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Baruch (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Barzillai (David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: When David fled from Absalom, this old and wealthy Gileadite fed him and his men. David later offered him a place at court. Barzillai turned it down.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Barzillai was a wealthy and elderly Gileadite who supplied David and his men with provisions during Absalom's rebellion, and David later offered to reward him with a place at the royal court, an honor Barzillai declined due to his advanced age, asking David to take his son instead.

witness.excerpt: These were Barzillai the Gileadite, and Siphar the ruler among the Ammonites, and Machir the principal man of Gilead; and these furnished him with plentiful provisions for himself and his followers, insomuch that they wanted no beds nor bla

But David desired Barzillai the Gileadite, that great and good man, and one that had made a plentiful provision for him at Mahanaim, and had conducted him as far as Jordan, to accompany him to Jerusalem, for he promised to treat him in his old age

I also commit to thee the son of Barzillai the Gileadite, whom, in order to gratify me, thou shalt have in great honor, and take great care of; for we have not done good to him first, but we only repay that debt which we owe to his father for what he did to me i

entries.title: Barzillai (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Bashan
entries.summary: The fertile tableland east of the Jordan, between Gilead and Mount Hermon. Og ruled it, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel beat him and gave the land to half the tribe of Manasseh.
entries.books: Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, Nehemiah, Psalm, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Amos, Micah, Nahum, Zechariah
entries.label: 15 books
entries.dictNote: Bashan was the fertile tableland east of the Jordan between Gilead and Mount Hermon, ruled by Og, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel defeated him and gave the territory to half the tribe of Manasseh. It was famous in the Bible for its oak forests, its rich pastures, and the strong cattle they produced, images the prophets used for pride and excess. After the exile the region was divided into the districts of Gaulanitis, Auranitis, Trachonitis, and Batanaea, names that carried into the New Testament era.

witness.excerpt: Now the cities which were set apart for this flight were these: Bezer , at the borders of Arabia; Ramoth , of the land of Gilead; and Golan , in the land of Bashan.

photo.description: panorama of a plain in Bashan

entries.title: Bashemath (Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: One of Esau's wives, in the Genesis lists. The name belongs to more than one of them, and to a daughter of Solomon too.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Bashemath (Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Another of Esau's wives with this name, the one in the Genesis 36 lists.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Basemath was the name of more than one wife of Esau in Genesis's genealogical lists, and also the name of one of Solomon's daughters.

entries.title: Bashemath (Woman living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 3 women called Bashemath. This one is a woman from the united kingdom, named once in 1 Kings.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Bath-rabbim
entries.summary: A gate of Heshbon with pools near it, where the Song of Solomon finds the beloved's eyes: the fishpools in Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A gate of the Ammonite-bordering city of Heshbon, near which lay pools of water; the Song of Solomon compares the eyes of the beloved to "the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim" (Song of Solomon 7:4). Its exact location within Heshbon is unknown.

entries.title: Bath-sheba (David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: She was Uriah the Hittite's wife. David saw her bathing, sent for her, and got her pregnant while Uriah was away fighting in David's own army. The cover-up ended with Uriah's death in battle, arranged by David.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Bathsheba was the wife of Uriah the Hittite until David saw her bathing, summoned her, and got her pregnant while Uriah was away at war under David's own command. David's cover-up ended with Uriah's engineered death in battle, a sin the prophet Nathan confronted directly with a parable that trapped David into condemning himself, and the child born from the affair died in infancy as part of the judgment. Bathsheba later became the mother of Solomon and intervened at a critical moment near David's death to make sure Solomon, not a rival half-brother, inherited the throne.

entries.title: Bath-shua (David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Daughter of Shua. Chronicles uses the phrase for two different women, and here it names the Canaanite wife of Judah, the mother of Er, Onan and Shelah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Bath-shua, meaning “daughter of Shua,” is used of two different women in Chronicles. It names the Canaanite wife of Judah, mother of Er, Onan, and Shelah, elsewhere called simply “the daughter of Shua” (1 Chronicles 2:3; compare Genesis 38:2). It is also used as a variant of Bathsheba, wife of David and mother of Solomon (1 Chronicles 3:5).

entries.title: Bavai (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: He ruled the district of Keilah and repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah, and he was Henadad's son.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Son of Henadad, Bavai ruled the district of Keilah and helped repair a section of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3:18).

entries.title: Bazlith (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Also spelled Bazluth. His family of temple servants, Nethinim, came back from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel, and nothing further is recorded about him.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Bazlith, also spelled Bazluth, headed a family of Nethinim, temple servants whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:52; Nehemiah 7:54). Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Bealiah (Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He was a Benjamite who went over to David at Ziklag while David was still on the run from Saul. He was one of the skilled warriors who could use bow and sling with either hand.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Bealiah was a Benjamite among the skilled warriors, expert with bow and sling from both hands, who defected to David at Ziklag while he was still an outlaw fleeing Saul (1 Chronicles 12:1-5). His name, meaning "the Lord is my lord," is notable for using the divine name Yahweh rather than Baal despite superficially resembling a Baal-compound name.

entries.title: Bealoth (Baalath-beer)
entries.summary: Down in the far south of Judah, likely the same town as Baalath-beer. Solomon's list of districts also names a region Aloth or Bealoth under one of his twelve governors.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Town in the far south of Judah (Josh. 15:24), likely the same as Baalath-beer (Josh. 19:8). Solomon's list of administrative districts also names a region called Aloth or Bealoth under one of his twelve governors (1 Kings 4:16).

witness.excerpt: And he removed from thence and went towards the south,  and he came to Hebron, and Hebron was built at, that time, and he dwelt there two years, and he went (thence) into the land of the south, to Bealoth  and there was a famine in the land.

entries.title: Bebai (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Head of a family among the returning exiles, and prominent enough to be among those who sealed Nehemiah's covenant renewal.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Bebai was the head of a family among the returning exiles, prominent enough to be listed among those who sealed Nehemiah's covenant renewal.

entries.title: Bebai (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Becher (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Benjamin's son, whose descendants became one of the clans of Benjamin's tribe.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Becher was a son of Benjamin, and his descendants formed one of the clans counted among Benjamin's tribe in Israel's genealogies.

witness.excerpt: And the sons of Benjamin: Bela and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, and Ehi, and Rosh, and Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard--eleven.

entries.title: Becher (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Numbers names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Bechorath (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Saul's family tree runs through him: son of Aphiah, an early forebear of Kish, Saul's father. The genealogy is there to set out Saul's Benjamite pedigree just before he comes on stage.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Bechorath was an ancestor of King Saul, named in the genealogy of 1 Samuel 9:1 as the son of Aphiah and an early forebear of Kish, Saul's father. The genealogy is given to establish Saul's Benjamite pedigree just before his introduction into the narrative. Nothing beyond this genealogical mention is recorded of him.

entries.title: Bedad (Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Hadad's father. Hadad was one of the early kings of Edom, and he beat the Midianites in the territory of Moab. Nothing else is recorded of Bedad.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Bedad was the father of Hadad, one of the early kings of Edom who defeated the Midianites in the territory of Moab (Genesis 36:35; 1 Chronicles 1:46). Nothing else is recorded of him.

entries.title: Bedan (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Samuel names him in his farewell speech among Israel's deliverers, with Jerubbaal, Barak and Jephthah. No judge called Bedan appears in the book of Judges, so who he was is uncertain.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Bedan is named among Israel's deliverers in Samuel's farewell speech, alongside Jerubbaal, Barak, and Jephthah, though his identity is uncertain since no judge by that name appears in the book of Judges; some identify him with Samson or Abdon, or take the name as a variant of Barak (1 Samuel 12:11). A different Bedan, of the tribe of Manasseh, appears in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles 7:17.

entries.title: Bedeiah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of the sons of Bani who had married a foreign wife and agreed to send her away under Ezra's reform, around 458 BC.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Bedeiah was one of the sons of Bani who had married a foreign wife and agreed, under Ezra's reform after the Babylonian exile, to send her away, around 458 BC (Ezra 10:35).

entries.title: Beeliada (David's son living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: David's son, born in Jerusalem. The other lists call him Eliada, and Beeliada looks like the earlier form of the name, later avoided.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of David's sons born in Jerusalem, listed in 1 Chronicles 14:7; the parallel lists in 2 Samuel 5:16 and 1 Chronicles 3:8 call him Eliada instead, Beeliada apparently being an earlier form of the name later avoided because it contained the element "Baal."

entries.title: Beelzebub (An angel in the Old Testament)
entries.summary: Lord of the flies. It started as a title for a Philistine god and became a common New Testament name for the prince of demons. Jesus's opponents said he cast out demons by Beelzebub's power.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Beelzebub, meaning lord of the flies, was a title for a Philistine deity that became a common New Testament name for the prince of demons, and Jesus's opponents accused him of casting out demons by Beelzebub's power, a charge Jesus rebutted by pointing out a kingdom divided against itself cannot stand.

witness.excerpt: As for the following history, it confirms what Christ says, Matthew 12;27 \"If I by Beelzebub cast out demons, by whom do your Sons cast them out?\"

entries.title: Beer
entries.summary: Beer means well, and two places carry it. One was a stop in the wilderness of Moab where Israel's leaders dug a well and a short song was sung over it; the other is in Judges 9:21.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Beer, simply meaning well, names two separate places. The first was a stopping point in the wilderness of Moab where Israel's leaders dug a well, commemorated by a short song recorded in the text (Num. 21:16-18). The second was a town in Judah's hill country where Jotham, the youngest son of Gideon, fled after denouncing his brother Abimelech's kingship at Shechem (Judg. 9:21).

entries.title: Beer-elim
entries.summary: Isaiah's oracle against Moab names this well of the mighty ones as a border point the news of Moab's fall reached.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Beer-elim, meaning well of the mighty ones, is named in Isaiah's oracle against Moab as a border point where news of Moab's downfall reached (Isa. 15:8). It is generally connected with the well called simply Beer in Numbers 21:16-18, dug by Israel's leaders during the wilderness journey and celebrated in a short victory song.

entries.title: Beer-lahai-roi
entries.summary: The well of the one who lives and sees me, in the Negev, where the angel of the Lord found Hagar pregnant and running away and spoke to her. Isaac later settled near it.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Well in the Negev, its name meaning "the well of the one who lives and sees me," where the angel of the Lord found the pregnant, fleeing Hagar and spoke to her (Gen. 16:7-14). Isaac later settled in the area and was there when Rebekah's caravan first arrived to meet him (Gen. 24:62), and he returned to it again after Abraham's death (Gen. 25:11). It is traditionally placed near Kadesh-barnea, though the precise site is unconfirmed.

entries.title: Beer-shebah
entries.summary: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.
entries.books: Genesis, Joshua, Judges, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Nehemiah, Amos
entries.label: 11 books
entries.dictNote: Beersheba marked the southern edge of Judah's territory, allotted first to Simeon before it came to define the phrase "from Dan to Beersheba," shorthand for the full length of Israel. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name, one where Abraham and Abimelech swore an oath over seven ewe lambs, another where Isaac's servants struck water there a generation later. Tel Aviv University excavated the site from 1969 to 1975 and uncovered a fortified Iron Age city, giving the patriarchal stories a real settlement to sit against rather than just a name in the text.
entries.dictSource: International Standard Bible Encyclopedia (1915); Logos Factbook

entries.title: Beera (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Descended from Asher through Zophah, he is named among the heads of households in 1 Chronicles 7:37.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A descendant of Asher through Zophah, named among the heads of households in the tribal genealogy of 1 Chronicles 7:37.

entries.title: Beerah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A chief of Reuben carried off into exile by the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser III, in the eighth-century deportation that emptied out Israel's Transjordan territories.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A chief of the tribe of Reuben carried into exile by the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser III, part of the same eighth-century deportation that emptied out Israel's Transjordan territories (1 Chronicles 5:6). Tiglath-pileser's own annals, recovered from Nimrud, record his campaigns against Israel and corroborate the biblical picture of Assyrian pressure on the region in this period.

entries.title: Beeri (Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Judith's father, a Hittite. She became one of Esau's wives, and the marriage grieved Isaac and Rebekah.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Beeri (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Hosea's father. The other Beeri is the Hittite whose daughter married Esau, a marriage that grieved Isaac and Rebekah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Two Old Testament men bear this name. The first was a Hittite whose daughter Judith became one of Esau's wives, a marriage that grieved his parents Isaac and Rebekah (Genesis 26:34-35). The second was the father of the prophet Hosea, known only from the opening verse of Hosea's book (Hosea 1:1).

entries.title: Beerites (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Beriah's clan, from a son of Asher, counted in the Numbers 26 census.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Beerites were the clan descended from Beriah, a son of Asher, counted in the Numbers 26 census.

entries.title: Beeroth
entries.summary: It was one of four Hivite cities, with Gibeon, Chephirah and Kiriath-jearim. Their people tricked Joshua into a peace treaty by dressing up as travellers from far away. Later it was allotted to Benjamin.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Beeroth was one of four Hivite cities, with Gibeon, Chephirah, and Kiriath-jearim, whose people tricked Joshua into a peace treaty by posing as distant travelers (Joshua 9:3-17). It was allotted to Benjamin, and two of its native sons, Baanah and Rechab, later murdered Ish-bosheth, Saul's surviving heir, hoping to curry favor with David, who instead had them executed (2 Samuel 4:2-12). Its people are listed among those returning from Babylonian exile in Ezra and Nehemiah (Ezra 2:25).

entries.title: Beeroth
entries.summary: Named once, in Judges, and nowhere else.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Beeroth of the children of Jaakan (Bene-jaakan)
entries.summary: Wells of the Bene-jaakan, a wilderness camp. From here, in Deuteronomy's itinerary, Israel moved on to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Beeroth of the children of Jaakan, "wells of the Bene-jaakan," was a wilderness campsite from which the Israelites journeyed on to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, according to Deuteronomy's itinerary (Deuteronomy 10:6). Numbers 33:31-32 records the same stop simply as Bene-jaakan, listing it among the stations between Sinai and the plains of Moab. Its location in the Sinai or Transjordan wilderness is not established.

entries.title: Beerothite
entries.summary: Someone from Beeroth, a town of the Gibeonite league that Joshua had spared. Rechab and Baanah were Beerothites, the two officers who killed Saul's son Ish-bosheth and were executed by David for it.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Beerothite marks someone from Beeroth, a town belonging to the Gibeonite league that Joshua had spared. Rechab and Baanah, the two Beerothite officers who assassinated Saul's son Ish-bosheth and were then executed by David for it, are the most notable examples.

entries.title: Beeshterah (Ashtaroth)
entries.summary: Out of Manasseh's land east of the Jordan, the Gershonite clan was given this Levitical city, likely the same as Ashtaroth, the old Amorite capital of King Og.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Beeshterah, a Levitical city given to the Gershonite clan out of the tribe of Manasseh's territory east of the Jordan (Josh. 21:27). It is likely the same as Ashtaroth, the old Amorite capital of King Og listed elsewhere (Josh. 12:4; 13:31).

entries.title: Behemoth (A monster)
entries.summary: The huge land animal God points Job to as proof of his own power. Most read the description as a hippopotamus.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Behemoth is not a person but a massive land creature God describes to Job as proof of his own power over creation, most often identified with the hippopotamus given the description of its strength, its grass diet, and its habitat among the reeds of the river (Job 40:15-24). Some interpreters read it instead as a more general symbol of untamable animal power, or pair it with Leviathan as a primeval chaos-beast, but the hippopotamus identification best fits the physical details in the text.

entries.title: Bel (A male deity in the Old Testament)
entries.summary: Babylon's title for the god Marduk, which Isaiah and Jeremiah both mock as a powerless idol that will go into captivity itself when Babylon falls.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Bel was the Babylonian title for the god Marduk, and Isaiah and Jeremiah both mock Bel directly as a powerless idol that will itself go into captivity when Babylon falls.

entries.title: Bela (King living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: An early king, first on the Genesis 36 list, from long before Israel had a throne.
entries.label: 2 books

witness.excerpt: There were five Kings that managed the affairs of this country: Ballas , Barsas , Senabar , and Sumobor , with the King of Bela ; and each King led on his own troops.

entries.title: Bela (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Bela. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Bela (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Two things go by this name in these verses. Bela, also called Zoar, was the one city of the plain spared, kept so Lot had somewhere near to run. The name also belongs to Benjamin's firstborn son.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Bela, also called Zoar, was the only one of the five cities of the plain spared destruction, preserved at Lot's plea so he would have somewhere nearby to flee. The same name belongs to Benjamin's firstborn son, to an early king of Edom listed in Genesis and Chronicles, and to a descendant of Reuben.

witness.excerpt: And the sons of Benjamin: Bela and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, and Ehi, and Rosh, and Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard--eleven.

entries.title: Belaites (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Descended from Bela, Benjamin's firstborn, and counted in the Numbers 26 census as a clan.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Belaites were the clan descended from Bela, the firstborn son of Benjamin, counted in the Numbers 26 census.

entries.title: Belial (An angel in the Old Testament)
entries.summary: Not a person. Belial is a Hebrew word for worthlessness or wickedness, and the Old Testament uses it in phrases like sons of Belial for scoundrels and troublemakers.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Belial is not the name of an individual but a Hebrew word meaning 'worthlessness' or 'wickedness,' used throughout the Old Testament in phrases like 'sons of Belial' for scoundrels and troublemakers (Judges 19:22; 1 Samuel 2:12). By the New Testament era it had become a proper name for Satan or a chief evil power, as reflected in Paul's rhetorical question in 2 Corinthians 6:15, 'what concord hath Christ with Belial?' The term appears often in this personified sense in Second Temple Jewish writings such as the Dead Sea Scrolls.

entries.title: Belshazzar (Emperor living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: He ruled Babylon during the exile, and almost all the Bible gives of him is one night: the handwriting on the wall of his banquet hall in Daniel 5. Scripture calls him Nebuchadnezzar's son.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Belshazzar ruled Babylon during the exile and appears in the Bible almost entirely in one scene: the night handwriting appeared on the wall of his banquet hall in Daniel 5. Scripture calls him Nebuchadnezzar's son, though cuneiform records identify his real father as Nabonidus, Babylon's last official king, who left Belshazzar running the city for over a decade while he campaigned in Arabia. That same inscription answered a long-standing objection to the book of Daniel: critics had assumed Daniel simply had the wrong king, since ancient king lists never named Belshazzar as ruler, until Babylonian texts turned him up. The Nabonidus cylinders name him as Nabonidus's firstborn son; it is the Verse Account of Nabonidus that has the king entrusting the kingship to him, which is what makes him exactly what Daniel implies, the man actually in charge when the Persians took the city.

entries.title: Belteshazzar (Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Daniel's Chaldee name, given him by Nebuchadnezzar, meaning Beltis protect the king.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Beltis protect the king!, the Chaldee name given to Daniel by Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:7).

entries.title: Ben (Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He was one of the gatekeepers David put over the ark of the covenant, in the list at 1 Chronicles 15:18. He does not reappear in the parallel list a few verses on.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ben was a Levite appointed by David as one of the porters, or gatekeepers, for the ark of the covenant, named in the list of temple musicians and doorkeepers in 1 Chronicles 15:18. He does not reappear in the parallel list a few verses later, leading some to think his name was duplicated by accident from a neighboring word in the Hebrew text.

entries.title: Ben-ammi (Ammonite living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Son of my people. Lot's younger daughter bore him after they fled Sodom, and he became the ancestor of the Ammonites.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ben-ammi, whose name means "son of my people," was the son born to Lot by his younger daughter after they fled the destruction of Sodom; he became the ancestor of the Ammonites (Genesis 19:38).

entries.title: Ben-hail (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: King Jehoshaphat sent him out, with priests and Levites, to teach the Book of the Law in the towns of Judah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of the officials King Jehoshaphat of Judah sent, along with priests and Levites, to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:7-9). This teaching mission is one of the few biblical accounts of organized religious instruction outside the temple.

entries.title: Ben-hanan (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Shimon's son, in the genealogy of Judah, and nothing more.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Son of Shimon, named in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:20).

entries.title: Ben-oni (Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Son of my sorrow. Rachel gave the name to her second son as she was dying in childbirth near Bethlehem. Jacob renamed the boy Benjamin, son of the right hand.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ben-oni, meaning "son of my sorrow," was the name Rachel gave her second son with her dying breath after a difficult childbirth near Bethlehem. Jacob renamed the boy Benjamin, "son of the right hand," and he became the ancestor of the tribe of Benjamin (Genesis 35:16-18).

entries.title: Ben-zoketh (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Judahite, one of Ishi's sons in 1 Chronicles 4:20, in a short genealogical note the text never explains.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ben-zoketh was a Judahite, one of the sons of Ishi listed in the tribal genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles 4:20. The verse groups him with Zoheth, Jezoah, and other descendants in a brief, otherwise unexplained genealogical note. Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Benaiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Benaiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 1 Chronicles names him once.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Benaiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 12 men called Benaiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

entries.title: Benaiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

entries.title: Benaiah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Ezra names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Benaiah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)

entries.title: Benaiah (Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A singer from David's time, listed among the musicians in 1 Chronicles 15 and 16. The Benaiah who led David's bodyguard is another man.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Benaiah (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: He commanded David's bodyguard, and before that he was known for killing a lion in a pit on a snowy day. He also beat an Egyptian giant by wrestling the giant's own spear off him and killing him with it.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Benaiah commanded David's personal bodyguard and was famous even before that role for killing a lion in a pit on a snowy day and defeating an Egyptian giant by wrestling away the giant's own spear and killing him with it. He stayed loyal to Solomon during Adonijah's attempted coup and personally executed both Joab and Adonijah on Solomon's orders afterward, and Solomon rewarded him by making him commander of the entire army in Joab's place.

witness.excerpt: So he called for Benaiah, the captain of the guards, and ordered him to slay his brother Adonijah.

The fifth of these was Benaiah, by lineage a priest; for being challenged by [two] eminent men in the country of Moab, he overcame them by his valor, Moreover, there was a man, by nation an Egyptian, who was of a vast bulk, and challenged him, yet di
The king also constituted Benaiah captain of the guards, and of the six hundred men.
He also made Seisan the scribe, and committed the command over the guards of his body to Benaiah; the son of Jehoiada.

Now Adonijah had for his assistants Joab the captain of the army, and Abiathar the high priest; and the only persons that opposed him were Zadok the high priest, and the prophet Nathan, and Benaiah, who was captain of the guards, and Shimei, David's friend, with all the other most mighty men.

entries.title: Benaiah (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Not the captain of the bodyguard but another of David's warriors with the same name. He turns up in 2 Samuel 23:30 and twice in Chronicles.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Bene-barak (Bene-berak)
entries.summary: A town allotted to Dan in the coastal plain. It is identified with modern Bnei Brak near Tel Aviv-Jaffa, and the name is still in use.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Bene-barak, a town allotted to the tribe of Dan in the coastal plain (Josh. 19:45). The King James Version spells it Beneberak, and it is identified with modern Bnei Brak near Tel Aviv-Jaffa, a name still in use today.

entries.title: Bene-jaakan
entries.summary: Sons of Jaakan, a stop on Israel's wilderness route, also called Beeroth Bene-jaakan, wells of the sons of Jaakan. The name likely comes from a clan descended from Jaakan.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Bene-jaakan, sons of Jaakan, was a wilderness station on Israel's route, also called Beeroth Bene-jaakan, wells of the sons of Jaakan (Num. 33:31-32; Deut. 10:6). The name likely derives from a clan descended from Jaakan, a Horite chief listed in Edom's genealogy (Gen. 36:27), whose territory the wells belonged to.

entries.title: Benhadad (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: The name was a royal title in Aram-Damascus, carried by at least two kings and possibly three, all of them at war with Israel. This one is the Ben-hadad of 1 Kings 15 and 20.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Ben-hadad was a dynastic name borne by at least two, possibly three, kings of Aram-Damascus who repeatedly warred against Israel, including a lengthy siege of Samaria that drove the city to starvation before Elisha predicted a sudden, miraculous end to the famine.

witness.excerpt: WHEN the affairs of Ahab were thus, at that very time the son of Hadad, [Benhadad,] who was king of the Syrians and of Damascus, got together an army out of all his country, and procured thirty-two kings beyond Euphrates to be his auxiliaries: so he made an expedition against Ahab; but because Ahab's

It deserves here to be remarked, that this Hadad, being a very great king, was conquered by David, whose posterity yet for several generations were called Benhadad, or the son of Hadad, till the days of Hazael, whose son Adar or Ader is also in our Hebrew copy (2 Kings 13:24) written Benhadad, but in Josephus Adad or Adar.

entries.title: Benhadad (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A later king of Aram-Damascus under the same dynastic name, in 2 Kings 13. Amos 1:4 names him too.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Benhadad (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: His siege of Samaria starved the city until Elisha predicted a sudden turn. He is the Ben-hadad of 2 Kings 6 and 8.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Beninu (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A Levite who sealed the covenant under Nehemiah after the return from exile. He is named only in that list of signers.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Beninu was a Levite among those who sealed the written covenant renewing Israel's commitment to the law under Nehemiah after the return from exile (Nehemiah 10:9-14). He is named only in this list of signers.

entries.title: Benjamin (Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.
entries.books: Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Ezra, Nehemiah, Psalm, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Hosea, Obadiah, Zechariah, Acts, Romans, Philippians, Revelation
entries.label: 23 books
entries.dictNote: Benjamin was Jacob's twelfth and youngest son, born to Rachel as she died giving birth to him on the road near Bethlehem, and Jacob's fierce protectiveness of him drives much of the tension in Joseph's story, since losing Benjamin too was a grief Jacob said would kill him. His tribe later nearly destroyed itself in a civil war recorded in Judges after refusing to hand over men guilty of a horrific crime, and centuries later Benjamin's tribe produced Israel's first king, Saul, and the apostle Paul.

witness.excerpt: As for Benjamin, as commonly explained, the son of the right hand , it makes no sense at all, and seems to be a gross modern error only.
The other, Benjamin, had ten sons - Bolau, Bacchar, Asabel, Geras, Naaman, Jes, Ros, Momphis, Opphis, Arad.

entries.title: Beon (Baal-meon)
entries.summary: Beon is a short form of Baal-meon, one of the towns in the Transjordan pastureland Reuben and Gad asked Moses for, to keep their livestock.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Beon, one of the towns in the Transjordan pastureland that the tribes of Reuben and Gad requested from Moses for their livestock (Num. 32:3). It is a shortened form of Baal-meon, a town the Moabite king Mesha later claimed to have rebuilt according to his own inscription on the Moabite Stone.
