entries.title: Haran (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Abraham's brother and Lot's father, who died young in Ur before the family moved.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hararite (Warriors from Harar or Harod (cf. 2Sa.23.11, 25))
entries.summary: Roughly, the mountaineer. Three of David's mighty men carry it, among them Shammah son of Agee, who held a field of lentils against a Philistine raid on his own.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hararite, meaning roughly "the mountaineer," identifies three of David's mighty men, including Shammah son of Agee, remembered for single-handedly defending a field of lentils against a Philistine raiding party.

entries.title: Harbona (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of the seven eunuchs of King Ahasuerus, sent to fetch Queen Vashti. At the end he points out the gallows Haman built for Mordecai, and Haman is hanged on it.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Harbona was one of seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus of Persia and was sent to summon Queen Vashti to the king's banquet (Esther 1:10). He reappears at the story's climax, pointing out to the king the gallows Haman had built for Mordecai, which Haman was then hanged on himself (Esther 7:9).

entries.title: Hareph (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: A son of Hur in Judah's genealogy, and founder of Beth-gader; the chapter uses his name to mark a town's clan.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Listed in the genealogy of Judah as a son of Hur and "father," meaning founder, of Beth-gader (1 Chr. 2:51). Like most names in this chapter he functions as an eponym marking a town's founding clan rather than a fully narrated individual.

entries.title: Harhaiah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Uzziel the goldsmith worked on the wall by the Old Gate, and Harhaiah was his father.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Father of Uzziel, one of the goldsmiths who helped repair a section of Jerusalem's wall near the Old Gate under Nehemiah's rebuilding project (Nehemiah 3:8).

entries.title: Harhas (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Grandfather of Shallum, the keeper of the king's wardrobe. Shallum's wife was Huldah the prophetess, the one consulted when the book of the law turned up in Josiah's temple repairs. Chronicles spells him Hasrah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Harhas was the grandfather of Shallum, keeper of the king's wardrobe, whose wife Huldah the prophetess was consulted after the book of the law was discovered during Josiah's temple repairs (2 Kings 22:14). The parallel account in 2 Chronicles 34:22 spells the name Hasrah.

entries.title: Harhur (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: His name means fever. His descendants were temple servants, Nethinim, who came back with Zerubbabel, and nothing more is known of him.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Harhur's descendants were among the families of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:51; Nehemiah 7:53). His name means “fever” or possibly “inflammation.” Nothing more is known of him.

entries.title: Harim (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: The third priestly course in 1 Chronicles 24:8 went by this name, and the family came back from exile. Some of them were among the men Ezra confronted for marrying foreign wives.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Harim was a common priestly family name in the postexilic period, listed among those who returned from exile and later among those confronted by Ezra for marrying foreign wives against the law.

entries.title: Harim (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Ezra and Nehemiah name him twice, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Hariph (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.

entries.title: Hariph (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A family head, also called Jorah, whose descendants came back from exile with Zerubbabel. The name is also among those who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hariph was the ancestral head of a family, also called Jorah, whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel; his name appears both among the list of returnees and among those who sealed the covenant under Nehemiah (Nehemiah 7:24; 10:19; compare Ezra 2:18).

entries.title: Harnepher (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Zophah's son, a chief of Asher, in 1 Chronicles 7:36. Nothing beyond the name survives.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A chief of the tribe of Asher listed among the sons of Zophah in the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles 7:36. Nothing beyond the name survives; he belongs to the long catalogue of tribal heads Chronicles preserves to anchor Israel's clan structure after the exile.

entries.title: Harodite
entries.summary: Shammah and Elika, two of David's mighty men, came from Harod, probably the spring near Mount Gilboa where Gideon had tested his troops.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Harodite identifies Shammah and Elika, two of David's mighty men, as being from Harod, likely the spring near Mount Gilboa where Gideon earlier tested his troops before facing the Midianites.

entries.title: Harorite (Harod)
entries.summary: It is what Chronicles calls Shammoth, one of David's mighty men, where Samuel's list has Shammah the Harodite.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Harorite marks Shammoth among the roll of David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles 11:27; the parallel list in 2 Samuel 23:25 gives the same warrior's name as Shammah the Harodite, tying him to En-harod, the spring near Mount Gilboa where Gideon had once tested his troops.

entries.title: Harosheth
entries.summary: Sisera's base, the Canaanite general who led Jabin's iron chariots. Barak broke his army at the Kishon and chased what was left back here. Where exactly it was is still argued over, near Mount Carmel or a district name for several settlements.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Fortified town on the northern edge of the plain of Jezreel, home base of Sisera, the Canaanite general who commanded Jabin's iron chariots (Judges 4:2). Barak's forces routed Sisera's army at the Kishon River and pursued the survivors back to Harosheth, breaking Canaanite power in the region (Judges 4:13-16). Its exact site is debated, with candidates ranging from a fortress near the Kishon's outlet at the foot of Mount Carmel to a district name covering several Canaanite settlements rather than a single town.

entries.title: Harsha (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Temple servants, Nethinim, back from Babylon with Zerubbabel, and his family was one of them. The name means worker, or possibly enchanter.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Harsha, whose name means “worker” or possibly “enchanter,” headed a family of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:52; Nehemiah 7:54). The Nethinim performed menial temple duties and were likely descended from Gibeonites and war captives assigned to that service centuries earlier. Nothing more is recorded of him personally.

entries.title: Harum (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Aharhel's father, in Judah's genealogy at 1 Chronicles 4:8.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Harum was a descendant of Judah named in the tribal genealogy of 1 Chronicles 4:8 as the father of Aharhel.

entries.title: Harumaph (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Named only so his son Jedaiah can be told apart. Jedaiah rebuilt the stretch of Jerusalem's wall opposite his own house.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: The father of Jedaiah, one of the men who helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall opposite his own house after the return from exile (Neh. 3:10). He is named only to identify his son.

entries.title: Haruphite (Warriors, perhaps from Haruph)
entries.summary: Shephatiah, a Benjamite archer and slinger, came from Hariph and joined David at Ziklag while David was still hiding from Saul.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Haruphite identifies Shephatiah, a Benjamite archer and slinger, as being from Hariph; he was among the warriors who joined David at Ziklag while David was still hiding from Saul.

entries.title: Haruz (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He came from Jotbah, and his daughter Meshullemeth married King Manasseh of Judah and bore King Amon. That one notice is all.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Haruz was the father of Meshullemeth, who became the wife of King Manasseh of Judah and the mother of King Amon; he is identified as being from Jotbah (2 Kings 21:19). He is mentioned only in this one royal genealogical notice.

entries.title: Hasadiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: In David's royal line after the exile, one of Pedaiah's sons. Nothing else about him is recorded.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hasadiah was one of the sons of Pedaiah listed in 1 Chronicles 3:20, part of the royal genealogy of David traced through Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile. Nothing else about him is recorded.

entries.title: Hasbadana (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: When Ezra read the law from the wooden platform, he was one of the men standing beside him. Nothing further is recorded about him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hasbadana was one of the men who stood beside Ezra on the wooden platform built for the public reading of the law after the return from exile (Nehemiah 8:4). Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Hasenuah (including the art)
entries.summary: The Hebrew name carries the article, the Senuah. A Benjamite family that settled in Jerusalem after the exile traced itself back to him.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hasenuah, whose Hebrew name includes the definite article (“the Senuah”), was an ancestor of a Benjamite family that resettled in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9:7; Nehemiah 11:9).

entries.title: Hashabiah (Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy)

entries.title: Hashabiah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: He served in Ezra's day; the name was a common Levitical one, carried by musicians, officials and administrators over several generations.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hashabiah was a common Levitical name, borne by several temple musicians, officials, and administrators across different generations in Chronicles, Ezra, and Nehemiah.

entries.title: Hashabnah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: He sealed the covenant Nehemiah led the returned exiles to make, and that is all.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of the leaders who sealed the covenant of renewed obedience to the law that Nehemiah led the returned exiles to affirm (Nehemiah 10:25-26).

entries.title: Hashabniah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Hattush, one of the men repairing Jerusalem's wall, was his son. Another Hashabniah of the same time was a Levite who helped lead the public confession.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hashabniah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A Levite who helped lead Israel in confession and prayer after the law was read out.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hashabniah was the name of two men in Nehemiah's time. One was the father of Hattush, who helped repair Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3:10). The other was a Levite who joined in leading Israel's public confession and prayer after the wall's completion (Nehemiah 9:4-5).

entries.title: Hashem (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Gizonite. His sons were among David's mighty men. Samuel's parallel list calls him Jashen.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hashem was a Gizonite whose sons are named among David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles 11:34. The parallel list in 2 Samuel 23:32 gives the name differently, as Jashen, reflecting the textual variants common between these two overlapping rosters.

entries.title: Hashmonah
entries.summary: One of the stops on the wilderness route, a little before Moseroth and near Mount Hor. The name may have to do with fatness or fruitfulness, and nobody knows where it was.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hashmonah was one of the stations on Israel's wilderness route, coming shortly before Moseroth in the itinerary of Numbers 33 (Num. 33:29-30), in the general vicinity of Mount Hor. Its name may relate to fruitfulness or fatness, though nothing further is recorded about it and its location is unknown.

entries.title: Hashub (Levite living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: The Levite of this name in the lists of those living in Jerusalem after the return.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hashub was a common postexilic name among those who helped repair sections of Jerusalem's walls under Nehemiah.

entries.title: Hashub (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A man from the exile and the return, and Nehemiah is the only book that names him.

entries.title: Hashub (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hashub (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of 4 men called Hashub. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hashubah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: David's line, after the exile: one of the sons listed after Zerubbabel in the royal genealogy.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hashubah was a descendant of David through Zerubbabel's line, one of several sons listed after Zerubbabel in the royal genealogy compiled after the exile (1 Chr. 3:19-20).

entries.title: Hashum (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Head of a family among the exiles who came back. Ezra 10:33 lists men of his family who had married foreign wives.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hashum was the head of a family among the returning exiles, listed among those who signed Nehemiah's covenant renewal.

entries.title: Hashum (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Hashum. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hashum (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hashupha (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Also spelled Hasupha. His family were Nethinim, temple servants, and they came back in the first group from Babylon. Nothing further is recorded about him.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hashupha, also spelled Hasupha, headed a family of Nethinim, temple servants whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile in the first group led by Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:43; Nehemiah 7:46). Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Hasrah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Huldah the prophetess was his wife, and Josiah's officials went to her when the Book of the Law was found. He kept the vestments, and Kings spells him Harhas.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Keeper of the sacred vestments in the temple and husband of Huldah the prophetess, whom King Josiah's officials consulted after the Book of the Law was discovered (2 Chronicles 34:22); the parallel account in 2 Kings 22:14 gives his name as Harhas.

entries.title: Hatach (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Esther's eunuch, the go-between who carried her messages to Mordecai and back while Haman's plot hung over the Jews.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hathach was a eunuch assigned to attend Queen Esther, and he served as the go-between carrying messages from Esther to Mordecai during the crisis over Haman's plot to destroy the Jews.

entries.title: Hatipha (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Of the Nethinim, the temple servants. His family came back from exile to Jerusalem.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hatipha headed a family among the Nethinim, the temple servants, whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:54; Nehemiah 7:56).

entries.title: Hatita (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Gatekeepers of the temple. His family held the post and came back from exile with Zerubbabel.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hatita headed a family of temple gatekeepers whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:42; Nehemiah 7:45).

entries.title: Hattil (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Among Solomon's servants, temple workers whose families came back with Zerubbabel, his was one. Nothing further is recorded about him.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hattil headed a family descended from "Solomon's servants," temple workers whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:57; Nehemiah 7:59). Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Hattush (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hattush (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: The Hattush in these verses is a priest, listed once among the men who sealed Nehemiah's covenant and once among the priests who came back. The note about David's descendant who came with Ezra fits a different man.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hattush was a descendant of David who returned from Babylonian exile with Ezra, keeping the royal line represented among those who came back to Jerusalem.

entries.title: Hattush (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of 4 men called Hattush. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Ezra.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hattush (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A man from the exile and the return, and Nehemiah is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hauran
entries.summary: Cave-land, the fertile east of Bashan, named in Ezekiel's boundaries for the land to come. The Greeks and Romans called it Auranitis, centred on Bosra, and its basalt buildings still stand.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hauran, cave-land, was the fertile eastern district of Bashan named in Ezekiel's description of Israel's future boundaries (Ezekiel 47:16, 18). The region, known to the Greeks and Romans as Auranitis, is centered on the city of Bosra and is noted for its dense, well-preserved basalt architecture; the Nabateans who controlled the area before Rome annexed it in AD 106 left monumental remains there comparable to those at Petra, confirming the district's long-standing prosperity as a crossroads of Arabian trade routes.

entries.title: Havilah
entries.summary: Genesis puts it near the rivers of Eden and calls it rich in gold. The name turns up in two different family lines, so it may be two places.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Havilah is named in Genesis as a land rich in gold near the garden of Eden's rivers, and the name also appears among the descendants of both Cush and Joktan, suggesting it may refer to more than one region.

entries.title: Havilah
entries.summary: Named once, in Genesis, and nowhere else.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Havilah (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Havilah (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Cush's son in Genesis 10:7. The same name is also a land rich in gold by Eden's rivers, and a son of Joktan, so it may cover more than one region.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Hazael (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Elijah was told to anoint him king of Aram, and the prophet wept over what Hazael would do to Israel. He smothered his own king to get the throne and was one of Israel's worst enemies for decades. An inscription with his name has been found in Damascus.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Hazael was a Syrian official whom the prophet Elijah was told to anoint as the next king of Aram, and Elijah wept when he predicted the atrocities Hazael would commit against Israel. Hazael smothered his own king to death to take the throne and spent decades afterward as one of Israel's most destructive enemies, and an inscription bearing his name has been found at his own capital, Damascus, independently confirming his reign.

witness.excerpt: Hazael makes an expedition against the people of Israel , and the inhabitants of Jerusalem .

The voice also commanded him to return home, and to ordain Jehu, the son of Nimshi, to be king over their own multitude; and Hazael, of Damascus, to be over the Syrians; and Elisha, of the city Abel, to be a prophet in his stead; and that of the impious multitude, some should be slain by Hazael, and others by Jehu.

Now it happened that Elisha the Prophet, at that time, was gone out of his own countrey to Damascus; of which Benhadad was informed, he sent Hazael, the most faithful of all his servants, to meet him, and to carry him presents, and bad him enquire of him about his distemper; and whether he should escape the danger that it threatened.

It deserves here to be remarked, that this Hadad, being a very great king, was conquered by David, whose posterity yet for several generations were called Benhadad, or the son of Hadad, till the days of Hazael, whose son Adar or Ader is also in our Hebrew copy (2 Kings 13:24) written Benhadad, but in Josephus Adad or Adar.

entries.title: Hazaiah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A man of Judah from the Shilonite clan, Shelah's line, who settled in Jerusalem after the exile. Nothing else is recorded about him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hazaiah was a man of Judah from the Shilonite clan, descended from Shelah, listed among those who settled in Jerusalem after the exile (Nehemiah 11:5). Nothing else is recorded about him.

entries.title: Hazar-addar
entries.summary: The border point near Kadesh-barnea on the south of the promised land, which Joshua 15:3 calls Addar.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hazar-addar, a point on Israel's southern boundary in the Negev near Kadesh-barnea, listed among the wilderness border markers of the promised land (Num. 34:4). The same site appears as Addar in Joshua 15:3.

entries.title: Hazar-enan
entries.summary: The corner of the promised land in the northeast, in Numbers 34:9-10, and again on the northern line of Ezekiel's restored Israel. It means village of springs. It probably sat in the Anti-Lebanon near Damascus, but nobody has found it.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Village named as a landmark on the northeastern frontier of the promised land in Moses' description of Israel's borders (Num. 34:9-10), and again on the northern boundary of Ezekiel's vision of a restored Israel (Ezek. 47:17; 48:1). Its name means "village of springs," and it likely lay somewhere in the Anti-Lebanon range near Damascus, though the exact site has not been identified.

entries.title: Hazar-enon (Hazar-enan)
entries.summary: Where the borders of Damascus and Hamath met, on Israel's northern line in Ezekiel 47:17. Its precise location has not been recovered.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A landmark village on the northern boundary of Israel's territory, marking the meeting point of the borders of Damascus and Hamath in the tribal boundary lists (Num. 34:9; Ezek. 47:17). Its name means village of springs, but its precise location has not been recovered.

entries.title: Hazar-gaddah
entries.summary: One of the towns in the far south of Judah's allotment, near the border with Edom, and its site has not been found.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hazar-gaddah was one of the towns in the southernmost district of Judah's tribal allotment, near the border with Edom (Joshua 15:27). Nothing more is recorded of it, and its site has not been identified.

entries.title: Hazar-hatticon (Hazer-hatticon)
entries.summary: The middle village, a marker on the northern boundary in Ezekiel's vision of the land restored, near Hamath and toward Hauran.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hazar-hatticon, a "middle village" marking part of Israel's future northern boundary in Ezekiel's vision of the restored land, located near Hamath toward the region of Hauran (Ezek. 47:16).

entries.title: Hazar-shual
entries.summary: Village of the jackal. It sat on Judah's southern border and later fell inside Simeon's share, and people came back to live there after the exile. It is commonly placed near Tell es-Sa'weh, between Beersheba and Moladah.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Hazar-shual, "village of the jackal," was a town on the southern border of Judah, later included within Simeon's allotment (Joshua 15:28; 19:3). Its residents returned there after the Babylonian exile, according to the settlement list in Nehemiah 11:27. It is commonly identified with a site near Tell es-Sa'weh, between Beersheba and Moladah.

entries.title: Hazar-susah
entries.summary: Village of the horse, a town on Judah's southern border that went to Simeon.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A town on the southern border of Judah assigned to Simeon, its name meaning village of the horse (Josh. 19:5). It is listed among Solomon's chariot cities in 2 Chronicles 1:14, fitting a name tied to horses.

entries.title: Hazar-susim
entries.summary: The same town Joshua calls Hazar-susah. In the Simeonite clan lists of 1 Chronicles 4:31 the name is plural, village of horses.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Simeonite town in the Negev whose name means village of horses, listed in the genealogical record of Simeon's clans (1 Chr. 4:31). It corresponds to Hazar-susah in Joshua 19:5.

entries.title: Hazarmaveth (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Joktan's son, in the Arabian branch of Shem's descendants. The name survives almost unchanged in Hadramawt, a region of southern Arabia in Yemen known in the ancient world for frankincense and spice.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hazarmaveth is listed in the Table of Nations as a son of Joktan, part of the Arabian branch of Shem's descendants (Gen. 10:26; 1 Chr. 1:20). The name is preserved almost unchanged in Hadramawt, a region of southern Arabia in modern Yemen, known in antiquity for its role in the frankincense and spice trade routes.

entries.title: Hazelelponi (Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: A woman in Judah's genealogy, sister of the sons of Etam. Nothing further is recorded about her.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hazelelponi was a woman named in the genealogy of Judah as the sister of the sons of Etam (1 Chronicles 4:3). Nothing further is recorded about her.

entries.title: Hazeroth
entries.summary: The third camp after Sinai, in the wilderness of Paran. Miriam and Aaron challenged Moses here over his Cushite wife. Miriam was struck with a skin disease and healed when Moses prayed for her.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hazeroth was the third campsite of the Israelites after leaving Sinai, in the wilderness of Paran (Numbers 33:17-18). It was here that Miriam and Aaron challenged Moses's authority over his marriage to a Cushite woman, and Miriam was struck with a skin disease until Moses interceded for her healing (Numbers 12:1-15).

witness.excerpt: A little while afterward he rose up, and went from mount Sinai; and having passed through several mansions, of which we will speak anon, he came to a place called Hazeroth : where the multitude began again to be mutinous, and to blame Moses for the misfortunes they had suffered in their travels; and that when he had persuaded to leave a good land, they at once had lost that land; and inst

entries.title: Hazezon-tamar (Engedi)
entries.summary: An Amorite town by the Dead Sea that Chedorlaomer's kings attacked in Abraham's day, later called En-gedi. The old name comes back in Jehoshaphat's reign, when Moabites, Ammonites and Meunites come up against Judah from there.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Amorite town by the Dead Sea attacked by the coalition of eastern kings under Chedorlaomer in Abraham's day (Gen. 14:7), later known by the name En-gedi. The older name resurfaces generations later when a coalition of Moabites, Ammonites, and Meunites invades Judah during Jehoshaphat's reign, approaching from this same location (2 Chr. 20:2).

entries.title: Haziel (Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He was a Gershonite Levite, through Shimei, in the lists David drew up for temple service.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Levite of the Gershonite clan, descended through Shimei, listed among those organized for temple service under David (1 Chronicles 23:9).

entries.title: Hazo (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Nahor and Milcah had him, one of the sons who became Aramean clans. Nahor was Abraham's brother.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of the sons of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his wife Milcah, listed among the Aramean clans descended from him (Genesis 22:22).

entries.title: Hazor
entries.summary: The head of all the Canaanite kingdoms, in Joshua's words, and the biggest city-state in the region. Its fall decided the northern campaign. The dig there found a huge Bronze Age city to match.
entries.label: 5 books
entries.dictNote: Hazor was the largest and most powerful Canaanite city-state in the region, and Joshua's destruction of it, described as the head of all the Canaanite kingdoms, was the decisive victory of the northern campaign. Excavations at the site have uncovered a massive Bronze Age city consistent with the biblical description of its scale.

witness.excerpt: For this Jabin came out of Hazor, a city that was situate over the lake Semechonitis; and had in pay three hundred thousand footmen; and ten thousand horsemen; with no fewer than three thousand chariots.

Testament of Judah, Chapter 3

3 1 And when the two kings of the Canaanites came sheathed in armour against our flocks, and much people with them, single-handed I rushed upon the king of Hazor, and smote him on the greaves 2 and dragged him down, and so I Slew him.

entries.title: Hazor
entries.summary: Jeremiah 49 pronounces judgment on the kingdoms of Hazor and says the place will be left desolate for good. It is not Joshua's Canaanite city; the name also belonged to a place in Arabia.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hazor
entries.summary: It is new Hazor, Hazor-hadattah, in the far south near Moladah, and Joshua 15:25 is its only appearance.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hazor
entries.summary: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hazor
entries.summary: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hazor
entries.summary: Nehemiah names him once, and nothing else is recorded.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Heber (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 4 men called Heber. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Heber (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Heber (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Not the Kenite. This Heber is in Genesis 46:17 among the family that went down to Egypt, and Numbers 26:45 makes him the head of a clan.
entries.label: 3 books

entries.title: Heber (Man living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Kenite, and his wife Jael killed Sisera in her tent when the Canaanite general came running. That fulfilled Deborah's word that a woman would get the credit.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Heber was a common Old Testament name, most notably a Kenite whose wife Jael killed the fleeing Canaanite general Sisera in her tent, fulfilling Deborah's prophecy that a woman would receive the credit for his death.

entries.title: Heberites (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Counted in Numbers 26, the clan of Heber, Asher's grandson through Beriah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Heberites were the clan descended from Heber, a grandson of Asher through Beriah, counted in the Numbers 26 census.

entries.title: Hebrew
entries.summary: In the New Testament it can mean the Jewish people, their old language or their traditional way of life. Philippians 3:5 has a Hebrew born of Hebrews.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Hebrew in the New Testament refers to the Jewish people, their ancestral language, or their traditional way of life, and it's also used to describe the language Jesus and others spoke, actually Aramaic in common first-century usage, in passages like the naming of Golgotha.

entries.title: Hebrew (A language)
entries.summary: In the New Testament it means the people, the language, or the way of life. Paul calls himself a Hebrew of Hebrews to say he is all three.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hebrew in the New Testament refers to the Jewish people, their ancestral language, or their traditional way of life, and Paul describes himself as a Hebrew of Hebrews to emphasize his thoroughly Jewish credentials before his conversion.

entries.title: Hebron
entries.summary: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.
entries.books: Genesis, Numbers, Joshua, Judges, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles
entries.label: 9 books
entries.dictNote: Hebron is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, sitting in the hill country south of Jerusalem and known earlier as Kirjath-arba. Abraham camped nearby at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah there to bury Sarah, and the site remained associated with the patriarchs; Herod's massive stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands as one of the best preserved ancient structures in the region. Joshua assigned the city to Caleb, and centuries later David reigned there for seven years before moving his capital to Jerusalem. The same Hebrew name also belongs to a son of Kohath the Levite and to a descendant of Caleb listed in Chronicles.

witness.excerpt: A leopard in Hebron leaped upon my dog, and I caught it by the tail, and 7 hurled it on the rocks, and it was broken in twain.

And the men of Hebron sent to him saying, "Behold thy brother hath come against thee, to fight thee, with four thousand girt with the sword, and they carry shields and weapons"; for they loved Jacob more than Esau.
So they came to Hebron, and showed David the head of Ishbosheth, and presented themselves to him as his well-wishers, and such as had killed one that was his enemy and antagonist.

entries.title: Hebron
entries.summary: A border town of Asher, sometimes spelled Ebron, and not the Hebron of Judah. Some manuscripts read Abdon here, and where it was is uncertain.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: This Hebron, sometimes spelled Ebron, was a border town of the tribe of Asher named in the list of Asher's territory (Josh. 19:28). It is a different place from the far better known Hebron of Judah, the burial site of Abraham and Sarah and later David's first royal capital; because of the similarity some manuscripts and versions read Abdon instead at this point, and the exact site of this Asherite town remains uncertain.

witness.excerpt: These cities were, of the tribe of Judah, Hebron; of that of Ephraim, Shechem; and of that of Naphtali, Cadesh; which is a place of the upper Galilee.

Testament of Asher, Chapter 8

8 1 And when he had said these things unto them he commanded them, saying: Bury me in Hebron.
[“Now Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.”] (17) Some of the ancients call this famous tree, or grove, an Oak , others, a Turpentine tree, or grove.

entries.title: Hebron (Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Kohath's son, a Levite, and a clan of Levites came from him.
entries.label: 3 books

entries.title: Hebron (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Hebron. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hebronites (Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: They were Levites of Kohath's line, through his son Hebron. Under David they were put over Israelite land west of the Jordan and over treasuries tied to the temple.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hebronites were a Kohathite Levitical clan descended from Hebron, one of Kohath's sons, distinct from the city of the same name. Under David they were given administrative duties over Israelite territory west of the Jordan and oversight of temple related treasuries.

entries.title: Hegai (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: The eunuch over King Ahasuerus's harem at Susa. He liked Esther from the start and gave her cosmetics, servants and the best place in the house, which likely helped her become queen.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hegai was the eunuch in charge of King Ahasuerus's harem at Susa who managed the young women, including Esther, brought in for the king's consideration (Esther 2:8). He took a particular liking to Esther and gave her preferential treatment, cosmetics, servants, and the best place in the harem, which likely improved her chances of being chosen queen (Esther 2:9, 15).

entries.title: Helah (Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of the two wives of Ashur, founder of Tekoa, in Judah's genealogy.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Helah was one of two wives of Ashur, the Chronicler's founder of Tekoa, listed in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:5, 7).

entries.title: Helam
entries.summary: East of the Jordan, where Joab led David's army against Hadadezer's Arameans under Shobach and broke them. After that the Arameans stopped helping the Ammonites. Nobody has fixed the site.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Helam was a location east of the Jordan where David's army, under Joab, decisively defeated the Aramean forces of Hadadezer, commanded by Shobach, ending Aramean support for the Ammonites in that war (2 Samuel 10:15-18). Its exact site has not been identified, though some have proposed a location near the upper Euphrates.

entries.title: Helbah
entries.summary: Asher never drove the Canaanites out of this town in the coastal plain of Phoenicia, and it has not been matched to a modern site.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Helbah was a town assigned to the tribe of Asher, one of the Canaanite towns Asher failed to drive its inhabitants out of, according to Judges 1:31. It lay somewhere in the coastal plain of Phoenicia and has not been securely identified with a modern site.

entries.title: Helbah (Helbon)
entries.summary: Ezekiel 27:18 actually says Helbon. Damascus sells Tyre the wine of Helbon and white wool, and Helbon is usually placed at Halbun in the hills northwest of Damascus, whose wine Strabo says the Persian kings imported.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: The reference carried here, Ezekiel 27:18, actually names Helbon rather than Helbah: in the prophet's list of Tyre's trading partners, Damascus supplies wine of Helbon along with white wool. Helbon is usually identified with the village of Halbun in the hills northwest of Damascus, a region whose wine, according to the Greek geographer Strabo, was prized enough for the Persian kings to import it. It should not be confused with the Helbah of Asher mentioned in Judges 1:31.

entries.title: Heldai (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Zechariah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Heldai (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Two men. One was over David's army in the twelfth month, a Netophathite. The other came back from Babylon with gold and silver, and Zechariah was told to make a crown from it for Joshua the high priest.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Two men in the Old Testament carry this name. The first, a Netophathite also called Heleb or Heled, was one of David's thirty mighty men and commanded the army division on duty in the twelfth month (2 Samuel 23:29; 1 Chronicles 27:15). The second was one of a group of exiles who returned from Babylon bringing gold and silver, from which the prophet Zechariah was told to make a crown for Joshua the high priest as a sign of the coming Messianic king-priest (Zechariah 6:10-11).

entries.title: Heleb (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Baanah's son, a Netophathite and one of David's thirty. Chronicles calls him Heled, and nothing else is recorded.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of David's thirty mighty men, listed as the son of Baanah the Netophathite (2 Sam. 23:29). The parallel list in 1 Chronicles 11:30 gives his name as Heled; nothing else about him is recorded beyond his place in this roster of elite warriors.

entries.title: Heled (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Chronicles has this name among David's thirty where Samuel has Heleb son of Baanah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of David's mighty men, listed among the thirty elite warriors in 1 Chronicles 11:30. The parallel list in 2 Samuel 23:29 calls him Heleb son of Baanah.

entries.title: Helek (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: From Manasseh through Gilead, he headed the Helekite clan, counted in the census and given land.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Helek was a descendant of Manasseh through Gilead, head of the Helekite clan counted in the wilderness census and later allotted land in Gilead (Numbers 26:30; Joshua 17:2). Nothing further is recorded of him individually.

entries.title: Helem (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: In Zechariah 6:14 he is one of the returned exiles whose silver and gold went into the crown for Joshua the high priest. Verse 10 calls him Heldai, so Helem is probably just another form of that name.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Helem appears in Zechariah's vision as one of the returned exiles whose silver and gold the prophet was told to use for a crown for the high priest Joshua, a sign pointing to the coming messianic "Branch" (Zechariah 6:9-14). Verse 10 calls the same man Heldai, so Helem is likely an alternate form of that name rather than the earlier Asherite of the same name in 1 Chronicles 7:35.

entries.title: Helem (Man living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: Of Asher, through Beriah's line, in the tribal genealogy at 1 Chronicles 7:35.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A descendant of Asher, listed in the tribal genealogy as a great-grandson through the line of Beriah (1 Chronicles 7:35).

entries.title: Heleph
entries.summary: Naphtali's boundary starts here. The name means exchange. Nobody has found the place.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Heleph marked the starting point of Naphtali's tribal boundary in the list recorded at Joshua 19:33. The Hebrew name means exchange or substitution, but the site itself has never been securely identified on the ground, and the text gives no further detail about it.

entries.title: Helez (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Helez (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of David's mighty warriors.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Helez was one of David's mighty warriors, and also, separately, the name of a descendant of Judah in the genealogies of Chronicles.

entries.title: Heli (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Luke 3:23 makes him Joseph's father, where Matthew names Jacob. Readers since antiquity have said Luke is tracing Mary's line, or that a levirate marriage explains it, and the question is still open.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus as the father of Joseph (Luke 3:23), though Matthew's genealogy names Jacob as Joseph's father instead. Since antiquity, readers have proposed that Luke traces Mary's ancestry through Heli while Matthew traces Joseph's, or that the two lists reflect a levirate marriage; the discrepancy is old and remains unresolved. Nothing else concerning Heli is recorded in scripture.

entries.title: Helkai (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: He headed a priestly family in the days of Joiakim the high priest. Nothing further is recorded about him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Helkai was the head of a priestly family in the days of the high priest Joiakim, listed in Nehemiah's roster of priests who had returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 12:15). The list documents the reconstituted priestly courses functioning in the early Second Temple period. Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Helkath
entries.summary: Asher's town, given with its pastures to the Gershonite Levites. Chronicles calls it Hukok.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Town allotted to the tribe of Asher and assigned, with its pasturelands, to the Gershonite Levites (Josh. 19:25; 21:31). A parallel list in Chronicles calls the same town Hukok (1 Chr. 6:75).

entries.title: Helkath-hazzurim
entries.summary: Field of blades, roughly. By the pool of Gibeon twelve of Joab's men and twelve of Abner's killed each other in pairs, and it set off the battle between David's side and Ish-bosheth's.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: The site near the pool of Gibeon where twelve of Joab's men and twelve of Abner's men killed each other in mutual single combat, an episode that touched off a larger battle between the forces of David and Saul's son Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 2:16). The name means roughly "field of daggers" or "field of sword-edges."

entries.title: Helkites (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: They came from Helek, Manasseh's grandson through Gilead, and got a share of the land.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Helkites were the clan descended from Helek, a grandson of Manasseh through Gilead, counted among the families that received an inheritance in the land.

entries.title: Helon (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Zebulun's leader in the wilderness census was his son.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Helon was the father of the tribal leader of Zebulun during the wilderness census.

witness.excerpt: Abdon also, the son of Hillel, of the tribe of Ephraim, and born at the city Pyrathon, was ordained their supreme governor after Helon.

Now when Esau, one of the sons of Isaac, whom the father principally loved was now come to the age of forty years, he married Adah, the daughter of Helon; and Aholibamah the daughter of Esebeon: which Helon and Esebeon were great Lords among the Canaanites: thereby taking upon himself the authority, and pretending to have dominion over his own marriages, without so much

entries.title: Hemam (Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Lotan's son and grandson of Seir the Horite, among the clan chiefs, and 1 Chronicles 1:39 calls him Homam.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Son of Lotan and grandson of Seir the Horite, listed among the clan chiefs of Edom (Genesis 36:22), called Homam in the parallel list in 1 Chronicles 1:39.

entries.title: Heman (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Kings and Psalm name him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Heman (Man living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Heman. This one is a man from the years before the monarchy, named once in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Heman (Singer living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: David put him among the chief musicians over the worship, a Levite. Psalm 88, one of the darkest laments in the book, is credited to him.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Heman was a Levite and one of the chief musicians David appointed over temple worship, credited as the author of Psalm 88, one of the darkest and most unresolved laments in the Psalter.

witness.excerpt: He also excelled and distinguished himself in wisdom above those who were most eminent among the Hebrews at that time for shrewdness; those I mean were Ethan, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol.

entries.title: Hemdan (Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Eldest son of Dishon, one of the Horite chiefs who held the land before Esau's descendants took it. Chronicles calls him Hamran.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Eldest son of Dishon, one of the Horite clan chiefs descended from Seir who inhabited the land before it was taken by Esau's descendants, the Edomites (Genesis 36:20-26). He appears only in this genealogical list; the parallel list in 1 Chronicles 1:41 gives the name as Hamran.

entries.title: Hen (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Son of Zephaniah, one of the men a crown in the temple was meant to remember. He is probably the Josiah son of Zephaniah of verse 10, though the text never explains the second name.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hen son of Zephaniah is named in Zechariah 6:14 as one of the men in whose honor a symbolic crown was placed in the temple as a memorial, part of Zechariah's prophetic sign-act pointing to the coming Branch. He is probably the same man called Josiah son of Zephaniah earlier in the same chapter (Zechariah 6:10), though the text does not explain the second name.

entries.title: Hena
entries.summary: The Assyrian messenger names it to Hezekiah as one more city Assyria has already taken. It is usually identified with Anah on the Euphrates, near Sepharvaim.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hena was a city in Mesopotamia that the Assyrian king listed among the places his empire had already conquered when his messenger tried to intimidate Hezekiah into surrendering Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:34; 19:13; Isaiah 37:13). It is usually identified with Anah, a town on the Euphrates not far from Sepharvaim, another city named in the same list.

entries.title: Henadad (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: His Levitical family helped oversee the temple rebuilding under Zerubbabel and, a generation on, the walls under Nehemiah.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Henadad was the head of a Levitical family who helped oversee the rebuilding of both the temple under Zerubbabel and, a generation later, Jerusalem's walls under Nehemiah.

entries.title: Henadad (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Henadad (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Henadad. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hepher
entries.summary: Named twice, in Joshua and 1 Kings, and nowhere else.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Hepher (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 4 men called Hepher. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hepher (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Gilead's son, of Manasseh, and the father of Zelophehad. Zelophehad had five daughters and no son, and their case before Moses won daughters the right to inherit.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hepher was a son of Gilead in Manasseh and father of Zelophehad, whose five daughters successfully petitioned Moses for the right to inherit their father's land in the absence of a son, a case that established a lasting principle of inheritance law in Israel. Separately, Hepher was a Canaanite royal city that Joshua conquered; it later gave its name to a district in Solomon's administrative system. The name also belonged to one of Asher's descendants and to one of David's mighty warriors.

entries.title: Hepher (Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A warrior from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Hepherites (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Hepher's clan, counted in Numbers 26.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Hepherites were the clan descended from Hepher, a grandson of Manasseh through Gilead, counted in the Numbers 26 census; his son Zelophehad's five daughters successfully petitioned Moses for a share of the tribal inheritance despite having no brothers.

entries.title: Hephzi-bah (Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: My delight is in her. She was Hezekiah's wife and Manasseh's mother. Isaiah takes the same name for Jerusalem restored, no longer the abandoned wife.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Hephzibah, meaning "my delight is in her," was the wife of King Hezekiah of Judah and mother of his son Manasseh (2 Kings 21:1). Isaiah later uses the same name as a symbolic title for restored Jerusalem, picturing the city as once again the object of God's delight rather than an abandoned wife (Isaiah 62:4).

entries.title: Heres
entries.summary: Sun. The Amorites held Mount Heres with Aijalon and Shaalbim until the house of Joseph subdued them, and Gideon came back from chasing the Midianite kings by the ascent of Heres. Whether that is one place or two is not certain.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Heres, meaning sun, names a hill-country location associated with the Amorites, who held Mount Heres along with Aijalon and Shaalbim until the house of Joseph subdued them (Judg. 1:35). The same name recurs as the ascent of Heres, a route Gideon took while returning from his pursuit of the Midianite kings (Judg. 8:13); whether the two references describe the same feature or two different places sharing the name is not certain from the text.

entries.title: Heresh (Levite living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of the Levites who resettled Jerusalem after the exile, from the gatekeepers who came out of the singers' guild.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Levite listed among those who resettled Jerusalem after the exile, one of the temple gatekeepers descended from the guild of singers (1 Chronicles 9:15).

entries.title: Hereth
entries.summary: A forest in Judah. David hid there with his growing band after leaving his parents with the king of Moab, and the prophet Gad told him to go. Where it was is unknown.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Not a person but a forest in Judah where David hid with his growing band of followers, shortly after he had placed his parents under the protection of the king of Moab and before the prophet Gad advised him to move on (1 Sam. 22:5). Its exact location is unknown today.

entries.title: Hermas (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: A Roman Christian Paul greets in his letter. Later tradition sometimes made him the author of The Shepherd of Hermas, but that book is almost certainly another man's, written a generation or more later.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Roman Christian greeted by Paul in Romans 16:14. Later Christian tradition sometimes credited him with writing the second-century work The Shepherd of Hermas, but that book was almost certainly written a generation or more later by a different Hermas.
