And Sherri also divided amongst his sons, and the first portion came forth for Elam and his sons, to the east of the river Tigris till it approacheth the east, the whole land of India, and on the Red Sea on its coast, and the waters of Dêdân, and all the mountains of Mebrî and ’Êlâ, and all the land of Sûsân and all that is on the side of Pharnâk  to the Red Sea and the river Tînâ.

521.] Now, in the first year of the King’s reign, Darius feasted those that were about him, and those born in his house, with the rulers of the Medes, and princes of the Persians, and the toparchs of India and Ethiopia, and the generals of the armies of his hundred and twenty seven provinces.

entries.title: Iphedeiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of Benjamin's chiefs, in the Chronicles genealogy of families settled in Jerusalem.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A chief of the tribe of Benjamin listed among the family heads who settled in Jerusalem, part of the genealogical record preserved in 1 Chronicles 8:25.

entries.title: Ir (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: A hard verse in Benjamin's genealogy, and many read this name as a variant of Iri, Bela's son a few verses earlier. Nothing else is known.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ir appears in the genealogy of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles 7:12, one of the more textually difficult verses in Chronicles; many read it as a variant or scribal form of Iri, a son of Bela named a few verses earlier (1 Chronicles 7:7). Beyond this genealogical mention, nothing else is known.

entries.title: Ira (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Ira (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Ira. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Samuel.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ira (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of David's elite warriors, who in Chronicles also commands one of the monthly army divisions. Ira was the name of more than one of David's men.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ira was the name of more than one of David's officials, including a priest and one of his elite warriors known as the Ithrite.

entries.title: Irad (Man living at the time before the Flood)
entries.summary: Cain's grandson through Enoch and Mehujael's father. His line runs on to Lamech and the culture-founders Jabal, Jubal and Tubal-cain.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A grandson of Cain through Enoch, and the father of Mehujael, in the brief genealogy Genesis 4:18 traces from Cain down to Lamech and his children. The list exists mainly to connect Cain's line to the culture-founders named two verses later, Jabal, Jubal, and Tubal-cain.

entries.title: Iram (Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: A clan chief of Edom, from Esau's descendants in the hill country of Seir.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Iram was a clan chief of Edom, listed among the descendants of Esau who headed tribal divisions in the hill country of Seir (Genesis 36:43; 1 Chronicles 1:54).

witness.excerpt:
Testament of Judah, Chapter 8

8 1, 2 And I had much cattle, and I had for chief herdsman Iram the Adullamite.

entries.title: Iri (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Bela's son and Benjamin's grandson, head of a family in Benjamin's genealogy.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Son of Bela and grandson of Benjamin, head of a family in the tribal genealogies of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7:7,12).

entries.title: Irijah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He was the guard captain at the Benjamin Gate who stopped Jeremiah leaving Jerusalem during a lull in the Babylonian siege and accused him of deserting to the Chaldeans. The princes had Jeremiah beaten and locked up.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Irijah was a captain of the guard at Jerusalem's Benjamin Gate who arrested the prophet Jeremiah as he tried to leave the city during a lull in the Babylonian siege, accusing him of deserting to the Chaldeans (Jeremiah 37:13-14). He handed Jeremiah over to the princes, who had him beaten and imprisoned. Jeremiah maintained his innocence, but the episode led to a long and dangerous confinement (Jeremiah 37:15-21).

entries.title: Irnahash
entries.summary: "City of the serpent", one of the town names in Judah's genealogy. Nobody knows where it was.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Irnahash, meaning "city of the serpent," a town listed among the descendants of Judah in the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles 4:12. Nothing else is known of it and its location has not been identified.

entries.title: Iron
entries.summary: In Upper Galilee, a fortified town of Naphtali, and nothing to do with the metal. It is generally identified with the modern village of Yarun, which keeps the old name.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A fortified town of the tribe of Naphtali in Upper Galilee (Josh. 19:38), distinct from the metal of the same English name. It is generally identified with the modern village of Yarun, which preserves the ancient name, called Yiron in some translations.

witness.excerpt: In this ridge of mountains there is one called the Iron mountain , that runs in length as far as Moab.

entries.title: Irpeel
entries.summary: One of Benjamin's fourteen cities near Gibeon, and no trace of it has been found.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin, listed among its fourteen cities near Gibeon (Josh. 18:27-28). No trace of its site has been identified.

entries.title: Iru (Man living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: Caleb's eldest son. Caleb was the faithful spy who got Hebron. Nothing further is recorded about Iru.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Iru was the eldest son of Caleb son of Jephunneh, the faithful spy who received Hebron as an inheritance, listed among Caleb's descendants in 1 Chronicles 4:15. Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Isaac (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.
entries.books: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Psalm, Jeremiah, Amos, Matthew, Mark, Luke, Acts, Romans, Galatians, Hebrews, James
entries.label: 21 books
entries.dictNote: Isaac was the long-promised son of Abraham and Sarah, born when his father was a hundred years old, and Scripture's most searching test of Abraham came when God ordered Isaac sacrificed on Mount Moriah before providing a ram at the last moment. He married Rebekah through his father's servant's mission back to Mesopotamia, and late in life, blind and dying, he was tricked by his younger son Jacob into giving him the blessing meant for the older twin, Esau. Isaac is the only patriarch who never left the land of Canaan, and the only one recorded marrying just one wife.

witness.excerpt: So he went immediately to the altar to be sacrificed. And the deed had been done if God had not opposed it; for he called loudly to Abraham by his name, and forbade him to slay his son.
Isaac, who is compared with Hope, was richly endowed before birth.
Isaac was weaned in this jubilee, and Abraham made a great banquet in the third month, on the day his son Isaac was weaned.  2.

entries.lukeNote: Named only three times in Luke, always paired with Abraham and Jacob as shorthand for the patriarchs (13:28, 20:37). Josephus tells the Moriah story with the same beats as Genesis 22, but adds Isaac's own willing consent as a grown man, a detail Genesis never states outright.

entries.title: Isaiah (Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Amoz's son, a prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century, who counselled four kings of Judah and is quoted in the New Testament more than any other prophet. He gave his two sons names that were sermons, Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem he told Hezekiah the city would stand, and the Taylor Prism brags of the siege without ever claiming the city fell.
entries.books: 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Ezra, Nehemiah, Isaiah, Matthew, Mark, Luke, John, Acts, Romans
entries.label: 12 books
entries.dictNote: Isaiah was an eighth-century prophet in Jerusalem, the son of Amoz, who advised four kings of Judah in succession and became the most quoted prophet in the New Testament. He was married to a woman Scripture itself calls a prophetess, and he named his two sons as walking sermons, Shear-jashub, meaning a remnant will return, and Maher-shalal-hash-baz, meaning the spoil speeds, the prey hastens. Isaiah told King Hezekiah that Jerusalem would survive Sennacherib's siege, and Assyria's own record of that campaign, the Taylor Prism, confirms the invasion happened and boasts of shutting Hezekiah up like a caged bird, though notably it never claims Sennacherib actually took the city, matching the Bible's account of a siege that stopped short.

witness.excerpt: he was by the confession of all, a divine and wonderful man in speaking truth; and out of the assurance that he had never written what was false, he wrote down all his prophecies.

And so God sent Isaiah the Prophet, and commanded him to inform Hezekiah, that “Within three days time he should get clear of his distemper, and should survive it fifteen years; and that he should have children also.” Now upon the Prophet’s s
This was known to Cyrus by his reading the book which Isaiah left behind him of his Prophecies.

entries.lukeNote: Luke opens John the Baptist's ministry by quoting Isaiah (3:4) and has Jesus himself read from the Isaiah scroll in the Nazareth synagogue (4:17), both times treating the text as self-evidently authoritative. Josephus, writing for outsiders to the faith, argues for that same authority on different grounds: Isaiah never wrote a false word, so his own writings needed no editor to verify them.

entries.title: Iscah (Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Haran's daughter, sister to Milcah and Lot, in one line of Terah's family record. Jewish tradition sometimes made her Sarah, though Genesis never says so.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Iscah was a daughter of Haran and sister of Milcah and Lot, named in the family record of Terah's household in Ur of the Chaldees (Genesis 11:29). Ancient Jewish tradition sometimes identified her with Sarah, Abraham's wife, though the biblical text does not make this connection explicit.

entries.title: Iscariot (Apostle living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Judas Iscariot kept the money for the twelve, and John says he stole from it. He sold Jesus for thirty pieces of silver and picked him out with a kiss in Gethsemane. Afterwards he gave the money back and hanged himself, though Matthew and Acts tell his death differently.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve apostles, entrusted with the group's money as its treasurer, and John's Gospel says he regularly stole from the funds even before his greater betrayal. He handed Jesus over to the religious authorities for thirty pieces of silver, identifying him with a kiss in the garden of Gethsemane, and afterward, overcome with remorse, he returned the money and hanged himself, though the accounts in Matthew and Acts describe the specifics of his death somewhat differently.

entries.title: Ish-bosheth (Saul's son living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Saul's surviving son, whom Abner made king over Israel while David held only Judah. When Abner went over to David, two of Ish-bosheth's own captains killed him in his bed.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ish-bosheth was Saul's surviving son, installed as a rival king over Israel by Saul's general Abner while David ruled only Judah, and after Abner defected to David's side, two of Ish-bosheth's own captains assassinated him in his bed, bringing his brief and largely powerless reign to an end.

entries.title: Ishbah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: "Father of Eshtemoa" in Judah's genealogy, which probably means he founded the town's settlement rather than fathered a son. Nothing else is recorded about him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ishbah appears in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles 4 as the father of Eshtemoa, meaning he was reckoned the founder or ancestor of that town's settlers rather than a literal parent. Nothing else is recorded about him.

entries.title: Ishbak (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Abraham had him by Keturah. He is usually taken as the ancestor of an Arabian tribe, but nobody can say which.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ishbak was a son of Abraham by his wife Keturah, traditionally regarded as the ancestor of an Arabian tribe, though it cannot be identified with certainty (Genesis 25:2).

witness.excerpt: And she bare him six sons, Zimram, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah, in the two weeks of years.

entries.title: Ishbi-benob (Giant living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: He was a Philistine giant from the Rephaim who almost killed David, until Abishai struck him down, and after that David's men would not let David go out to battle again.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of the descendants of the Rephaim, a Philistine giant who nearly killed David in battle before Abishai intervened and struck him down (2 Samuel 21:16-17). The episode marks the point at which David's men insisted he no longer go out to battle personally.

entries.title: Ishi (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Named once in Judah's genealogy. The word means "my husband", and Hosea uses it for Israel coming back to God, in place of the colder "my master".
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ishi (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

entries.title: Ishi (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 4 men called Ishi. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ishi (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A name in the genealogies of Judah and Manasseh. The word itself means my husband, and Hosea uses it for what Israel will call God again.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ishi was a common name in the genealogies of Judah and Manasseh, and the word itself, meaning my husband, is also used by Hosea as a picture of Israel's restored, tender relationship with God, contrasted with the more formal my master.

entries.title: Ishiah (Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A levite from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ishiah (Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: A Levite in the lists of temple divisions, named twice in Chronicles. Isshiah was a common Levitical name.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Isshiah was a common Levitical name in Chronicles, borne by several musicians and descendants of Izhar.

entries.title: Ishiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 5 men called Ishiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ishiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ishiah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A man from the exile and the return. Ezra names him once.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ishma (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: One name in a short, tangled fragment of Judah's genealogy, grouped with Etam.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ishma appears in a terse genealogical fragment of the tribe of Judah, grouped with the clans associated with Etam (1 Chr. 4:3). The family relationships in this passage are difficult to reconstruct with certainty.

entries.title: Ishmael (Abraham's son living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Abraham's first son, by Hagar, Sarah's servant. Sarah had given Hagar to Abraham while she was still childless, then wanted mother and son gone after Isaac came. God promised Hagar her son would father a great nation too, though the covenant line ran through Isaac.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Ishmael (Jeremiah's adversary living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: After Jerusalem fell this Ishmael murdered Gedaliah, the governor the Babylonians had set over the land, and the killing sent another wave of Jews running for Egypt.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ishmael was Abraham's first son, born to Sarah's servant Hagar after Sarah, still childless, offered Hagar to Abraham as a way to fulfill God's promise of an heir on their own timetable. After Isaac was born, tension between the two half-brothers led Sarah to insist Hagar and Ishmael be sent away, and God promised Hagar that Ishmael would also become the father of a great nation, though not the covenant line. A later Ishmael, generations afterward, assassinated the Babylonian-appointed governor Gedaliah after Jerusalem's fall, triggering a fresh wave of Jewish flight into Egypt.

witness.excerpt: And Abraham said unto God: "O that Ishmael might live before thee!" 19.

entries.title: Ishmael (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 6 men called Ishmael. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ishmael (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ishmael (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

entries.title: Ishmael (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Ezra names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.

entries.title: Ishmaelite (Abraham's son living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: The Ishmaelites came from Abraham's son Ishmael and traded across the country south and east of Canaan. One of their caravans bought Joseph from his brothers and took him down to Egypt.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Ishmaelites were descendants of Ishmael, Abraham's son by his wife's servant Hagar, and lived as nomadic traders in the region south and east of Canaan. A caravan of Ishmaelite merchants bought Joseph from his brothers and carried him down into Egypt, setting up the rest of his story.

witness.excerpt:
And they dealt treacherously with him, and formed a plot against him to slay him, but changing their minds,

they sold him to Ishmaelite merchants, and they brought him down into Egypt, and they sold him to Potiphar, the eunuch  of Pharaoh, the chief of the cooks,  priest of the city of ’Êlêw.  12.

entries.title: Ishmaiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A ruler over Zebulun in David's organisation of the tribes.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Two men named Ishmaiah appear in Chronicles. One was a Gibeonite warrior who joined David's forces at Ziklag while David was still fleeing Saul, noted as a leading man among the thirty mighty men (1 Chronicles 12:4). The other, son of Obadiah, served as chief officer over the tribe of Zebulun under David (1 Chronicles 27:19).

entries.title: Ishmaiah (Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Gibeonite who came over to David at Ziklag while David was still on the run from Saul, and a leader among the thirty.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ishmerai (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: From Elpaal's family, a Benjamite household head in Jerusalem, and nothing more is said of him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Benjamite of the family of Elpaal, listed among the heads of families living in Jerusalem in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles 8:18. Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Ishod (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Hammoleketh's son, of the half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ishod was a son of Hammoleketh, of the half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan, named in the tribal genealogy of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:18).

entries.title: Ishpan (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Benjamite listed under Shashak's family, and that is all.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ishpan was a Benjamite listed among the family of Shashak in the tribal genealogy of 1 Chronicles 8:22.

entries.title: Ishuai (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: One of the household that went down to Egypt, named again in the Numbers census with a clan of his own and once more in Chronicles.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Ishvi was a son of Saul, listed among his children in 1 Samuel, though he does not appear among those killed alongside Saul at Gilboa, and some scholars think the name may be an alternate designation for one of the other sons.

entries.title: Ishuai (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ishvah (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: A son of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family. Numbers leaves him out of Asher's clans, which may mean he founded no line.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ishvah was a son of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family (Genesis 46:17; 1 Chronicles 7:30). He is absent from the later clan census of Asher in Numbers 26, which may mean he died without founding a family line.

witness.excerpt: And the sons of Asher: Imnah, and Ishvah, (and Ishvi), and Beriah, and Serah, their one sister--six.

entries.title: Ismachiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: In Hezekiah's reforms the temple filled with tithes and gifts, and Ismachiah was one of the Levites set over them, with Cononiah and Shimei, under the high priest Azariah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ismachiah was a Levite appointed as one of the overseers of the freewill offerings, tithes, and dedicated gifts brought into the temple during King Hezekiah's religious reforms, serving alongside Cononiah and Shimei under the high priest Azariah (2 Chr. 31:12-13).

entries.title: Ispah (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: A Benjamite family head from Beriah's line who lived in Jerusalem.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A head of a Benjamite family descended from Beriah, listed among the clan leaders who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:16, 28).

entries.title: Israel (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.
entries.books: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, Ruth, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Ezra, Nehemiah, Psalm, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Song of Solomon, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel, Daniel, Hosea, Joel, Amos, Obadiah, Micah, Nahum, Zephaniah, Zechariah, Malachi, Matthew, Mark, Luke, John, Acts, Romans, 1 Corinthians, 2 Corinthians, Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, Hebrews, Revelation
entries.label: 47 books
entries.dictNote: Israel is the name God gave Jacob after he wrestled through the night with a mysterious figure at Peniel, and it became the name of the entire nation descended from Jacob's twelve sons, which is why this single name accounts for well over two thousand references across the Bible, far more than any individual person could generate alone. See the entry for Jacob for the man himself; most uses of Israel elsewhere refer to the people, the twelve-tribe nation, the northern kingdom after the split from Judah, or the land itself, depending on context and period.

witness.excerpt: And Israel took his journey from †Haran†  from his house on the new moon of the third month, and he went on the way of the Well of the Oath,  and he offered a sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac on the seventh of this month.
And all Israel mourned for him, and all Egypt, with a great mourning.
But when Israel saw that the famine was very sore in the land, and there was no deliverance, he said unto his sons: "Go again, and procure food for us that we die not." 16.

entries.title: Israelite (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: One of the people descended from Jacob, who was renamed Israel. Paul calls himself an Israelite in Romans 11 when he argues God has not dropped his people.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Israelite denotes a member of the covenant people descended from Jacob, who was renamed Israel, and the word is used across both Testaments as a marker of that shared identity. Paul, for instance, appeals to his own status as "an Israelite" when defending God's continued faithfulness to his ancient people in Romans 11.

witness.excerpt: Know therefore that I shall provide for you all in common what is for your good, and particularly for thyself what shall make thee famous; for that child, out of dread of whose nativity the Egyptians have doomed the Israelite children to destruction, shall be this child of thine, and shall be concealed from those who watch to destroy him: and when he is brought up in a surprising way, he shall deliver the Hebrew nation from the distress they

entries.title: Israelitish (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Not a name. Leviticus uses it for the mother of a man stoned for blasphemy, Shelomith, daughter of Dibri of Dan, who had married an Egyptian. The case asked whether the law covered someone of mixed parentage, and the answer was one law for native and foreigner alike.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Israelitish is not a personal name but an adjective describing the mother of the man stoned for blasphemy in Leviticus 24:10-11; she is named Shelomith, daughter of Dibri of the tribe of Dan, married to an Egyptian. The passage uses her Israelite identity to raise the legal question of whether the law against blasphemy applied to someone of mixed parentage. God's answer, that one law applies to native and foreigner alike, settles the case.

entries.title: Isri (Levite living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: In the census of Numbers 26 this is the clan from Jezer, Naphtali's son, rather than one man.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Isri is not a personal name but the gentilic form of Jezer, one of the sons of Naphtali, used in the wilderness census of Numbers 26:49 to identify the clan descended from him: "of Jezer, the family of the Jezerites." The underlying Hebrew word functions the same way as Hamulites or Shuhamites elsewhere in that same census chapter, marking a family group rather than an individual person. Its appearance among personal-name records in older reference works reflects the difficulty early lexicographers had distinguishing Hebrew gentilic adjectives from proper names once transliterated into English.

entries.title: Issachar (Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Jacob's ninth son. His tribe held the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Chronicles says its men understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do.
entries.books: Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, 1 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Ezekiel, Revelation
entries.label: 11 books
entries.dictNote: Issachar was Jacob's ninth son, and his tribe's territory in the fertile Jezreel Valley made it one of the more agriculturally prosperous regions, while 1 Chronicles describes the men of Issachar as having understanding of the times, knowing what Israel ought to do, a phrase later commentators have taken as a model for discerning wisdom.

entries.title: Italian (Italy)
entries.summary: In Acts 10 Cornelius is a centurion of the Italian Cohort at Caesarea, a Roman auxiliary unit. Inscriptions from Syria show a Cohors II Italica in the region in the first century, and many scholars take it to be this unit.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: The word Italian in Acts 10:1 describes the Italian Cohort, the Roman auxiliary unit commanded by the centurion Cornelius at Caesarea. Such cohorts were recruited from freeborn citizens native to Italy rather than from the local population, and inscriptions found in Syria attest to a Cohors II Italica stationed in the region in the first century, which many scholars identify with the unit named in Acts.
