entries.title: Italy
entries.summary: Aquila and Priscilla had just come from Italy when Paul met them, after Claudius threw the Jews out of Rome. Paul later went there as a prisoner, by way of a shipwreck. Hebrews ends with greetings from "those from Italy".
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Italy is named several times in the New Testament in connection with the spread of the early church. Aquila and Priscilla had recently come from Italy when Paul met them in Corinth, having been expelled from Rome along with other Jews by an edict of the emperor Claudius, a decree the Roman historian Suetonius later corroborates, noting that Claudius expelled Jews from the city for rioting "at the instigation of Chrestus," likely a garbled reference to disputes over Christ (Acts 18:2). Paul was later transported to Italy as a prisoner, surviving a shipwreck off Malta before finally reaching Rome (Acts 27:1-6; 28:11-16), and the writer of Hebrews closes his letter with greetings from "those from Italy," likely Italian Christians living abroad (Hebrews 13:24).

witness.excerpt: So he sent Mucianus to Italy, and committed a considerable army both of horsemen and footmen to him.

For all men that were in Italy showed their respects to him in their minds before he came thither, as if he were already come, as esteeming the very expectation they had of him to be his real presence, on account of the great desires they had to see
BY this time Herod had sailed out of Italy to Ptolemais, and had gotten together no small army, both of strangers and of his own countrymen, and marched through Galilee against Antignus.

entries.title: Ithai (David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Ittai, a Philistine commander from Gath, who would not leave David when Absalom rebelled, though David offered to release him. David gave him a third of the army.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ittai was a Philistine commander from Gath who insisted on staying loyal to David and fleeing with him during Absalom's rebellion rather than accepting David's offer to release him from any obligation, and David rewarded that loyalty by giving him command of a third of his army.

witness.excerpt: Absalom attacked him, but set over his men captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds, and divided his army into three parts; the one part he committed to Joab, the next to Abishai, Joab's brother, and the third to Ittai, David's companion and friend, but one that came from the city Gath; and when he was desirous of fighting himself among them, his friends would not let him: and this refusal of theirs was founded upon very wise reasons:

entries.title: Ithai (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a warrior from the united kingdom.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Ithamar (Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Aaron's youngest son. Two of his brothers died for offering unauthorized fire and Eleazar became high priest, and Ithamar was put over the Levites who carried and kept the tabernacle. Eli came from his line, which held the high priesthood for a while before it went back to Eleazar's line under Zadok.
entries.label: 5 books
entries.dictNote: Ithamar was Aaron's fourth and youngest son, and after his two eldest brothers died for offering unauthorized fire and his other brother Eleazar became high priest, Ithamar oversaw the Levites responsible for transporting and maintaining the tabernacle. His descendants held the high priesthood for a period, including Eli, before it returned to Eleazar's line under Zadok.

witness.excerpt: Now Eli was the first of the family of Ithamar, the other son of Aaron, that had the government: for the family of Eleazar officiated as High Priest at first; the son still receiving that honour from the father: which Eleazar bequeathed to his son Phineas; after who

He had at that time four sons; Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

2.

He divided them also into courses: and when he had separated the priests from them, he found of these priests twenty-four courses, sixteen of the house of Eleazar, and eight of that of Ithamar; and he ordained that one course should minister to God eight days, from sabbath to sabbath.

entries.title: Ithiel (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of the Benjamite ancestors of the families who settled Jerusalem after the exile.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ithiel (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of the two men Agur addresses at the head of his sayings in Proverbs.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Two different men bear this name in the Bible. One is listed among the Benjamite ancestors of the Jerusalem settlers who returned after the exile (Nehemiah 11:7). The other appears in the opening line of Agur's sayings in Proverbs 30:1, addressed alongside Ucal, though the Hebrew wording there is difficult and some translations read it as a phrase rather than a personal name.

entries.title: Ithmah (Moabite warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: David's mighty men included a Moabite, and this is him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Moabite counted among the elite warriors of David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles 11:46, notable as a foreigner who attained a place of honor in David's inner circle of fighters.

entries.title: Ithnan
entries.summary: Far south in Judah near Edom, listed with Kedesh and Hazor, and no trace of it has been found.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ithnan was one of the southernmost towns allotted to Judah, near the border with Edom, listed alongside Kedesh and Hazor in Joshua's territorial record (Joshua 15:23). Nothing else is known of it, and no trace of the site has been found.

entries.title: Ithra (Ishmaelite living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Amasa's father, and Amasa led Absalom's army against David. Ithra married Abigail, David's sister, so Amasa was David's nephew. Samuel calls him an Israelite; Chronicles calls him Jether the Ishmaelite.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ithra was the father of Amasa, the commander David's son Absalom placed over his rebel army during the revolt against David. He is called an Israelite in 2 Samuel 17:25 but Jether the Ishmaelite in the parallel genealogy of 1 Chronicles 2:17, one of several small textual variants in the record of David's extended family. His wife Abigail was David's sister, making Amasa David's nephew.

witness.excerpt: He appointed Amasa to be captain of all his host, instead of Joab his kinsman: his father was Ithra and his mother Abigail: now she and Zeruiah, the mother of Joab, were David's sisters.

entries.title: Ithran (Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: A Horite clan name, from Edom's earlier inhabitants.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ithran was a Horite clan name listed among Edom's earlier inhabitants, and also the name of a descendant of Asher in the tribal genealogies.

entries.title: Ithran (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ithream (David's son living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: David's sixth son born at Hebron, by his wife Eglah, and the story never mentions him again.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ithream was the sixth son born to David during his reign in Hebron, his mother being David's wife Eglah (2 Samuel 3:5; 1 Chronicles 3:3). He is not mentioned again in the narrative.

entries.title: Ithrite (Warriors, perhaps from Ithar)
entries.summary: Ira and Gareb, two of David's mighty men, both carry this label. It may tie them to Kiriath-jearim, but where the name comes from is not known for sure.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ithrite marks two of David's mighty men, Ira and Gareb, and may connect them to the town of Kiriath-jearim, though the name's exact origin is uncertain.

entries.title: Ittahkazin (Eth-kazin)
entries.summary: A marker on Zebulun's border, found in Joshua 19:13 and nowhere else. Nobody has located it.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ittah-kazin was one of the boundary markers listed for the tribal territory of Zebulun in Joshua 19:13, and it is not mentioned anywhere else in the Bible. Its precise location has not been identified.

entries.title: Ituraea
entries.summary: Northeast of Galilee, around Mount Hermon and the Anti-Lebanon, and Philip ruled it with Trachonitis when John began preaching. Its people, the Itureans, were semi-nomadic Arabs.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A region northeast of Galilee, around Mount Hermon and the Anti-Lebanon range, ruled together with Trachonitis by the tetrarch Philip in Luke's account of John the Baptist's ministry (Luke 3:1). Its inhabitants, the Itureans, were a semi-nomadic Arab people later absorbed into the Roman client kingdom of Chalcis; Roman-era coinage from the region confirms the local dynasts Luke's Gospel situates alongside Herod's sons.

entries.title: Izeharites (Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: The family of Izhar, Kohath's son. Korah came from them, the Levite who rebelled against Moses and Aaron and was swallowed by the earth.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Izharites were a Kohathite Levitical family descended from Izhar, son of Kohath. The most notorious member of this clan was Korah, who led a rebellion against the authority of Moses and Aaron in the wilderness and was swallowed up by the earth as a result in Numbers 16.

entries.title: Izhar (Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: He was Kohath's son, and his own son Korah led the rebellion against Moses in the wilderness.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Izhar was a son of Kohath and the father of Korah, the Levite who led the rebellion against Moses in the wilderness.

entries.title: Izrahiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Two men. One is a chief of Issachar in the genealogies; the other, generations later, is at the dedication of Jerusalem's rebuilt walls under Nehemiah.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Two men carry this name. One was a chief of the tribe of Issachar listed in the tribal genealogies (1 Chronicles 7:3). The other was a priest present at the dedication of Jerusalem's rebuilt walls under Nehemiah, generations later (Nehemiah 12:42).

entries.title: Izrahite (Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: The label on Shamhuth, who commanded David's division for the fifth month. It most likely means he came from Zerah, Judah's son.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Izrahite identifies Shamhuth, commander of David's military division for the fifth month, an epithet that likely points to descent from Zerah, one of Judah's sons.

entries.title: Jaakan (Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Ezer's son, grandson of Seir the Horite, and Genesis calls him Akan. His descendants gave their name to one of Israel's camps in the wilderness.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Son of Ezer and grandson of Seir the Horite (1 Chronicles 1:42), called Akan in the parallel Edomite genealogy of Genesis 36. His descendants, the Bene-jaakan, gave their name to one of Israel's wilderness campsites.

entries.title: Jaakobah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A clan leader of Simeon, with a name built on the same root as Jacob.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jaakobah, a name built from the same root as Jacob, was a descendant of Simeon listed among the clan leaders of that tribe (1 Chronicles 4:36).

entries.title: Jaala (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: His family were among the Nethinim, the temple servants, who came back from Babylon with Zerubbabel.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jaala headed a family among the Nethinim, the temple servants whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:56; Nehemiah 7:58). The Nethinim performed menial temple duties and are traditionally traced back to Gibeonites and war captives assigned to Levitical service.

entries.title: Jaanai (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Gadite chief in Bashan, named once.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A chief among the Gadites who settled in Bashan, named in the tribal record of 1 Chronicles 5:12.

entries.title: Jaare-oregim (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Samuel names him as father of Elhanan, who killed Goliath the Gittite. Chronicles has the father as Jair and the victim as Lahmi, Goliath's brother, and most scholars think "oregim", weavers, slipped in from the next words about the spear shaft.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jaare-oregim was a Bethlehemite named in 2 Samuel 21:19 as the father of Elhanan, the warrior credited there with killing Goliath the Gittite. The parallel account in 1 Chronicles 20:5 instead names the father as Jair and specifies that Elhanan killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath, a difference most scholars attribute to a scribal duplication of the word "oregim" (weavers) from the following clause describing the spear shaft. The name itself, meaning "forests of the weavers," likely preserves a trade-guild connection rather than functioning as a simple personal name.

entries.title: Jaasau (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: In Ezra's list of men who agreed to put away the foreign wives they had married.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of the Israelites listed in Ezra's record who agreed to separate from the foreign wives they had married during the years Israelites lived among the surrounding nations (Ezra 10:37).

entries.title: Jaasiel (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Son of Abner, and chief officer over Benjamin in David's administration.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: This name is attached to two men in Chronicles. Jasiel the Mesobaite appears among David's mighty warriors (1 Chronicles 11:47), while Jaasiel son of Abner served as chief officer over the tribe of Benjamin under David's administrative system (1 Chronicles 27:21). Whether these are the same man is not stated in the text.

entries.title: Jaasiel (Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He is Jasiel the Mesobaite in the roll of David's mighty warriors.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jaazaniah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: More than one man had the name. One is an army captain who came to the new governor after Jerusalem fell, in Kings and again in Jeremiah; another heads the family Jeremiah brought into the temple and offered wine.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jaazaniah was the name of more than one Old Testament figure, including a man Ezekiel saw in a vision leading elders in secret idol worship inside the temple itself.

entries.title: Jaazaniah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Jaazaniah. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Ezekiel.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jaazaniah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Ezekiel names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jaazer
entries.summary: Jazer, an Amorite town in Gilead east of the Jordan. Israel took it and gave it to Gad, then to the Levites of Merari. Isaiah and Jeremiah both use its ruined vineyards as a picture of Moab's ruin.
entries.books: Numbers, Joshua, 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, Isaiah, Jeremiah
entries.label: 6 books
entries.dictNote: Jazer was an Amorite town east of the Jordan in Gilead, taken by Israel and assigned to Gad, then given to the Levites descended from Merari. It later belonged to a district under a Hebronite overseer in David's administration. Isaiah and Jeremiah both use Jazer's ruined vineyards as an image of Moab's coming devastation.

entries.title: Jaaziah (Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: One of Merari's descendants, listed when David set the Levites into divisions for temple service.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jaaziah was a descendant of Merari, one of the three Levitical clans, listed among those reorganized into divisions of temple service under David (1 Chronicles 24:26-27).

entries.title: Jaaziel (Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He played the harp when David brought the ark up to Jerusalem, and he is probably the Aziel named two verses later.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Levite musician appointed to play the harp when David brought the ark of the covenant up to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 15:18-20). He is probably the same Levite called Aziel in the list of harpists two verses later.

entries.title: Jabal (Man living at the time before the Flood)
entries.summary: Cain's line through Lamech and Adah comes down to him and his brother: Jabal is "the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle", and Jubal is credited with music.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A descendant of Cain through Lamech and Adah, remembered in Genesis 4:20 as "the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle," marking him as the traditional originator of a nomadic, herding way of life. His brother Jubal is credited in the same passage with originating instrumental music.

entries.title: Jabbok
entries.summary: Jacob crossed this stream alone the night before he met Esau, wrestled until daybreak, and came away named Israel and limping. It runs west into the Jordan through a gorge in Gilead, halfway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea, and is the Zarqa River today.
entries.label: 5 books
entries.dictNote: The Jabbok is a stream flowing west into the Jordan roughly midway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea, running through a deep gorge in the Gilead highlands; it formed a boundary between the Ammonites and the kingdom of Og, and later between Reuben and half of Manasseh (Joshua 12:2; Deuteronomy 3:16). Jacob crossed it alone the night before meeting Esau and there wrestled with a divine figure until daybreak, coming away with the name Israel and a permanent limp (Genesis 32:22-31); it is identified today with the Zarqa River in Jordan.

witness.excerpt: And he passed over the Jabbok  in the ninth month, on the eleventh thereof.

entries.title: Jabez
entries.summary: Named once, in 1 Chronicles, and nowhere else.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jabez (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Jabez prayed for God to bless him and widen his borders, and the text says God did. He is from Judah's genealogy, and the prayer is all we have of him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jabez names both a person and a place under one Hebrew word. The person is a descendant of Judah remembered for a short prayer asking God to bless him and enlarge his territory, a prayer the text says God granted (1 Chronicles 4:9-10). Separately, 1 Chronicles 2:55 lists Jabez as a town inhabited by families of scribes connected to the Kenite clans of the house of Rechab.

entries.title: Jabin (King living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: King of Hazor, and master of Sisera, whom Deborah and Barak beat. A Psalm still asks God to deal with Israel's enemies as he dealt with Jabin.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jabin was a title used for at least two different kings of Hazor, one defeated by Joshua during the conquest and a later one whose general Sisera was defeated by Deborah and Barak generations afterward.

witness.excerpt: And since in the beginning of the next chapter it is said by Josephus, that there was hardly a breathing time for the Israelites before Jabin came and enslaved them; it is highly probable that some of the copies in his time had here only 8 years, instead of 80.

And now it was that the Israelites, taking no warning by their former misfortunes to amend their manners; and neither worshipping God, nor submitting to the laws; were brought under slavery by Jabin the King of the Canaanites; and that before they had a short breathing time after the slavery under the Moabites.

entries.title: Jabin (King living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: Joshua names him once, and he is a king from the years before the monarchy.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jabneel
entries.summary: On Judah's northwestern border near the coast, the town later called Jabneh or Jamnia. Uzziah tore down its walls.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jabneel
entries.summary: Two towns carry the name, not a man, and this one is on Naphtali's border.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jabneel is the name of two towns in the conquest narratives, not a person. One marked the northwestern border of Judah near the coast, later known as Jabneh or Jamnia (Joshua 15:11); the other lay on the boundary of Naphtali in the north (Joshua 19:33). The coastal Jabneh later became a notable Jewish town, and its walls were torn down by King Uzziah of Judah (2 Chronicles 26:6).

entries.title: Jabneh (Jabneel)
entries.summary: Uzziah broke down Jabneh's walls after beating the Philistines. It is the same town as Jabneel, and as Jamnia, or Yavne, it became a centre of Jewish learning after the temple fell in 70 AD.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jabneh, a Philistine border town whose walls King Uzziah of Judah broke down after defeating the Philistines (2 Chr. 26:6). It is the same town as Jabneel (Josh. 15:11) and later became known as Jamnia, or Yavne, a center of Jewish scholarship after the Second Temple's destruction in 70 AD.

witness.excerpt: He made an expedition also against the Philistines, and overcame them in battel, and took the cities of Gath and Jabneh,20 and brake down their walls.

entries.title: Jachan (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Gadite chief in Bashan, among the family heads, and nothing further is recorded about him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A chief among the Gadite clans who settled in Bashan, listed among the heads of families in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles 5:13. Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Jachin (A pillar in the temple)
entries.summary: Named twice, in 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles, and nowhere else.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Jachin (Levite living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of 4 men called Jachin. This one is a Levite from the exile and the return, named twice in 1 Chronicles and Nehemiah.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Jachin (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jachin (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: One of the men who went down to Egypt, and a clan is counted from him in the Numbers census. The same name, meaning "he shall establish", was given to one of the temple's two bronze pillars.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Jachin was the name given to one of the two bronze pillars Solomon set up at the entrance of the temple, meaning he shall establish, paired with a second pillar named Boaz.

witness.excerpt:
Simeon and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad,

and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul, the son of the Zephathite  woman--seven.

The one of these pillars he set at the entrance of the porch on the right hand, and called it Jachin (9) and the other at the left hand, and called it Booz.
5.

entries.title: Jachinites (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Jachin's clan, from Simeon's line, counted in the census of Numbers 26.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jachinites were the clan descended from Jachin, one of the sons of Simeon, listed in the Numbers 26 census of Israel's fighting men.

entries.title: Jacob (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Matthew names him twice, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jacob (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.
entries.books: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, Psalm, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel, Hosea, Amos, Obadiah, Micah, Nahum, Malachi
entries.label: 22 books
entries.dictNote: Jacob was Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born grasping his brother Esau's heel, and he later bought Esau's birthright for a bowl of stew and stole his father's dying blessing with his mother's help, forcing him to flee for his life to his uncle Laban in Mesopotamia. There he worked fourteen years for his two wives, Leah and Rachel, fathered the twelve sons who became the tribes of Israel, and on his way back to Canaan wrestled all night with a mysterious figure who renamed him Israel, meaning he struggles with God. Jacob spent his last seventeen years in Egypt after his son Joseph, whom he had long believed dead, turned out to be the country's second-in-command, and he was buried back in Canaan in the family tomb at Machpelah exactly as he had asked.

witness.excerpt: Jacob celebrates the Feast of Tabernacles and offers Tithes.

Now Jacob also, when he understood that foreigners might come, sent all his sons into Egypt to buy corn, for the land of Canaan was grievously afflicted with the famine; and this great misery touched the whole continent.
And Jacob sod lentil pottage, and Esau came from the field hungry.
And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings in the land of Canaan.

entries.title: Jacob (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: In the New Testament the name mostly means the patriarch, set beside Abraham and Isaac, and Luke's angel promises Mary that Jesus will reign "over the house of Jacob forever". Matthew's genealogy also has a Jacob as the father of Joseph.
entries.books: Matthew, Luke, John, Acts, Romans, Hebrews
entries.label: 6 books

witness.excerpt: O Jacob, it is not fit for thee, who art the son of a good father, and grandson of one who had obtained a great reputation for his eminent virtue, to be dejected at thy present circumstances, but to hope for better times, for thou shalt have great abundance of all good things, by my assistance…

entries.lukeNote: Luke's angel tells Mary that Jesus will reign ‘over the house of Jacob forever’ (1:33), the same Jacob paired with Abraham and Isaac as founding-father shorthand later (13:28, 20:37). Josephus's version of the Genesis 28 vision at Bethel has God open with almost a pep talk, don't be dejected at your present circumstances, before the land-and-descendants promise Genesis itself records.

entries.title: Jada (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Onam's son and Shammai's brother, in the Jerahmeelite branch of Judah's family.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jada was a son of Onam and brother of Shammai, listed in the genealogy of the Jerahmeelite branch of Judah's descendants (1 Chronicles 2:28, 32).

entries.title: Jaddua (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jaddua (Priest living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Nehemiah's list of high priests ends with him, among the last priests the Old Testament names.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jaddua was a high priest listed at the end of Nehemiah's priestly genealogy, among the last named in the postexilic period covered by the Old Testament.

witness.excerpt: As in the case of Joseph in Egypt; of Jaddua the High-priest, in the days of Alexander the Great, &c.
Now when John had departed this life, his son Jaddua succeeded in the High Priesthood.

335.] But the elders of Jerusalem, being very uneasy that the brother of Jaddua the High Priest, though married to a foreigner, should be a partner with him in the High Priesthood, quarrelled with him.

entries.title: Jadon (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: He came from Meronoth and worked on Jerusalem's wall beside the men of Gibeon and Mizpah when Nehemiah rebuilt it. Nothing further is recorded about him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A man from Meronoth who helped repair a section of Jerusalem's wall alongside men of Gibeon and Mizpah during Nehemiah's rebuilding project (Neh. 3:7). Nothing further is recorded about him.

witness.excerpt: 8 [The Prophet Jadon]: Not Achias ; as the last editions have it, from one copy.
And as the Prophet [Jadon,8] who came to Jeroboam, when he was offering sacrifice, and when all the people heard him, foretold what would come to pass;9 viz.

So he went up to the altar, with his own priests about him; but when he was going to offer the sacrifices and the burnt-offerings, in the sight of all the people, a prophet, whose name was Jadon, was sent by God, and came to him from Jerusalem, who stood in the midst of the multitude, and in the 'hearing of' the king, and directing his discourse to the altar, said thus: God foretells that there shall be a certa

entries.title: Jael (Woman living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: Sisera ran from the battle to her tent, since her Kenite family was at peace with his king. She gave him milk, let him fall asleep, and drove a tent peg through his head. Deborah had said a woman would get the credit for his death.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jael was the wife of a Kenite whose family had a peace treaty with the Canaanite king Sisera served, and when the defeated Sisera fled to her tent for refuge, she gave him milk and let him fall asleep before driving a tent peg through his head, fulfilling Deborah's prophecy that a woman would get the credit for his death.

witness.excerpt: At last Sisera, as soon as he saw himself beaten, fled away, and came to a woman whose name was Jael , a Kenite; who received him, when he desired to be concealed; and when he asked for somewhat to drink, she gave him sour milk.

entries.title: Jagur
entries.summary: On Judah's southern border, toward the edge of the Negev, and the site has not been found.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A town on the southern border of Judah, toward the edge of the Negev (Joshua 15:21). Its exact site is unidentified.

entries.title: Jah (The Deity)
entries.summary: A short, poetic form of Yahweh, God's covenant name. It turns up mostly in the Psalms, and it is the end of Hallelujah, "praise Yah".
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Jah is a shortened poetic form of God's covenant name, Yahweh, appearing in the Old Testament mainly in the Psalms, including as the second half of the word Hallelujah, meaning praise Yah.

entries.title: Jahath (Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 4 men called Jahath. This one is a Levite from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jahath (Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: A Levite of Gershon's line in Chronicles. The name comes up often in the Levite genealogies, for men of both Gershon and Kohath.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jahath was a common Levitical name in the genealogies of Chronicles, borne by several men descended from Gershon and Kohath.

entries.title: Jahath (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jahath (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jahaz
entries.summary: Moses beat Sihon, the Amorite king, at Jahaz, on the plateau north of the Arnon. The town went to Reuben and then to the Merarite Levites, and because it changed hands with Moab more than once, Isaiah and Jeremiah both name it in their oracles against Moab.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Jahaz, also called Jahaza, Jahazah, or Jahzah, was a town on the plateau north of the Arnon River where Moses defeated Sihon, king of the Amorites, opening the way for Israel's settlement of the region (Numbers 21:23; Deuteronomy 2:32). It fell within the territory of Reuben and was later assigned to the Merarite Levites (Joshua 13:18; 21:36). Isaiah and Jeremiah both cite Jahaz in their oracles against Moab, since the town changed hands more than once during Moab's later conflicts with Israel (Isaiah 15:4; Jeremiah 48:34).

entries.title: Jahaziah (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: When Ezra moved against the foreign marriages, he was one of the few who spoke up against it, or at least against how it was being done; the Hebrew does not make plain which.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of the few men named as raising objections during Ezra's investigation into Israelite men who had married foreign wives after the return from exile (Ezra 10:15). The Hebrew text is ambiguous about whether he and the others named opposed the reform itself or simply thought the process should move more carefully.

entries.title: Jahaziel (Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: A Levite named twice in the Chronicles lists of Levite families, and nothing more is told of him. Another Jahaziel prophesied to Jehoshaphat.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jahaziel was a Levite who prophesied during King Jehoshaphat's crisis, assuring Judah that the battle against the invading Moabite and Ammonite coalition belonged to God, not to them, a promise fulfilled when the invaders destroyed each other.

witness.excerpt: Upon which a certain Prophet, Jahaziel by name, came into the midst of the assembly, and cryed out, and spake both to the multitude, and to the King; that “God heard their prayers, and promised to fight against their enemies.” He also gave order, that the Ki

entries.title: Jahaziel (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 5 men called Jahaziel. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jahaziel (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jahaziel (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A man from the exile and the return. Ezra names him once.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jahaziel (Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a warrior from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jahdiel (Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of the family heads of the half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A chieftain of the half-tribe of Manasseh settled east of the Jordan, named among the heads of families in 1 Chronicles 5:24.

entries.title: Jahdo (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Buz's son and Jeshishai's father, in Gad's family east of the Jordan. Nothing further is known of him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jahdo was a Gadite, son of Buz and father of Jeshishai, listed in the tribal genealogy of Gad east of the Jordan (1 Chronicles 5:14). Nothing further is known of him.

entries.title: Jahleel (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Zebulun's third son, and the Jahleelite clan came from him.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jahleel was the third son of Zebulun and the ancestral head of the Jahleelite clan within that tribe (Genesis 46:14; Numbers 26:26).

witness.excerpt: Zebulon and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel--four.

entries.title: Jahleelites (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Jahleel's clan, from Zebulun, in the wilderness census.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jahleelites were the clan descended from Jahleel, a son of Zebulun, counted among the tribe's families in Israel's wilderness census.

entries.title: Jahmai (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: In David's day he headed a family in the house of Tolah, one of Issachar's clans of fighting men.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A head of a family within the house of Tolah, one of the clans of Issachar counted as fighting men in David's day (1 Chronicles 7:2).

entries.title: Jahzeel (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: The first of Naphtali's four sons, who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household. The Jahzeelites came from him, and nothing else is recorded of him.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jahzeel was the first of Naphtali's four sons who went to Egypt with Jacob's household (Genesis 46:24), and he became ancestor of the Jahzeelite clan counted in the wilderness census (Numbers 26:48). Nothing else is recorded of him.

entries.title: Jahzeelites (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Counted in the census of Numbers 26, the clan that came from Jahzeel, Naphtali's firstborn.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jahzeelites were the clan descended from Jahzeel, the firstborn son of Naphtali, counted in the Numbers 26 census.

entries.title: Jahzerah (Levite living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A priest in the line of those who resettled Jerusalem, Meshullam's son and Adiel's father. Nehemiah's list calls him Ahzai.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A priest in the genealogy of those who resettled Jerusalem after the exile, son of Meshullam and father of Adiel (1 Chronicles 9:12); the parallel list in Nehemiah 11:13 gives the name as Ahzai.

entries.title: Jahziel (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Chronicles spells him this way. He is Naphtali's son, head of a clan, and Genesis and Numbers call him Jahzeel.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Son of Naphtali and head of one of Naphtali's clans (1 Chronicles 7:13), called Jahzeel in the earlier genealogies of Genesis 46 and Numbers 26.

witness.excerpt: And these are the names of the sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shallum, and ‘Îv.  31.

entries.title: Jair
entries.summary: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jair (Judge living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: Judges names him twice, and he is a judge from the years before the monarchy.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jair (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: He judged Israel twenty-two years. His thirty sons rode thirty donkeys and held thirty towns, which says money and reach, not battles won.
entries.label: 5 books
entries.dictNote: Jair was a judge of Israel who governed for twenty-two years and had thirty sons who rode thirty donkeys and controlled thirty towns, a detail highlighting his considerable wealth and influence rather than any recorded military deliverance.

witness.excerpt: Now it was that Jair the Gileadite, of the tribe of Manasseh, took the government.

entries.title: Jair (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: A man from the exile and the return, and Esther is the only book that names him.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jair (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Not the judge, and not Jair of Gilead. This Jair was father of Elhanan, the warrior of David's who killed Lahmi, Goliath's brother.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Distinct from the better-known Jair of Gilead and the judge of Israel, this Jair was the father of Elhanan, one of David's warriors who killed Lahmi, the brother of the giant Goliath, in a battle against the Philistines (1 Chronicles 20:5).

entries.title: Jairite (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Ira, who served David as a priest or chief officer, carries this label, which ties him to Jair. He closes the list of David's court officials, after Joab, Benaiah and Jehoshaphat the recorder.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jairite marks Ira, who served David as a priest or royal chief officer, as a descendant of Jair. He appears in the closing list of David's court officials in 2 Samuel 20:23-26, alongside Joab, Benaiah, and Jehoshaphat the recorder.

entries.title: Jairus (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: He ran the synagogue at Capernaum, and his twelve-year-old daughter was dying. Jesus was held up on the way, word came that she was dead, and he went to the house anyway and raised her.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jairus was a ruler of the synagogue at Capernaum whose twelve-year-old daughter was dying when he came to Jesus for help. While Jesus was delayed healing a woman on the way, word came that the girl had died, but Jesus went to the house anyway and raised her (Mark 5:21-43; Luke 8:41-56).

witness.excerpt: A few there were of them who privately escaped to Masada, among whom was Eleazar, the son of Jairus, who was of kin to Manahem, and acted the part of a tyrant at Masada afterward.

entries.title: Jakeh (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Agur's father, and Agur's sayings make up Proverbs 30. Nothing else about Jakeh is recorded.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jakeh appears only as the father of Agur, whose sayings make up Proverbs 30. Nothing else about him is recorded in scripture, and Agur's own identity and homeland (possibly Massa, an Arabian tribe) remain debated among scholars.

entries.title: Jakim (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jakim (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Benjamite family head living in Jerusalem, in the Chronicles genealogy.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jakim was the priest who headed the twelfth of the twenty-four priestly divisions David organized for temple service (1 Chronicles 24:12). A separate Jakim was a Benjamite family head living in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 8:19-21). The King James margin at Matthew 1:11 also uses “Jakim” as an alternate rendering of Jehoiakim.

entries.title: Jalam (Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Esau's son by Oholibamah, whose descendants became one of Edom's clans.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jalam was a son of Esau by his wife Oholibamah, and his descendants became a clan chief among the Edomites.

entries.title: Jalon (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Last of the four sons of Ezra in Judah's genealogy, and nothing further is known of him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jalon was the last of four sons of Ezra listed in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles 4:17. Nothing further is known about him.

entries.title: Jambres (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Paul names Jannes and Jambres as the men who opposed Moses, and so a warning about anyone who resists the truth. Exodus has Pharaoh's magicians copy some of the signs but never names them; the names come from Jewish tradition.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jambres, along with Jannes, was one of two Egyptian magicians tradition names as having opposed Moses before Pharaoh, replicating some of the plague signs through their secret arts (compare Exodus 7:11, 22). Paul cites the pair by name in 2 Timothy 3:8 as an example of men who oppose the truth, drawing on a tradition current among Jewish teachers though not recorded by name in the Old Testament text itself.

witness.excerpt: Bernard informs us here, that instead of this single priest or prophet of the Egyptians, without a name in Josephus, the Targum of Jonathan names the two famous antagonists of Moses, Jannes and Jambres.

entries.title: James (Apostle living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Zebedee's son and John's older brother. He was one of the three closest to Jesus, and the first of the twelve to be killed, by Herod Agrippa the First.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Two apostles named James appear among the twelve. James the son of Zebedee, John's older brother, was part of Jesus's inner circle and became the first apostle martyred, executed by Herod Agrippa the First. A different James, the son of Alphaeus, is listed among the twelve but otherwise unmentioned in the Gospels. A third James, Jesus's own half-brother, did not believe in him during his ministry but became a leading figure in the Jerusalem church after the resurrection and is traditionally credited with writing the New Testament letter of James.

witness.excerpt: James affirm, that this drought lasted in all three years and six months.
James, 5:12; but all admit of particular exceptions for solemn causes, and on great and necessary occasions.
2, than his slaughter of James the brother of John, and his imprisonment of Peter, or his vain-glorious behavior before he died, both in Acts 12:13; and here, ch.
4 The names of those sons were James and Simon : whom Alexander commanded to be crucified.

entries.title: James (Apostle living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Alphaeus's son, one of the twelve, and the Gospels say almost nothing else about him.
entries.label: 3 books

entries.title: James (Father of an apostle living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: A man from the New Testament, named twice across Luke and Acts.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: James (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: The brother of Jesus. He did not believe during the ministry, then led the Jerusalem church after the resurrection, and the letter of James is traditionally his.
entries.books: Matthew, Mark, Acts, 1 Corinthians, Galatians, James, Jude
entries.label: 7 books

entries.title: Jamin (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jamin (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: One of Simeon's sons, in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers and Chronicles. The name was common.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Jamin was a common name, borne by a son of Simeon and by a Levite who helped explain the law to the people after Ezra's public reading.

witness.excerpt:
Simeon and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad,

and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul, the son of the Zephathite  woman--seven.

entries.title: Jamin (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Jamin. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jamlech (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A chief of Simeon's clans. Nothing else is recorded about him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A chief man of the tribe of Simeon listed among the clan heads in 1 Chronicles 4:34. Nothing else is recorded about him.

entries.title: Janna (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: In Luke's genealogy of Jesus, between Joseph and Melchi. Some manuscripts spell it Jannai.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: An ancestor of Jesus listed in Luke's genealogy, between Joseph and Melchi (Luke 3:24); some manuscripts and the Revised Version spell the name Jannai.

entries.title: Jannes (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: The other of the two Egyptian magicians who stood against Moses before Pharaoh. Exodus does not name either, and Paul takes the names from a well-known tradition.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: One of two Egyptian magicians, remembered in later Jewish tradition as Jannes and Jambres, who imitated Moses's signs before Pharaoh and opposed him, according to 2 Timothy 3:8. Neither man is actually named in Exodus itself; Paul draws on a well-known tradition as an example of false teachers who resist the truth.

witness.excerpt: Bernard informs us here, that instead of this single priest or prophet of the Egyptians, without a name in Josephus, the Targum of Jonathan names the two famous antagonists of Moses, Jannes and Jambres.

entries.title: Janoah
entries.summary: Named once, in 2 Kings, and nowhere else.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Janoah
entries.summary: On Ephraim's northeastern border, in the Jordan Valley. It is identified with the village of Yanun, southeast of Nablus.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Janoah names two different towns. One lay on the northeastern border of Ephraim, in the Jordan Valley, identified with the modern village of Yanun southeast of Nablus (Josh. 16:6-7). The other was a town in Naphtali, in the north, captured by Tiglath-pileser III of Assyria along with Galilee and Gilead during his campaign against Israel under King Pekah, an event corroborated by Tiglath-pileser's own royal inscriptions listing his conquests in the Levant (2 Kings 15:29).

entries.title: Janum (Janim)
entries.summary: A hill-country town of Judah near Hebron, listed with Beth-tappuah and Aphekah and never mentioned again.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Janum, a town in the hill country of Judah near Hebron, listed among towns such as Beth-tappuah and Aphekah in Joshua 15:53. It is not mentioned again and its site is unidentified.

entries.title: Japha (Joppa)
entries.summary: The Hebrew name for Joppa, the port that is Jaffa today. Solomon's cedar came in by sea there, and so did Ezra's timber for the second temple, and Jonah sailed from it toward Tarshish. The Amarna letters already mention its guarded gate.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Japho is the Hebrew name for the port city better known by its Greek form, Joppa (modern Jaffa, now part of Tel Aviv). Solomon's cedar for the temple, and later Ezra's timber for the second temple, arrived by sea at Joppa before being hauled up to Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 2:16; Ezra 3:7). It also marked the tribal border of Dan (Joshua 19:46) and was the port Jonah fled through toward Tarshish. Egyptian records from the Amarna archive already mention a guarded gate of Joppa centuries earlier, showing the city's long standing as a coastal gateway.

witness.excerpt: But still Joppa stood in his way, and hindered his going thither; for it was necessary to take that city first, which was in the enemies' hands, that when he should go to Jerusalem, no fortress might be left in the enemies' power behin
Strato's Tower, and Sebaste, and Joppa, and Jerusalem; but as to the Grecian cities, Gaza, and Gadara, and Hippos, he cut them off from the kingdom, and added them to Syria.
However, its breadth is extended from the river Jordan to Joppa.
But he went not, out of fear: nay he ran away from God to the city of Joppa: and finding a ship there, he went into it, and sailed to Tarsus, in Cilicia. .
After which he came to Ascalon, and thence to Jamnia, and after that to Joppa, and from Joppa to Cesarea: having taken a resolution to gather all his other forces together at that place.

entries.title: Japheth (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Noah's son. With Shem he covered their drunken father without looking, and Noah asked God to enlarge Japheth's territory. Genesis 10 traces his descendants to the peoples of Asia Minor and the Aegean.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Japheth was Noah's third son, and along with his brother Shem he respectfully covered their father's nakedness without looking, earning Noah's blessing that God would enlarge Japheth's territory. Genesis 10 traces his descendants to peoples associated with Asia Minor and the regions around the Aegean.

witness.excerpt: Japheth, and in the fourth year he begat a son, and called his name Shelah;  for he said: "Truly I have been sent."  6.
And Japheth also divided the land of his inheritance amongst his sons.

And Japheth and his sons went towards the sea and dwelt in the land of their portion, and Madai saw the land of the sea and it did not please him, and he begged a (portion) from Elam and Asshur and Arpachshad,

And Shem took his garment and arose, he and Japheth, and they placed the garment on their shoulders and went backward and covered the shame of their father, and their faces were backward.  10.
Ham, and in the first year in the sixth week she bare him Japheth.

entries.title: Japhia
entries.summary: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Japhia (David's son living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: Born to David in Jerusalem, and sharing his name with a king of Lachish and a town of Zebulun.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Japhia is a name shared by a place and two men. It names a town on the southern border of Zebulun near Nazareth (Joshua 19:12); a king of Lachish who joined the Amorite coalition against Joshua and was defeated and killed (Joshua 10:3, 5); and a son born to David in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:15).

entries.title: Japhia (King living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: Joshua names him once, and he is a king from the years before the monarchy.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Japhlet (Man living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: From Asher through Beriah, and head of the Japhletite clan. Nothing else is known of him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Japhlet was a descendant of Asher through Beriah and the head of a family clan within the tribe, the Japhletites (1 Chronicles 7:32-33). Nothing else is known of him.

entries.title: Japhleti (Man living before Israel's Monarchy)
entries.summary: A border mark in Joshua 16:3, "the border of the Japhletite", on the edge of Ephraim's land. The clan is otherwise unknown and was probably Canaanite.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Not a person but a clan or territorial name: "the border of the Japhletite" marks a boundary point in the description of Ephraim and Manasseh's territorial allotment in Joshua 16:3. The Japhletites are otherwise unknown, and the name likely designated a local Canaanite clan whose territory bordered the tribal land.

entries.title: Jarah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Saul's line runs through Jonathan and Mephibosheth to Micah, and Jarah is Micah's son. The other copy of the list calls him Jehoadah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jarah was a descendant of Saul through Jonathan and Mephibosheth, the son of Micah in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 9:42. The parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 8:36 lists the same figure as Jehoadah, evidence of scribal variation in transmitting Benjamite names.

entries.title: Jareb (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Hosea twice has Israel running to "King Jareb" for help against its troubles, and the help never comes. It is probably not a name at all but a title for the king of Assyria, something like "the great king".
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jareb is not a personal name but an obscure Hebrew phrase, traditionally rendered “King Jareb,” that appears twice in Hosea describing Israel's futile appeals to Assyria for help (Hosea 5:13; 10:6). Most modern scholars read it as an epithet for the Assyrian king, something like “a king who contends” or “the great king,” rather than a proper name, so it likely refers to Tiglath-pileser III or the Assyrian monarchy in general rather than to a specific named individual.

entries.title: Jared (Man living at the time before the Flood)
entries.summary: Enoch's father, in Seth's line down to Noah, and he lived nine hundred sixty-two years.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Jared was a descendant of Seth in the genealogy leading to Noah, father of Enoch, and Genesis records his lifespan as nine hundred sixty-two years.

witness.excerpt: Now Jared was the son of Enoch: whose son was Malaliel: whose son was Mathusela: whose son was Lamech.

And they were in all two hundred; who descended in the days of Jared on the summit of Mount Hermon, and they called it Mount Hermon, because they had sworn and bound themselves by mutual imprecations upon it.

Now he was the tenth from Adam: as being the son of Lamech: whose father was Mathusala: he was the son of Enoch, the son of Jared: and Jared was the son of Malaleel : who, with many of his sisters, were the children of Cain[an], the son of Enos.

said unto him: ‘The Lord will do a new thing on
the earth, and this I have already seen in a vision,
and make known to thee that in the generation of
my father Jared some of the angels of heaven transgressed
the word of the Lord.

entries.title: Jaresiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Benjamite family head, descended from Jeroham.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Benjamite descendant of Jeroham, listed among the heads of families in the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles 8:27.

entries.title: Jarha (Egyptian living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Sheshan had no sons. He gave his daughter to Jarha, his Egyptian servant, to keep the line going. Their descendants run on for generations in Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jarha was an Egyptian servant of Sheshan, a descendant of Judah who had no sons. Sheshan gave Jarha his daughter in marriage to preserve the family line, and their descendants are traced several generations forward in Chronicles, eventually including Zabad, one of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 2:34-35; 11:41).

entries.title: Jarib (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Ezra sent a Jarib, one of the leaders, to recruit Levites for the return. Chronicles lists a second man of the name in a genealogy.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jarib was a common name, borne by a leader Ezra sent to recruit Levites for the return journey and by a priest confronted for a foreign marriage.

entries.title: Jarib (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Ezra names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jarmuth
entries.summary: Its king joined the march on Gibeon after Gibeon made peace with Israel, and Joshua beat them in the battle where the sun stood still.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jarmuth was a Canaanite city whose king joined a coalition against Gibeon after Gibeon made peace with Israel, a coalition Joshua defeated in the battle where the sun stood still.

entries.title: Jarmuth
entries.summary: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jaroah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: They list him among the chiefs of Gad in Bashan, and nothing else is recorded of him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A chief of the tribe of Gad listed among the leading families of that tribe settled in the land of Bashan (1 Chronicles 5:14). Nothing else is recorded of him.

entries.title: Jashen (Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: His sons fought among David's mighty men, and Chronicles calls him Hashem.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jashen was the father of several warriors in David's elite fighting force, listed among his mighty men (2 Sam. 23:32); he is called Hashem in the parallel list at 1 Chronicles 11:34.

entries.title: Jashobeam (Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Chief of David's three greatest warriors, credited with killing three hundred men in one fight.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jashobeam was the chief of David's three mightiest warriors, credited with killing three hundred men in a single encounter.

entries.title: Jashobeam (Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a warrior from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jashub (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Issachar's son, and his clan was counted in the census of Numbers.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jashub was a son of Issachar, and also the name of a man confronted for a foreign marriage under Ezra.

entries.title: Jashub (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Ezra names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jashubi-lehem (Bethlehem)
entries.summary: Older dictionaries could not decide whether this is a man or a place, "those who returned to Lehem". It sits in the genealogy of Judah through Shelah, and modern translations mostly read it as a place.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A name in the genealogy of Judah's descendants through Shelah, so obscure that older dictionaries debated whether it names a person or records a place, those who returned to Lehem (1 Chronicles 4:22). Modern translations generally treat it as tied to a place or event referenced in that verse rather than as an individual's name.

entries.title: Jashubites (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Jashub's clan, of Issachar, counted in Numbers 26. The King James has him as Job in Genesis 46:13.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jashubites were the clan descended from Jashub, a son of Issachar, counted in the Numbers 26 census; the same name appears as Job in the King James rendering of Genesis 46:13.

entries.title: Jason (Man living at the time of the New Testament)
entries.summary: Paul and Silas stayed with him in Thessalonica. When a mob came for Paul and could not find him, they dragged Jason before the city officials instead, charging him with harbouring men who defied Caesar's decrees, and he had to post bond to go free.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jason was a believer in Thessalonica who hosted Paul and Silas, and when a mob unable to find Paul dragged Jason before the city officials instead, accusing him of harboring men who defied Caesar's decrees, Jason had to post bond before being released.

entries.title: Jathniel (Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Meshelemiah's fourth son, a Korahite Levite, and one of the gatekeepers at the temple's entrances under David.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Korahite Levite, the fourth son of Meshelemiah, listed among the gatekeepers assigned to guard the temple's entrances under David (1 Chr. 26:2).

entries.title: Jattir
entries.summary: A priests' town in the hill country of Judah, given to Aaron's line. David sent its elders a share of the Amalekite plunder, as he did for many towns while he was on the run. It is identified with Khirbet Attir, south of Hebron.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Jattir was a town in the hill country of Judah assigned to the priestly line of Aaron among the Levitical cities (Joshua 15:48; 21:14). David sent part of the plunder taken from the Amalekites to its elders as a gift, one of many towns he cultivated as allies during his fugitive years (1 Samuel 30:27-31). It is identified with the ruin Khirbet Attir, south of Hebron.

entries.title: Javan (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Japheth's fourth son in the table of nations. The Hebrews took his descendants to be the Ionians, the Greek world, and the prophets use Javan to mean Greece and its merchants. Modern Hebrew still calls Greece by the name.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: In the table of nations, Javan is the fourth son of Japheth, whose descendants the Hebrews identified with the Ionians and, more broadly, the Greek world (Genesis 10:2, 4). The prophets use "Javan" as shorthand for Greece and its merchants (Isaiah 66:19; Ezekiel 27:13, 19), and the name survives in modern Hebrew as the word for Greece itself.

witness.excerpt: And for Javan  came forth the fourth portion every island  and the islands which are towards the border of Lud.
Now as to Javan and Madai, the sons of Japhet; from Madai came the Madeans, who are called Medes, by the Greeks; but from Javan, Jonia, and all the Grecians are derived.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer and Magog and Madai and Javan, Tubal and Meshech and Tiras: these are 1324-1372 A.M.

entries.title: Jaziz (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: King David's flocks were his to look after, and he was a Hagrite.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jaziz was a Hagrite who oversaw King David's flocks, one of the officials in charge of royal property listed in 1 Chronicles 27:31.

entries.title: Jearim (Chesalon)
entries.summary: A wooded ridge on Judah's northern border. The name means "forests", and it lives on in Kirjath-jearim, "city of forests", the town nearby.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A hill or wooded ridge on the northern border of Judah's territory (Joshua 15:10). Its name, meaning "forests," is preserved in the fuller place name Kirjath-jearim, "city of forests," the town that stood near it.

entries.title: Jeaterai (Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Zerah's son, a Gershonite Levite, in the genealogy of Chronicles. Nothing further is recorded of him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jeaterai was a Gershonite Levite, son of Zerah, listed in the Levitical genealogy of 1 Chronicles 6. Nothing further is recorded of him.

entries.title: Jeberechiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: When Isaiah wrote on a tablet in the days of Ahaz, he took Jeberechiah's son Zechariah as a witness.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Father of a Zechariah whom Isaiah took as a witness when the prophet inscribed a tablet during the reign of King Ahaz (Isaiah 8:2).

entries.title: Jebus (Jerusalem)
entries.summary: What Jerusalem was called while the Jebusites held it. David took it and made it his capital.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jebus was the pre-conquest name for Jerusalem while it was still held by the Jebusites, before David captured it and made it his capital.

entries.title: Jecholiah (Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Amaziah's wife and Uzziah's mother, a woman of Jerusalem. Her son came to the throne at sixteen and reigned over fifty years. Nothing further is recorded of her.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jecholiah was the wife of King Amaziah of Judah and mother of his successor, Uzziah (also called Azariah), who came to the throne at sixteen and reigned for over fifty years (2 Kings 15:2; 2 Chronicles 26:3). Chronicles names her hometown as Jerusalem. Otherwise nothing further is recorded of her.

entries.title: Jechonias (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: The Greek form of Jeconiah, the king of Judah taken to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar after three months on the throne. Matthew's genealogy turns on him at the exile. Babylonian ration tablets list food for "Yaukin, king of the land of Yahud" and his sons.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jechonias is the Greek form of Jeconiah, also called Jehoiachin, the young king of Judah exiled to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar after a three-month reign (2 Kings 24:8-15); Matthew's genealogy lists him at the pivotal generation marking the exile (Matthew 1:11-12). Babylonian ration tablets excavated in the city and dated to Nebuchadnezzar's reign list regular food allotments for “Yaukin, king of the land of Yahud” and his sons, confirming that the exiled king was kept alive and provided for at the Babylonian court, exactly as 2 Kings 25:27-30 describes decades later. Jeremiah had pronounced a curse that none of his descendants would sit on David's throne (Jeremiah 22:30), a tension Matthew resolves by tracing Jesus' legal, not biological, throne-right through Joseph rather than a reigning bloodline.

entries.title: Jeconiah (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Another name for Jehoiachin, the king of Judah carried off to Babylon. In the end a Babylonian king let him out and gave him a seat at the royal table.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Jeconiah is an alternate name for Jehoiachin, the king of Judah taken captive to Babylon and later released to a place of honor at the Babylonian king's table, covered more fully under the entry for Jehoiachin.

entries.title: Jedaiah (Levite living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: The name was common among priests after the exile. Several who came back from Babylon and served in the rebuilt temple carried it.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jedaiah was a common priestly name in the postexilic period, borne by several priests who returned from Babylonian exile and served in the rebuilt temple.

entries.title: Jedaiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: The second priestly division in Chronicles carries his name, and his descendants are counted among the priests who came back from Babylon.
entries.label: 3 books

entries.dictNote: Jediael was a common name among David's warriors and Benjamite clan leaders listed in the genealogies of Chronicles.

entries.title: Jedidah (Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Amon's wife, and mother of Josiah, the king who reformed Judah more thoroughly than almost anyone.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Wife of King Amon of Judah and mother of Josiah, remembered as one of Judah's most thoroughgoing religious reformers (2 Kings 22:1).

witness.excerpt: His mother was of the city of Boscath; and her name was Jedidah.

entries.title: Jedidiah (King living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: "Beloved of the LORD." Nathan gave the baby Solomon this name at God's direction, right after the story of David and Bathsheba and the death of their first child, but Solomon is the name that stuck.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: The name the prophet Nathan gave to the infant Solomon at God's direction, meaning "beloved of the LORD" (2 Sam. 12:25). It marks God's favor toward Solomon immediately after the account of David's sin with Bathsheba and the death of their first child, though "Solomon" remained the name history remembered him by.

entries.title: Jeduthun (Levite living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles and Nehemiah name him twice, and he is a Levite from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Jeduthun (Singer living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: David put three chief musicians over temple worship, Heman, Asaph and Jeduthun. Several psalms carry Jeduthun's name in their headings.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Jeduthun was one of the three chief musicians David appointed over temple worship, alongside Heman and Asaph, and several psalms carry his name in their superscriptions as a musical or performance notation.

entries.title: Jeezer (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Head of the Jeezerite clan among the Manassites in the wilderness census. Elsewhere the name is Abiezer, and Gideon came from that clan.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Head of the Manassite clan of the Jeezerites counted in the wilderness census (Numbers 26:30); the same name appears elsewhere as Abiezer, the fuller form from which Gideon's own clan later descended (Judges 6:11).

entries.title: Jegar-Sahadutha (Ramoth-gilead)
entries.summary: Laban's Aramaic name for the heap of stones he and Jacob raised in Gilead to witness their covenant. Jacob called it Galeed. Both names mean "heap of witness".
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jegar-sahadutha is not a person but the Aramaic name Laban gave to the heap of stones he and Jacob raised as a witness to their covenant in Gilead (Genesis 31:47). Jacob gave the same monument a Hebrew name, Galeed, meaning the same thing: "heap of witness."

entries.title: Jehalellel (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: The name means "praise God". This one is in Judah's genealogy; another was a Levite whose sons helped cleanse the temple under Hezekiah.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jehalellel (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: The name means praise God. This one is a Levite whose sons helped clean out the temple.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jehalellel's name means “praise God.” One man of this name appears in the tribe of Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 4:16). A second Jehalellel was a Levite whose sons helped lead the purification of the temple under King Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 29:12).

entries.title: Jehdai (Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Six sons are credited to Jehdai in the genealogy of Judah, through Caleb's line.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jehdai, also spelled Jahdai, was a descendant of Caleb through the line of Ezrah, listed as the father of six sons in the tribal genealogy of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:47).

entries.title: Jehdeiah (Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Levite from Shubael's line, given a division of temple service under David. Another Jehdeiah, a Meronothite, looked after the royal donkeys.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Jehdeiah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He looks after the donkeys on the royal estates. The other Jehdeiah is a Levite in David's temple rota.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jehdeiah's name means “he who rejoices in the LORD.” One Jehdeiah was a Levite descended from Shubael who was assigned to a division of temple service under David (1 Chronicles 24:20). A second Jehdeiah, a Meronothite, was in charge of the donkeys used in David and Solomon's royal service (1 Chronicles 27:30).

entries.title: Jehiah (Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He kept the door for the ark, with Obed-edom, when David brought it to Jerusalem.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jehiah was one of the doorkeepers appointed to guard the ark of the covenant when David brought it to Jerusalem, along with Obed-edom (1 Chronicles 15:24). The role placed him among the Levites David organized for tabernacle service ahead of Solomon's temple.

entries.title: Jehiel (Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of the temple musicians David appointed when the ark came up, playing before it. The name was common in Levitical families in Chronicles.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jehiel was a common Levitical name in Chronicles, borne by several temple musicians and officials serving under David and later kings.

entries.title: Jehieli (Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Gershonite Levite from Ladan's line. He and his brother Zetham kept the temple treasuries under David, the gifts and spoils set aside for the house of the LORD, and nothing further is recorded about him.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jehieli was a Gershonite Levite descended from Ladan, head of a family placed in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD under David (1 Chronicles 26:21-22). He and his brother Zetham administered the dedicated gifts and spoils brought in for the temple's future construction. Nothing further is recorded about him.

entries.title: Jehoada (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: In Saul's line through Jonathan and Mephibosheth, the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth and Zimri. The other copy of the list calls him Jarah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A descendant of Saul through Jonathan and Mephibosheth, listed in Benjamin's genealogy as the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri (1 Chronicles 8:36). The parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 9:42 calls the same man Jarah.

entries.title: Jehoaddan (Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Jehoash's wife, and Amaziah's mother. She came from Jerusalem, and the record gives her the brief notice most queen mothers of Judah get.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Jehoaddan, also called Jehoaddin, was the wife of King Jehoash of Judah and the mother of his successor, King Amaziah; she is identified as a native of Jerusalem (2 Kings 14:2; 2 Chronicles 25:1). Scripture records nothing further about her, typical of the brief, formulaic queen-mother notices given for most kings of Judah.

entries.title: Jehoahaz (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: King of northern Israel, and a weak one, worn down by Aramean pressure through his reign.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: At least two kings named Jehoahaz appear in the Old Testament, one a brief and militarily weakened ruler of northern Israel under Aramean pressure; the other a son of Josiah who reigned in Judah for only three months before the Egyptian pharaoh Necho deposed him and took him captive to Egypt, where he died.

witness.excerpt: As also how Neco carried Jehoahaz , who had been made King, into Egypt , and delivered the Kingdom to Jehoiakim .

entries.title: Jehoahaz (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Josiah's son. He reigned in Judah three months before Pharaoh Necho deposed him and took him to Egypt, where he died.
entries.label: 2 books

entries.title: Jehoash (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Joash under a longer spelling: the king of Judah hidden from Athaliah as a child.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Jehoash is an alternate form of the name Joash, covered under that entry; it refers to a king of Judah hidden from Athaliah as a child and a king of Israel who defeated the Arameans and later Judah's King Amaziah.

witness.excerpt: Jehoash , the King of Jerusalem , at first is careful about the worship of God; but afterwards becomes impious, and commands Zechariah to be stoned.

But when he came to the management of affairs, and to the government, he resolved that he ought first of all to avenge his father Jehoash; and to punish those his friends that had laid violent hands upon him.

entries.title: Jehoash (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: The king of Israel who beat the Arameans and then beat Amaziah, king of Judah. Jehoash is the longer form of Joash.

entries.dictNote: Jehohanan was a common priestly and military name, including a temple gatekeeper under David and a military commander under Jehoshaphat.
