entries.title: Zichri (Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A common name. This one is an Ephraimite warrior who killed a son of King Ahaz in the war between Israel and Judah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zichri was a common Old Testament name, borne by several military officers, Levites, and officials, including an Ephraimite warrior who killed a son of King Ahaz during a war between Israel and Judah.

entries.title: Ziddim
entries.summary: A walled town of Naphtali, listed with Hazor, Rakkath and Kinnereth. Some place it near the Sea of Galilee.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ziddim, a fortified town of Naphtali listed in Joshua 19:35 alongside Hazor, Rakkath, and Kinnereth. It appears only in this one boundary list and its exact site is not known with certainty, though some place it near the Sea of Galilee.

entries.title: Zif (Name of the 2nd month)
entries.summary: Second month, meaning brightness or blossoming, later called Iyar. It dates the start and the finish of Solomon's temple and nothing else.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zif is not a person but the name of the second month of the ancient Hebrew calendar, meaning “brightness” or “blossoming,” later called Iyar; it is used only to date the start of Solomon's temple construction, in the fourth year of his reign, and its completion seven years later (1 Kings 6:1, 37). The month falls roughly in April and May.

entries.title: Ziha (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Head of a family of temple servants that came back from exile.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ziha was the head of a family of temple servants among the returning exiles, listed in both Ezra and Nehemiah's records.

entries.title: Ziha (Man living at the time of Exile and Return)
entries.summary: Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ziklag
entries.summary: Achish of Gath gave this town in the Negev to David while he was running from Saul, and David lived there more than a year. Amalekites burned it while he was away and took the women and children, and he went after them and got everyone back.
entries.label: 5 books
entries.dictNote: Ziklag was a town in the Negev assigned to Judah and Simeon that fell under Philistine control; King Achish of Gath gave it to David as a base during his flight from Saul, and David used it as his home for over a year. While David's men were away, Amalekite raiders burned Ziklag and carried off the women and children, prompting David's pursuit and recovery of the captives. It was at Ziklag that David received news of Saul and Jonathan's deaths at Gilboa. Archaeologists led by Yosef Garfinkel have proposed Khirbet a-Ra'i, between Kiryat Gat and Lachish, as the site of Ziklag, based on a destruction layer and finds dated to the time of David, though the identification is contested by other scholars.

witness.excerpt: So Achish gave him a certain village, called Ziklag : which place David and his sons were fond of when he was King, and reckoned it to be their peculiar inheritance.
THIS fight proved to be on the same day whereon David was come back to Ziklag, after he had overcome the Amalekites.

I have given thee, without suspecting any harm: and there keep my countrey: lest any of our enemies should make an incursion upon it: which will be one part of that assistance which I expect from thee.” So David came to Ziklag, as the King of Gath bid him.

entries.title: Zillah (Woman living at the time before the Flood)
entries.summary: Lamech's second wife, in Cain's line, and mother of Tubal-cain, who forged tools of bronze and iron.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zillah was one of Lamech's two wives in Cain's genealogical line, and the mother of Tubal-cain, remembered as an early forger of bronze and iron tools.

entries.title: Zilpah (Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Leah's servant. In the contest between Leah and Rachel for sons she was given to Jacob, and she bore him Gad and Asher.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zilpah was Leah's servant, given to Jacob as a secondary wife in the competition between Leah and Rachel to produce sons, and she became the mother of Gad and Asher.

witness.excerpt: And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's handmaid, the wife of Jacob, whom she bore unto Jacob, Gad and Asher.
And Joseph told our father that the sons of Zilpah and Bilhah were slaying the best of the flock and eating them against the judgement of Reuben and Judah.

And Laban made a feast, and took Leah his elder daughter, and gave (her) to Jacob as a wife, and gave her Zilpah his handmaid for an handmaid; and Jacob did not know, for he thought that she was Rachel.

And he was taken captive and was bought by Laban; and he gave him Euna his handmaid to wife, and she bore a daughter, and called her name Zilpah, after the name 12 of the village in which he had been taken captive.

entries.title: Zilthai (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Zilthai (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: The name means shadow of the LORD. This one headed a Benjamite family in 1 Chronicles 8:20.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zilthai's name means “shadow of the LORD.” One Zilthai was a Benjamite family head (1 Chronicles 8:20). A second Zilthai was a captain from the tribe of Manasseh who defected to join David's forces at Ziklag while David was still fleeing Saul (1 Chronicles 12:20).

entries.title: Zimmah (Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Levite in Gershon's line, named in the Chronicles genealogies.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zimmah was a common Levitical name among the descendants of Gershon listed in the genealogies of Chronicles.

entries.title: Zimmah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Zimran (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Abraham's son by Keturah. He is generally taken as the father of an Arabian tribe that nobody can now identify.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Zimran was a son of Abraham by his wife Keturah, generally taken as the ancestor of an Arabian tribe, though the tribe cannot be identified with certainty (Genesis 25:2; 1 Chronicles 1:32).

entries.title: Zimri
entries.summary: Named once, in Jeremiah, and nowhere else.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Zimri (King living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: He killed King Elah of Israel and took the throne, and lasted seven days. The army made its own commander king, and Zimri burned the palace down over himself rather than be taken.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Zimri assassinated King Elah of Israel and seized the throne, only to reign seven days before the army proclaimed a rival commander king instead; Zimri burned the palace down around himself rather than be captured.

witness.excerpt: Even Zimri, the head of the tribe of Simeon, accompanied with Cozbi, a Midianitish women, who was the daughter of Sur; a man of authority in that countrey: and being desired by his wife to disregard the laws of Moses, and to follo
Of which Phineas we made mention a little before, as he that had guarded the laws of the Hebrews, and had inflicted punishment upon Zimri, when he had transgressed them.

entries.title: Zimri (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him twice, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Zimri (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: One of 4 men called Zimri. This one is a man from the wilderness years, named once in Numbers.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Zin
entries.summary: The Wilderness of Zin, where Kadesh lay. Miriam died there, and there Moses struck the rock in anger when he had been told to speak to it.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: The Wilderness of Zin was a desert region Israel passed through during their wilderness wanderings, the site of Kadesh, where Miriam died and where Moses struck the rock in anger instead of speaking to it.

entries.title: Zina (Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: A Gershonite Levite, Shimei's son, one of the family heads David organized for the temple. The next verse calls him Zizah.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zina was one of the sons of Shimei, a Levite of the Gershonite line, listed among the Levitical family heads David organized for temple service (1 Chronicles 23:10). The next verse calls him Zizah, likely a variant spelling of the same name.

entries.title: Zion (Jerusalem)
entries.summary: The fortified hill on Jerusalem's southeastern ridge that David took from the Jebusites and called the city of David. He built his palace there. Archaeologists have uncovered the Stepped Stone Structure on that ridge, and many tie it to David's time.
entries.books: 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Psalm, Song of Solomon, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Joel, Amos, Obadiah, Micah, Zephaniah, Zechariah
entries.label: 16 books
entries.dictNote: Zion was originally the fortified hill on Jerusalem's southeastern ridge that David captured from the Jebusites and made his capital, building his palace there and giving it the name “the city of David.” Excavations on this ridge have exposed a massive Stepped Stone Structure and an adjoining Large Stone Structure that many archaeologists link to fortifications from David's era, along with tunnels including Warren's Shaft and Hezekiah's Tunnel. Later biblical writers extended the name to cover all of Jerusalem, then Israel as God's chosen people, and New Testament writers apply it to the church and to the heavenly city.

witness.excerpt: And he knew that the Garden of Eden is the holy of holies, and the dwelling of the Lord, and Mount Sinai the centre of the desert, and Mount Zion--the centre of the navel of the earth: these three  were created as holy places facing each other.

28.  And the Lord will appear to the eyes

of all,  and all will know that I am the God of Israel and the Father of all the children of Jacob,  and King on Mount Zion  for all eternity.

For the Lord hath four places  on the earth, the Garden of Eden, and the Mount of the East,  and this mountain on which thou art this day, Mount Sinai, and Mount Zion (which) will be sanctified in the new creation for a sanctification of the earth; through it will the earth be sanctified from all (its) guilt and its uncleanness throughout the generations of the world.  27.

entries.title: Zior
entries.summary: In the hill country of Judah near Hebron, named once, and commonly identified with es-Sa'ir northeast of Hebron.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zior, a town in the hill country of Judah near Hebron, listed in Joshua 15:54. It occurs only this once in scripture and is commonly identified with the modern village of es-Sa'ir northeast of Hebron.

entries.title: Ziph
entries.summary: David hid in the wilderness around Ziph, southeast of Hebron, while Saul was hunting him. The people of Ziph told Saul where he was, twice.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Ziph was a town in the hill country of Judah southeast of Hebron whose surrounding wilderness gave David refuge while he fled from Saul. The Ziphites twice betrayed David's location to Saul, prompting psalms that reflect on that betrayal. A second, smaller Ziph lay further south in the Negev, and the name also recurs among Judah's genealogies.

witness.excerpt: Then David removed thence, and came to a certain place called the New Place , belonging to Ziph .

Now Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, who, as we said before, was king of the two tribes, built strong and large cities, Bethlehem, and Etare, and Tekoa, and Bethzur, and Shoco, and Adullam, and Ipan, and Maresha, and Ziph, and Adorlam, and Lachlsh, and Azekah, and Zorah, and Aijalon, and Hebron; these he built first of all in the tribe of Judah.

entries.title: Ziph
entries.summary: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ziph (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Ziph. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ziphah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Jehallelel's son, in Judah's genealogy.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ziphah was a son of Jehallelel listed among the descendants of Judah in the tribal genealogy of 1 Chronicles 4:16.

entries.title: Ziphim
entries.summary: The people of Ziph, who twice gave David's hiding place away to Saul. Psalm 54 is headed with that betrayal.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Ziphites were the inhabitants of Ziph, a town in the wilderness of Judah southeast of Hebron. Twice they betrayed David's hiding place to Saul while he was a fugitive, an episode remembered in the heading of Psalm 54.

witness.excerpt: 1097.] There was a man that was a Ziphite, of the city of Maon; who was rich, and had a vast number of cattle: for he fed a flock of three thousand sheep, and another flock of a thousand goats.

entries.title: Ziphion (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Gad's son, one of the seventy who went down to Egypt with Jacob. Numbers 26:15 calls him Zephon.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A son of Gad listed among the seventy who went down to Egypt with Jacob (Gen. 46:16). The parallel census in Numbers 26:15 gives his name as Zephon, and most translations treat the two forms as the same person.

witness.excerpt: And these are the names of their sons who went with him into Egypt: the sons of Gad: Ziphion, and Haggi, and Shuni, and Ezbon, (and Eri) and Areli, and Arodi--eight.

entries.title: Ziphron
entries.summary: A point on the northern border of the land Moses described, southeast of Hamath. Nobody has found it.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Ziphron marked a point on the northern boundary of the land Israel was to inherit, as described in Moses' instructions before entering Canaan, situated southeast of Hamath (Numbers 34:9). Its exact site is unidentified, though the boundary description places it in the general region of the Beqaa Valley or southern Syria.

entries.title: Zippor (Moabite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Balak's father. Balak was the Moabite king who hired Balaam to curse Israel.
entries.label: 3 books
entries.dictNote: Zippor was the father of Balak, the Moabite king who hired Balaam to curse the invading Israelites.

entries.title: Zipporah (Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Moses's wife, Jethro's daughter. On the road back to Egypt the Lord sought to kill Moses, and Zipporah circumcised their son and touched Moses with the foreskin, and he lived. Scripture does not explain it.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zipporah was Moses's wife, a daughter of the Midianite priest Jethro, and in a strange episode on the way back to Egypt she circumcised their son herself and touched Moses with the foreskin to avert what Scripture describes only as the Lord seeking to kill him, an act that saved his life.

witness.excerpt: And Moses took Zipporah his wife, and his children, and pleased himself with his coming.
And he took with him Zipporah, the daughter of Raguel, whom he had married, and the children he had by her, Gersom and Eleazer, and made haste into Egypt.

entries.title: Zithri (Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Uzziel's son, a Kohathite Levite, brother to Mishael and Elzaphan.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Levite of the Kohathite line, son of Uzziel and brother of Mishael and Elzaphan (Exodus 6:22).

entries.title: Ziz
entries.summary: The Moabites and Ammonites came up against Jehoshaphat by the ascent of Ziz, a pass near En-gedi on the Dead Sea. It is generally identified with a steep track climbing toward Tekoa.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: The ascent of Ziz was a pass near En-gedi on the western shore of the Dead Sea, the route by which a coalition of Moabites and Ammonites advanced against King Jehoshaphat of Judah (2 Chron. 20:16). It is generally identified with a steep track climbing from the Dead Sea shore toward Tekoa, matching the rugged terrain of the En-gedi cliffs.

entries.title: Ziza (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A Simeonite chief whose clan, in Hezekiah's reign, drove out the people of Gedor and took their land.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Ziza (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: A son of Rehoboam. The other Ziza is a Simeonite prince who took land at Gedor.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Two men named Ziza appear in Chronicles. The first was a Simeonite prince whose clan drove out the peaceful people of Gedor and settled their land during Hezekiah's reign (1 Chronicles 4:37-43). The second was a son born to King Rehoboam of Judah by his favored wife Maachah (2 Chronicles 11:20-21).

entries.title: Zizah (Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: The same Gershonite Levite as Zina a verse earlier, by the look of it, Shimei's son in David's list of family heads.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A Gershonite Levite, son of Shimei, listed among the heads of Levitical families organized by David for temple service (1 Chr. 23:11). He is likely the same man called Zina one verse earlier in the same list (1 Chr. 23:10), Zizah apparently being a variant spelling of his name.

entries.title: Zoan
entries.summary: Tanis, to the Greeks, a city in the Nile delta that was once Egypt's capital. Numbers says it was built seven years after Hebron. The psalmist puts the plagues in the field of Zoan.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Zoan, known to the Greeks as Tanis, was an ancient city in the Nile delta that served for a time as Egypt's capital and is described in Numbers as having been built seven years after Hebron. The psalmist recalls the plagues of the exodus as wonders worked "in the field of Zoan," and Isaiah and Ezekiel both single it out in oracles against Egypt's rulers and counselors. Excavations at Tanis by Pierre Montet in 1939 uncovered the intact royal tombs of several pharaohs, including Psusennes I, a discovery rivaling Tutankhamun's tomb that was overshadowed at the time by the outbreak of the Second World War.

entries.title: Zoar
entries.summary: Lot asked that this little town be spared so he could run to it, and it was, while Sodom and Gomorrah burned. It was first called Bela, and it lay where Moab met the Dead Sea plain.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Zoar was a small town near the Dead Sea, originally called Bela, to which Lot and his daughters fled for refuge when Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed; Lot had asked that the town be spared because of its small size, and it was. Isaiah and Jeremiah both mention Zoar in oracles concerning Moab, since it lay near the border between Moab and the Dead Sea plain.

witness.excerpt: It is to this day called Zoar ; for that is the word which the Hebrews use for a small thing .
The length of this lake is five hundred and eighty furlongs; where it is extended as far as Zoar in Arabia, and its breadth is an hundred and fifty.

entries.title: Zoba
entries.summary: An Aramean kingdom north of Damascus. Saul fought it, David beat its king Hadadezer and took his chariots and his bronze, and a man from Zobah named Rezon troubled Solomon from Damascus.
entries.label: 4 books
entries.dictNote: Zobah was an Aramean kingdom north of Damascus that repeatedly clashed with Israel. Saul fought against it, and David decisively defeated its king Hadadezer, capturing chariots, horsemen, and a large amount of bronze that later went into temple furnishings. Solomon later contended with a rebel from Zobah named Rezon, who established himself as a persistent adversary in Damascus.

witness.excerpt: And he also fought against the neighbouring nations, and subdued the Ammonites, and Moabites, and Philistines, and Edomites, and Amalekites; as also the King of Zobah.

He also took away the bucklers of gold, and the shields, which Solomon the king had made; nay, he did not leave the golden quivers which David had taken from the king of Zobah, and had dedicated to God; and when he had thus done, he returned to his own kingdom.

entries.title: Zobebah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Coz's son, in Judah, beside his brother Anub. The verse is one of the loose genealogical scraps in that chapter.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zobebah was a son of Coz, of the tribe of Judah, listed in the brief genealogical notice of 1 Chronicles 4:8 alongside his brother Anub and the families of Aharhel. The verse is part of a cluster of otherwise unattached Judahite genealogical fragments in that chapter. Nothing further is known of him.

entries.title: Zohar (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: Two men. One was Ephron's father, the Hittite who sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah. The other is a son of Simeon in the family lists.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Zohar was the father of Ephron, the Hittite from whom Abraham purchased the cave of Machpelah as a family burial site.

witness.excerpt:
Simeon and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad,

and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul, the son of the Zephathite  woman--seven.

entries.title: Zoheleth (En-rogel)
entries.summary: The serpent stone, by the spring of En-rogel outside Jerusalem. Adonijah held a sacrificial feast there to have himself proclaimed king while David was dying, and left Solomon and Nathan off the guest list.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zoheleth, meaning "the serpent stone," was a rock near the spring of En-rogel outside Jerusalem where Adonijah, David's son, held a sacrificial feast to have himself proclaimed king while David lay dying, deliberately leaving out Solomon, Nathan, and Solomon's other supporters (1 Kings 1:9-10). The plot collapsed once Nathan and Bathsheba persuaded David to have Solomon publicly anointed instead.

entries.title: Zoheth (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Ishi's son, in Judah's genealogy, and that is the whole record.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: A son of Ishi listed among the descendants of Judah in 1 Chronicles 4:20. Nothing else is recorded about him.

entries.title: Zophah (Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy)
entries.summary: Helem's son, a chief of Asher, at the head of a family known for its warriors.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zophah was a son of Helem and a chief of the tribe of Asher, listed at the head of a family record noted for its many able warriors (1 Chronicles 7:35, 40).

entries.title: Zophai (Levite living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: He was a Kohathite Levite and Samuel's ancestor, also spelled Zuph. The hill country where Elkanah's family lived was called the land of Zuph after him.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Zophai, also spelled Zuph, was a Kohathite Levite and an ancestor of the prophet Samuel through Elkanah's line (1 Chronicles 6:26, 35). The hill country where Elkanah's family lived is called the land of Zuph at 1 Samuel 9:5, apparently after him.

entries.title: Zophai (Zuph)
entries.summary: Named once, in 1 Samuel, and nowhere else.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Zophar (Man living at the time of the Patriarchs)
entries.summary: The Naamathite, the third of Job's friends and the bluntest. He insisted Job's suffering proved hidden sin. God rebuked him for it.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zophar was the third and harshest of Job's three friends, a Naamathite whose brief, blunt speeches insist even more forcefully than his companions that Job's suffering proves hidden sin, a position God later rebukes.

entries.title: Zorites (People, perhaps from Shobal)
entries.summary: The people of Zorah, Samson's town on the border of Judah and Dan. Chronicles counts them as a clan among Caleb's descendants.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zorites were the inhabitants of Zorah, a town on the border of Judah and Dan and the birthplace of Samson. In Chronicles they appear as a Judahite clan within the larger genealogical record of Caleb's descendants.

entries.title: Zuar (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Father of Issachar's tribal leader during the wilderness census.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zuar was the father of the tribal leader of Issachar during the wilderness census.

entries.title: Zur (King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: A Midianite chief killed in Israel's war against Midian. Phinehas had already killed his daughter Cozbi over the idolatry that brought the plague.
entries.label: 2 books
entries.dictNote: Zur was a Midianite chief killed in Israel's war against Midian, and his daughter Cozbi was killed by Phinehas for her role in the idolatry and sexual immorality that had provoked a plague on Israel.

entries.title: Zur (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: One of 3 men called Zur. This one is a man from the wilderness years, named once in Numbers.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Zur (Man living at the time of United Monarchy)
entries.summary: 1 Chronicles names him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.
entries.label: 1 book

entries.title: Zuriel (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: Chief of the Merarite Levites in the wilderness. His clan camped on the north side of the tabernacle and carried its frames, bars, pillars and sockets.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zuriel was the chief of the Merarite Levite clan at the time of the exodus, appointed to oversee that family's portion of the tabernacle service (Numbers 3:35). The Merarites camped on the north side of the tabernacle and were responsible for its frames, bars, pillars, and sockets.

entries.title: Zurishaddai (Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness)
entries.summary: His son led Simeon during the wilderness census.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: Zurishaddai was the father of the tribal leader of Simeon during the wilderness census.

entries.title: Zuzims (People, perhaps from Zuz)
entries.summary: A people east of the Jordan whom Chedorlaomer's coalition beat on the campaign that ended with Lot carried off from Sodom. Some think they are the Zamzummim.
entries.label: 1 book
entries.dictNote: The Zuzim were a people living east of the Jordan whom the invading coalition led by Chedorlaomer defeated in the campaign that eventually swept up Lot at Sodom (Genesis 14:5). Some identify them with the Zamzummim, a similarly obscure people the Ammonites are said to have displaced from the same region (Deuteronomy 2:20).
